Experiment: Step1: Define composition matrix and sample codes. Prepare a two-factor design varying BaO2 at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 wt% (relative to SEG-211 powder) and Ag2O at 0 or 10 wt%, with Pt fixed at 0.5 wt%. Include a boundary case at 5 wt% BaO2 with 10 wt% Ag2O for defect mapping only. Prepare at least n=3 replicates per composition for statistical confidence.

Step2: Set target geometry and batch plan. Aim for single-domain cylindrical bulks of 12–14 mm diameter and 4–6 mm final thickness. Plan batch runs of up to 6 samples per furnace cycle using identical stack geometry to enable cost-effective throughput.

Step3: Reagents and storage. Use high-purity oxides/carbonates: Sm2O3, Eu2O3, Gd2O3, BaCO3, CuO, Y2O3 (if synthesizing Y-123), Ag2O (≥99.9%), Pt powder (≤1 μm, ≥99.9%), BaO2 (≥95%). Store BaO2 and Ag2O in a desiccator; minimize moisture exposure. Use MgO or YSZ setter plates and high-purity alumina fixtures.

Step4: Synthesize SEG-211 precursor powder. Weigh Sm2O3:Eu2O3:Gd2O3 in equimolar proportion (or chosen SEG ratio) to form (Sm,Eu,Gd)2BaCuO5 with BaCO3 and CuO stoichiometry for RE2BaCuO5. Ball mill in isopropanol 12 h with zirconia media. Dry, sieve 200 mesh. Calcine in air: 900°C 12 h, cool, grind; then 950°C 12 h with intermediate regrind. Confirm phase by XRD; minor CuO is acceptable.

Step5: Prepare Y-123 powder for liquid source (if not purchased). Mix Y2O3:BaCO3:CuO in 1:2:3 molar ratio. Calcine in air at 930–940°C for 12–24 h with one regrind. Confirm YBa2Cu3O7−δ by XRD.

Step6: Prepare Ba3Cu5O8 liquid source powder. Mix BaCO3:CuO in 3:5 molar ratio. Calcine at 850–880°C for 10–12 h, regrind, then 900°C for 8–10 h. Confirm Ba3Cu5O8/BaCuO2–CuO mixture by XRD.

Step7: Formulate liquid-source (LS) pellets. Blend Ba3Cu5O8 with Y-123 at 90:10 wt% (targeting Ba–Cu–O rich liquid with a minor Y-123 oxygen buffer). Add 1–2 wt% PVA binder in ethanol. Press 12–14 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick pellets at ~150 MPa. Dry at 80°C. Optional: presinter at 880–900°C for 2 h to strengthen.

Step8: Formulate SEG-211 green bodies with dopants. For each composition, blend SEG-211 with 0.5 wt% Pt powder, BaO2 per design (0–5 wt%), and Ag2O per design (0 or 10 wt%). Keep Ag2O addition restricted to the 211 compact to localize Ag formation in the 123 matrix. Wet-mix in ethanol 4 h, dry under vacuum at ≤60°C. Add 1–2 wt% PVA binder. Press 12–14 mm diameter, 4–6 mm thick pellets at 120–180 MPa.

Step9: Presinter SEG-211 green bodies to set open porosity. Heat in air: ramp 2°C/min to 500°C (binder burnout, 1 h), then to 900–920°C for 2 h, cool to room temperature. Target bulk density ~55–65% to promote capillary infiltration.

Step10: Seed preparation and alignment. Use a c-axis oriented NdBa2Cu3O7 (Nd-123) seed plate (~2×2×0.5 mm^3). Verify orientation by Laue or XRD. Optionally apply a thin (~50–100 μm) buffer layer of undoped SEG-211 or Y-211 powder on the 211 pellet top to protect the seed and promote epitaxy.

Step11: Stack assembly for top-seeded infiltration growth (TSIG). On a MgO or YSZ setter, place an LS pellet. Place the doped SEG-211 pellet directly on top of the LS pellet to allow upward infiltration. Place the Nd-123 seed on the center of the 211 pellet. Use an alumina confinement ring (slightly larger than pellet diameter) to contain melt spread. Ensure vertical alignment and intimate contact between pellets.

Step12: Furnace atmosphere. Conduct growth in flowing air (pO2≈0.21 atm). Maintain a clean hot zone to avoid contamination. Position a thermocouple near the stack to calibrate actual temperature.

Step13: Thermal profile for TSIG. Execute the following cycle in air:
- Ramp 3°C/min to 600°C, hold 1 h (binder burnout completion).
- Ramp 3°C/min to 1035–1040°C, hold 1–2 h to fully melt Ba–Cu–O liquid in LS (avoid seed dissolution by keeping seed cooler using top-cooling if available).
- Reduce to growth window 1015–1020°C and begin slow cooling at 0.2°C/h down to 985–990°C to traverse the peritectic growth range for SEG-123 while maintaining seed stability.
- Hold 985–990°C for 5 h to complete 211 depletion and 123 thickening.
- Cool 60°C/h to 450°C.
Note: For BaO2≥3 wt% or Ag2O present, reduce the peak hold by ~15–30 min to limit excessive liquid and suppress macro liquid pooling. Keep the slow-cooling rate at 0.2°C/h as specified to ensure single-domain growth.

Step14: Post-growth handling. After cooling to 450°C, remove samples from the furnace in air. Inspect for seed imprint, radial growth striations, and absence of multiple nucleation centers. Discard samples with evident spontaneous nucleation away from the seed.

Step15: Oxygenation anneal. Place samples in flowing high-purity O2 (≥99.995%). Use a stepped schedule to optimize oxygen ordering while limiting RE/Ba cation mobility:
- Ramp 1°C/min to 450°C, hold 150 h.
- Cool at 0.5°C/min to 400°C, hold 100 h.
- Cool at 0.5°C/min to 350°C, hold 100 h.
- Slow cool 0.5°C/min to room temperature.
Optionally perform an intermediate 300°C hold (50 h) for further ordering if ΔTc remains >1.5 K.

Step16: Machining and surface preparation. Lap the top surface to remove seed residue and expose the grown 123 surface. Prepare polished cross sections for microstructural analysis using SiC papers and diamond suspensions down to 0.25 μm.

Step17: Phase and texture verification by XRD. Use Cu-Kα radiation. Perform:
- θ–2θ scan (10–80°) on the top surface to confirm c-axis texture (dominant 00l reflections).
- Powder XRD on crushed fragments to confirm phase purity (SEG-123 dominant, with controlled 211 residuals and minimal Ba–Cu–O secondary phases).
- Determine c-axis parameter (target ~11.74 Å) and orthorhombicity from (00l) and (hkl) peak splitting on powder mounts.

Step18: Microstructure by FE-SEM/EDS. Acquire BSE and SE images on polished cross sections. Quantify 211 particle size distribution via image analysis (≥500 particles per sample); target mean ~3 μm with narrow distribution. Map RE/Ba/Cu/Ag/Pt distributions by EDS; identify Ag dispersoids and check for Ba-rich secondary phases. Note and catalog any liquid-inclusion defects (smooth-edged pools), especially for BaO2≥4 wt%.

Step19: Density and porosity. Measure bulk density by Archimedes. Correlate porosity with infiltration completeness. Accept samples with density ≥92% of theoretical for property measurements.

Step20: Magnetic transition measurements (Tc and ΔTc). Use SQUID magnetometry:
- Measure ZFC/FC M(T) at 1 mT from 100 K to 60 K with H∥c (field perpendicular to pellet surface).
- Define Tc(onset) at 1% of full diamagnetic signal; determine ΔTc between 10% and 90% criteria.
- Accept compositions that yield Tc≥93 K and ΔTc≤1.5 K for performance benchmarking.

Step21: Critical current density Jc from M–H loops. At 77 K and 65 K, record M(H) loops up to 5 T with H∥c. Calculate Jc using the extended Bean model for rectangular/cylindrical specimens:
- For a rectangular bar with dimensions a<b (cm): Jc(A/cm^2)=20ΔM/(a(1−a/3b)), where ΔM is the half-width of the M–H loop in emu/cm^3.
- Correct for demagnetization as needed based on geometry.
Report Jc(77 K, self-field) and Jc(65 K, 3 T) for each composition.

Step22: Irreversibility field and pinning analysis. Determine Hirr by Kramer extrapolation or criterion where Jc falls below 10^2 A/cm^2. Compute pinning force Fp=μ0 Jc H and normalized f_p=Fp/Fp,max versus reduced field h=H/Hirr. Extract hmax for each composition to classify dominant pinning (δl vs δTc) and quantify shifts with BaO2/Ag2O additions.

Step23: Optimization decision rules. Identify the BaO2 level that maximizes high-field Jc at 65 K and 77 K while maintaining Tc≥93 K and ΔTc≤1.5 K. Flag BaO2≥4 wt% samples showing macro liquid inclusions or broadened ΔTc; if present, refine by reducing LS/211 mass ratio or peak hold time and retest.

Step24: Trapped field evaluation for application relevance. Field-cool samples in an external electromagnet: apply 2–3 T at 300 K, cool to 77 K (LN2) or 65 K (cold N2 gas), switch off field, map trapped field over the surface with a 0.5 mm step Hall probe at 0.5 mm lift-off. Compute peak trapped field and field uniformity. Inspect for flux jumps or cracking during pulsed-field magnetization (optional).

Step25: Mechanical assessment. Measure Vickers hardness on polished surfaces at 0.5–1 N loads to ensure adequate mechanical robustness for trapped-field duty. Inspect for microcracks by optical microscopy.

Step26: Repeatability and scale-up. Repeat the optimal composition run in a multi-pellet batch (≥6 bulks) using identical TSIG conditions to assess yield. Monitor seed survival and domain uniformity across the furnace footprint; adjust thermal gradients or stack shielding if peripheral samples show secondary nucleation.

Step27: Quality controls. Before each run, verify seed quality and orientation. Verify LS pellet thickness and mass to maintain a consistent LS:211 mass ratio of ~0.8–1.2. Track green density and porosity for each 211 compact. Implement process logs for temperature profile and actual thermocouple readings.

Step28: Safety and handling. Handle BaO2 and Ag2O with gloves and eye protection; avoid moisture and organics near BaO2. Provide adequate ventilation during high-temperature steps to vent O2 from BaO2/Ag2O decomposition. Ensure furnace interlocks when using oxygen during annealing.

Step29: Data analysis and reporting. Compile Tc, ΔTc, Jc(H,T), hmax, 211 size statistics, phase purity, and defect incidence for all compositions. Correlate BaO2 addition with Tc sharpening and hmax shifts; correlate Ag2O co-doping with high-field Jc enhancement and 211 refinement. Select the composition that delivers approximately doubled high-field Jc without Tc penalty for application tests.

Step30: Go/no-go criteria for application readiness. Proceed to device-level tests if the selected composition meets all of: Tc(onset)≥93 K, ΔTc≤1.5 K, Jc(77 K, 0 T)≥30 kA/cm^2, Jc(65 K, 3 T)≥50 kA/cm^2, single-domain XRD texture (00l only), mean 211 size ~3 μm with narrow distribution, and absence of macro liquid inclusions. Otherwise, iterate BaO2 within 2–4 wt% and adjust LS peak/hold conditions to eliminate defects.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – Precursor powder synthesis  
- Sm-211, Eu-211 and Gd-211 powders: stoichiometric mixtures of Sm₂O₃/Eu₂O₃/Gd₂O₃ (Kojundo) + BaO₂ + CuO were calcined 12 h each at 860 °C, 900 °C, 950 °C with intermediate grindings.  
- SEG-211 precursor: equal-weight mixture of the three 211 powders + 0.5 wt % Pt.  
- Liquid-source powder: 1:1 weight mixture of Y-123 (Y₂O₃ + BaO₂ + CuO calcined 860–920 °C) and Ba₃Cu₅O₈ (BaO₂ + CuO calcined 860 & 880 °C).  

Step 2 – BaO₂ doping series  
- Batches of SEG-211 were admixed with 0–5 wt % BaO₂ (samples Ba-0 to Ba-5).  

Step 3 – Pellet assembly (TSIG stack)  
- 20-mm-diameter pellets: SEG-211 (top) / liquid-source (bottom) at weight ratio 1.3 : 1.  
- A c-axis-oriented NdBa₂Cu₃Oᵧ seed crystal was placed on top of the SEG-211 pellet.  
- Whole stack was supported underneath by Y₂O₃ powder layer + MgO crystal to limit liquid loss.  

Step 4 – Single-domain growth heat treatment (air atmosphere)  
- Heat to 1080 °C at 100 °C h⁻¹, hold 1 h.  
- Slow cool 1060 → 1020 °C over ≈150 h, then furnace cool to room temperature.  

Step 5 – Oxygenation  
- Anneal 450 → 350 °C for 250 h in flowing O₂ (250 ml min⁻¹).  

Step 6 – Ag₂O-added sample (SEG-Ag)  
- Identical precursor preparation but with 4 wt % BaO₂ + 10 wt % Ag₂O in SEG-211.  
- Because Ag₂O lowers peritectic T by ~25 °C, both maximum and slow-cooling temperatures were reduced by 25 °C; other parameters (ramp rate, dwell, oxygenation) unchanged.  

Step 7 – Structural verification  
- X-ray diffraction on 2 × 2 mm ab-plane cleavage pieces (Cu-Kα); (00l) peaks used to confirm single-domain character and to extract c-lattice parameter.  

Step 8 – Superconducting property measurements  
- Tc and ΔTc: zero-field-cooled (ZFC) DC magnetic susceptibility at 1 mT (H // c) using SQUID; pieces cut ~2 mm below seed.  
- Jc(H,T): magnetisation hysteresis (M–H) loops up to 5 T at 80, 77, 75, 65 K (H // c) on ~1.5 × 1.5 × 0.5 mm³ specimens; Jc extracted via extended Bean model (Eq. 1).  

Step 9 – Microstructural analysis  
- Field-emission SEM (JEOL-7100F, 1500×) on ab-plane ~2 mm below surface; 211 particle size distribution evaluated with ImageJ.  

Step 10 – Flux-pinning analysis  
- Volume pinning force Fp = B·Jc(77 K); irreversibility field Hirr taken at Jc = 100 A cm⁻²; normalised curves Fp/Fp,max vs h = H/Hirr fitted to Fp/Fp,max = A h^p (1–h)^q to extract hmax = p/(p+q) and identify pinning regime.  

[Experimental Design Details]
- All processing performed in ambient air (no controlled pO₂).  
- Liquid-source / 211 weight ratio fixed at 1.3 for every sample.  
- Pt (0.5 wt %) added to refine 211 particles; no other dopants except specified BaO₂ and Ag₂O.  
- Temperature profile, pellet size, oxygen-flow rate, and measurement positions explicitly stated; other environmental details (humidity, furnace type, heating element, crucible material) not specified in the paper.

Experiment: Step1: Define the design-of-experiments matrix: prepare MOD-derived YBCO coated conductors with BaHfO3 (BHO) nanocrystals at 5, 10, and 15 mol% relative to Y; target two mean BHO sizes (5.5 nm and 6.5 nm) via controlled two-step growth schedules; include controls: pristine YBCO (0% BHO) and 15 mol% BHO grown by a conventional single-step schedule; plan N=3 independent tapes per condition for statistics.
Step2: Choose substrate and buffer architecture: use Hastelloy C-276 tapes with an oxide buffer stack (Al2O3/Y2O3/IBAD-MgO/LaMnO3 or equivalent LMO/MgO/Y2O3/Al2O3) exhibiting Δφ ≤ 5° and Δω ≤ 3°; verify texture by XRD φ-scan and rocking curve on incoming tapes; clean via acetone/isopropanol and dry N2.
Step3: Prepare low-fluorine MOD stock solutions: dissolve Y, Ba and Cu 2-ethylhexanoates or propionates in 2-methoxyethanol with minimal trifluoroacetate content; use total cation concentration 0.6–0.8 M; chelate with monoethanolamine or triethanolamine (≤5 mol% of total cations) to stabilize; filter at 0.2 µm; measure viscosity (20–30 mPa·s) and adjust with solvent.
Step4: Prepare BHO precursor component: dissolve Hf(IV) 2,4-pentanedionate (or Hf 2-ethylhexanoate) and Ba 2-ethylhexanoate in 2-methoxyethanol with acac as needed to enhance solubility; maintain Ba:Hf = 1:1; filter 0.2 µm; verify Hf concentration via ICP-OES.
Step5: Mix YBCO and BHO precursor solutions: for each target BHO content x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15 (mol per mol Y), add extra Ba and Hf to achieve BHO molar fraction x without disturbing Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3 for the superconducting matrix; for 15 mol% BHO, target cation ratios: Y:Ba:Cu:Hf ≈ 1:(2 + 0.15):3:0.15; confirm final stoichiometry by ICP-OES.
Step6: Establish coating parameters on reel-to-reel line: slot-die or micro-gravure coat at line speed 1–3 m/min; set wet film thickness to yield ~0.5 µm per pass; use three passes to reach ~1.5 µm total thickness; dry at 120 °C between passes; maintain clean, dry atmosphere (<30% RH) during coating.
Step7: Low-F pyrolysis after each pass: ramp at 10 °C/min to 375–425 °C in flowing O2 (0.2–1 atm) with 5–10 vol% H2O; dwell 30–60 min to remove organics and residual fluorine; monitor off-gas for CO2/HF; avoid rapid heating that can cause BaCO3 formation; cool to room temperature in dry N2.
Step8: Define two-step crystallization schedules to tune BHO size while suppressing coarsening: use flowing N2 with 200–400 ppm O2 and 3–5 vol% H2O; fast ramp to pre-growth temperature followed by a short high-temperature finish and rapid cool.
Step9: Two-step schedule for 5.5 nm BHO target: ramp 15 °C/min to 785 °C; dwell 10–12 min (promote simultaneous YBCO nucleation and BHO nucleation at high supersaturation); ramp 2 °C/min to 788–790 °C; dwell 6–8 min; cool at ≥20 °C/min to 500 °C under the same pO2; then cool to room temperature in dry N2; note: this schedule minimizes growth time to limit BHO radii.
Step10: Two-step schedule for 6.5 nm BHO target: ramp 15 °C/min to 785 °C; dwell 20–25 min (allowing BHO particles to reach a slightly larger, more stable size); ramp 2 °C/min to 792–795 °C; dwell 8–10 min; cool at ≥20 °C/min to 500 °C; then to room temperature in dry N2; note: the brief high-T finish coalesces YBCO grains while limiting Ostwald ripening by short exposure.
Step11: Single-step growth control (coarsening baseline): ramp 15 °C/min to 790–795 °C in the same atmosphere; dwell 30–40 min; cool at ≥20 °C/min to 500 °C and then to room temperature; apply to 15 mol% BHO samples.
Step12: Oxygenation anneal: load tapes in flowing O2 (1 atm); ramp at 5 °C/min to 450 °C; dwell 8–12 h; cool at 1–2 °C/min to room temperature; confirm δ is near optimum by measuring Tc onset (expect ~90 K with slight depression at high BHO loadings).
Step13: Sectioning and dimensional metrology: dice 4 mm × 4 mm squares from each tape; measure total film thickness by cross-sectional SEM or FIB-SEM; record dimensions for Bean-model Jc; prepare multiple pieces per condition for magnetometry and transport.
Step14: Phase and texture verification by XRD: θ–2θ scans to confirm c-axis oriented YBCO (00l) and absence of parasitic phases (e.g., BaCuO2, CuO); search for broad BHO reflections; φ-scans on YBCO {103} and ω-rocking curves on (005) to confirm maintained biaxial texture; target Δφ ≤ 5°, Δω ≤ 3° at all BHO levels.
Step15: Microstructure mapping by TEM/STEM: prepare cross-sectional lamellae by FIB (protective Pt cap); perform HRTEM and STEM-HAADF to visualize BHO nanocrystals in the YBCO matrix; index BHO by FFT to confirm cubic perovskite; acquire EDS maps for Ba/Hf localization; for each sample measure ≥200 particles to build size histograms; extract mean diameter, standard deviation, and number density; verify isotropic 3D distribution and absence of oriented nanorods.
Step16: Strain characterization: use geometric phase analysis on HRTEM images to map local strain fields around BHO particles; complement with XRD Williamson–Hall analysis to estimate microstrain; correlate strain amplitude and spatial extent with BHO size and content.
Step17: Surface morphology and continuity: AFM over 5 µm × 5 µm areas to assess RMS roughness; SEM plan-view to check for pores/cracks; ensure continuous films at 1.5 µm thickness for all loadings; reject samples with visible cracking.
Step18: Magnetization-based Jc measurement: use a PPMS or VSM to acquire M–H loops; measure at T = 4.2, 20, 30, and 77 K; sweep field from 0 to 7 T (extend to 12–14 T if available) with field both parallel and perpendicular to c-axis; mount samples to minimize substrate contribution; measure and subtract background from an uncoated buffered substrate piece; compute Jc from the extended Bean model using sample dimensions a = b = 4 mm and film thickness; report Jc(B,T) and calculate Fp = Jc × B.
Step19: Transport Jc cross-check: pattern 1–2 mm wide bridges or use intact squares with soldered current/voltage leads; measure four-probe Jc at 77 K self-field and at 20–30 K in 0–7 T with E-field criterion 1 µV/cm; compare to magnetization-derived Jc; ensure agreement within 15–20%.
Step20: Angular Jc(θ) assessment: at 30 K and 3 T, rotate the sample from H∥c to H∥ab; measure Jc(θ) every 5–10°; verify that BHO-doped samples display weak anisotropy (consistent with 3D isotropic pins) compared to pristine YBCO; quantify anisotropy ratio γJc = max(Jc)/min(Jc).
Step21: Evaluate coarsening sensitivity: subject a subset of 5.5 nm and 6.5 nm BHO samples to a post-growth thermal soak at 790 °C for 20 min in the same low-pO2 atmosphere; re-image by TEM to quantify particle growth and redistribution; reassess Jc at 30 K; determine stability margin of each size.
Step22: Mechanical integrity and residual stress: perform tape bend tests (e.g., 5 mm radius, 100 cycles) and re-measure Jc at 77 K to detect degradation; examine cross-sections by SEM for microcracks; use Raman micro-spectroscopy (G-line shifts of YBCO) where accessible to compare residual stress among conditions.
Step23: Data analysis and optimization: plot Jc(B,T) and Fp(B) for all conditions; determine Fp,max and the corresponding field; compare two-step vs single-step at each BHO content; identify the combination of 6.5 nm vs 5.5 nm and 10–15 mol% that maximizes Jc at 20–30 K in 3–7 T while maintaining self-field Jc > 2 MA/cm² at 77 K and strong texture; use ANOVA to assess the significance of particle size, content, and growth schedule.
Step24: Scale-up trial on 1 m tape: run the best-performing recipe on the reel-to-reel line; monitor furnace temperatures and pO2 uniformity; map Jc at 77 K self-field every 10 cm by transport or scanning Hall probe; cut three 4 × 4 mm pieces along the length for PPMS 30 K, 3 T tests; assess uniformity and yield.
Step25: Risk mitigation and controls: if texture degradation is observed at 15 mol% BHO, reduce per-pass thickness and increase number of passes to improve outgassing; if BaCO3 forms during pyrolysis, increase humidity or adjust ramp rate; if BHO agglomerates, increase chelator content slightly and shorten high-T dwell; maintain clean precursor filtration and substrate handling to avoid heterogeneous nucleation.
Step26: Documentation: record all processing parameters (solution age, viscosity, coating speeds, furnace profiles, gas flows, pO2, humidity), characterization results (XRD, TEM size distributions, strain maps), and electrical data (Jc, Fp, anisotropy); compile a processing–microstructure–property map to guide further iterations focused on maximizing Jc at 30 K, 3–7 T while preserving high 77 K performance.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – BHO nanocrystal synthesis  
- BHO nanocrystals are produced by a solvothermal route.  
- Size control (5.5 nm or 6.5 nm average) is achieved by adjusting reaction time and surfactant ratios (details of exact times/ratios not given).

Step 2 – precursor solution preparation  
- A 2.5 M (total cation) low-fluorine MOD (LF-MOD) YBCO precursor solution is prepared.  
- Monodisperse BHO nanocrystals are dispersed into the solution at 5, 8, 10 or 15 mol % relative to Y content; a 0 mol % reference is also prepared.

Step 3 – continuous reel-to-reel coating  
- The precursor is coated onto LaMnO₃/MgO/Y₂O₃/Al₂O₃/Hastelloy substrates using industrial reel-to-reel equipment (Shanghai Creative Superconductor Technologies Co. Ltd).  
- Coating sequence:  
  – First deposition gives a 200–300 nm YBCO seed layer.  
  – A pyrolysis step is applied (specific temperature/time not quoted).  
  – Second deposition brings the final YBCO thickness to ≈ 1.5 µm.

Step 4 – two-step growth/oxygenation (reconstructed from multiple sections)  
- Pyrolysed tapes are heat-treated in two stages:  
  1. 785 °C for 20 min in N₂/O₂/H₂O mixed atmosphere at < 100 Pa, then cooled.  
  2. Re-heated to 785–795 °C for ~1 h to complete epitaxial growth.  
- Final oxygen anneal: 450 °C for 60 min in O₂ to obtain the superconducting YBCO phase.

Step 5 – microstructural characterisation  
- BHO size and dispersion in colloidal state: JEOL JEM-2010F field-emission HRTEM.  
- Cross-sectional TEM of finished films: prepared by FEI Helios Nanolab 600i FIB; imaged with the same JEOL microscope; Hf distribution checked by EDS mapping.

Step 6 – magnetisation and Jc measurement  
- Hysteretic magnetisation loops recorded with a Quantum Design Physical Properties Measurement System at 4.2 K, 20 K, 30 K and 77 K in magnetic fields up to at least 3 T (exact maximum field not stated).  
- Jc extracted from the loops via the extended Bean model using sample dimensions a = 4 mm, b = 4 mm.  
- Flux-pinning force density Fp = Jc × B calculated from the same data.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Substrate architecture: LaMnO₃/MgO/Y₂O₃/Al₂O₃/Hastelloy.  
- Final YBCO thickness: ≈ 1.5 µm (two deposition passes).  
- BHO concentrations tested: 0, 5, 8, 10, 15 mol %.  
- BHO primary sizes tested: 6.5 nm ± 2.5 nm and 5.5 nm ± 2.5 nm.  
- Growth atmosphere for first step: N₂/O₂/H₂O, < 100 Pa; second step and oxygenation atmosphere not detailed beyond temperature and duration.  
- Jc calculation assumes full penetration and uniform current density (Bean model); no correction factors mentioned.

XPS (Mn 2p, Mn 3s multiplet splitting) on witness samples to gauge Mn3+/Mn4+ ratio and surface oxygen; cross-section TEM on a representative coupon to verify coherent interface with Epi-MgO and absence of secondary phases.

AFM RMS target unchanged (≤2 nm) and absence of grain coarsening. Raman: look for blue-shift and narrowing of Mn–O stretching consistent with vacancy reduction; XPS/EELS (on TEM lamellae) to confirm increase in Mn4+ fraction; verify no interdiffusion into Epi-MgO (STEM-EDS/EELS line scans of La/Mn/Mg). Step8: Residual stress and strain assessment in annealed LMO; perform XRD sin²ψ measurements on LMO(002) to estimate in-plane stress changes across anneal series; cross-check with wafer curvature on LMO grown on 25×25 mm MgO crystals to calibrate stress sign/magnitude. Step15: Correlate LMO lattice parameter with YBCO texture and performance; plot aLMO versus YBCO a-axis fraction, ΔφYBCO, ΔωYBCO, misfit dislocation density, and Ic/Jc. [Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Substrate preparation  
- Start with 50 µm-thick, 12 mm-wide Hastelloy C-276 tapes.  
- Electrochemically polish and clean the tapes.

Step 2: Multilayer buffer deposition (roll-to-roll, SCSC)  
- Deposit sequentially by industrial roll-to-roll systems:  
  – Al₂O₃ (60 nm) barrier layer  
  – Y₂O₃ (10 nm) nucleation seed layer  
  – IBAD-MgO (10 nm) biaxial-texture layer  
  – Epi-MgO (60 nm) texture-repair layer  

Step 3: LMO buffer deposition  
- Deposit 50 nm LaMnO₃−δ film by DC reactive magnetron sputtering in roll-to-roll mode.  
  – Target: 99.95 % pure La:Mn (1:1 atomic ratio) alloy.  
  – Gas: Ar/O₂ mixture, total pressure 1 Pa; Ar 135 sccm, O₂ 20–25 sccm.  
  – Power: 1000 W; substrate temperature 750 °C (induction heating).

Step 4: Post-annealing of LMO films  
- Anneal LMO-coated short samples (temperature series: 500 °C – 620 °C in 20 °C steps; time series at 550 °C: 5 min – 2 h).  
- Atmosphere: flowing 99.999 % O₂, slight over-pressure ≈ 1.05 atm.  
- Heating rate: 5 °C min⁻¹; cool naturally to room temperature.

Step 5: LMO characterization  
- XRD θ–2θ scans (Cu Kα, 20–55°) to track (00ℓ) peak shifts and extract lattice constant.  
- ω-scans (rocking curves) on (002) and φ-scans on (011) to obtain out-of-plane (∆ω) and in-plane (∆φ) texture (FWHM).  
- Raman spectroscopy (room temperature) to monitor Mn–O vibration modes (~500 cm⁻¹ B₁g bend, ~620 cm⁻¹ Eg stretch).  
- AFM (tapping mode, 5 × 5 µm²) to measure RMS surface roughness.

Step 6: YBCO deposition  
- Deposit 1.5 µm YBCO film on each LMO template by low-fluorine metal–organic deposition (MOD) in the same roll-to-roll line (SCSC); processing details referenced but not repeated in the paper.

Step 7: YBCO characterization  
- XRD θ–2θ, ω, φ scans to check c-axis orientation and texture.  
- Measure critical current Ic at 77 K, self-field with dynamic contact-free Mcorder system (magnetic induction).  
- For selected samples, measure field-dependent Ic and pinning force density Fp at 30 K, 50 K, 77 K (magnetic field range not specified in the paper).

[Experimental Design Details]
- Lattice mismatch evaluation: pseudocubic LMO lattice constant compared to YBCO a-b plane (≈ 3.85 Å).  
- Optimal annealing identified at 560 °C (2 h) giving LMO a = 3.853 Å and mismatch ≈ 0.06 %.  
- Texture quality: ∆φ (LMO) ≈ 7°, ∆ω (LMO) ≈ 2.5° for all annealed samples; no degradation observed.  
- Surface roughness: RMS ≈ 2.5 nm, independent of annealing temperature.  
- Performance metric: 77 K self-field Ic enhancement ~19 % (short samples) and ~26 % (60 m tape) relative to unannealed LMO.

Experiment: Step1: Define sample matrix and objectives. Prepare three groups (n ≥ 6 per group for statistics): (A) CPP baseline: YBa2Cu3O7−δ + 35 mol % Y2BaCuO5 (Y211) + 1 wt % CeO2; (B) MPP baseline: Y2O3 + Ba–Cu–O precursor that forms Y211/Y123 in situ + 1 wt % CeO2; (C) C-MPP layered: upper CPP over lower MPP, both with 1 wt % CeO2. Include parameter sweeps in C-MPP: layer-thickness ratios (CPP:MPP = 60:40, 50:50, 40:60 by height), Y211 in CPP (25, 35, 40 mol %), CeO2 (0.5, 1.0, 1.5 wt %), and buffer pellet thickness (1, 2, 3 mm). Target final bulk dimensions: diameter 24–30 mm, thickness 9–10 mm after melt-growth. Acceptance targets: single-domain growth, a–b texture from SmBCO seed, porosity ≤ 18 %, no macro-cracks, Tc ≥ 90 K, levitation force density Fv ≥ 1.27e−2 N mm−3 and relaxation R ≤ 13 % at 77 K.
Step2: Source and verify raw materials. Powders: YBa2Cu3O7−δ (Y123, ≥ 99.9 %), Y2BaCuO5 (Y211, ≥ 99.9 %), Y2O3 (Y200, ≥ 99.99 %), BaCO3 and CuO (≥ 99.9 %) to prepare Ba–Cu–O (e.g., BaCuO2 and CuO for Ba2Cu3Ox), CeO2 (nano or submicron, 30–100 nm preferred), Yb2O3 (substrate layer), binders (PVA), solvents (ethanol/IPA), and MgO/Al2O3 plates for substrates. SmBCO seed crystals (or Sm123 oriented seeds) with known orientation. Verify phase purity by quick XRD scans for incoming powders.
Step3: Prepare CPP powder. Dry Y123 and Y211 powders at 200 °C for 2 h to remove moisture. Weigh to 35 mol % Y211 relative to Y123 (and the other target molar levels for the sweep). Add 1 wt % CeO2 relative to total ceramic mass. Wet-mix by planetary ball milling in ethanol with zirconia media (ball:powder ≈ 5:1), 300 rpm, 4 h. Dry at 80–100 °C, deagglomerate through a 200-mesh sieve. Add 2 wt % PVA binder in ethanol/water, granulate, dry, and sieve again.
Step4: Prepare MPP powder (in-situ Y211/Y123 formation). Mix Y2O3 with Ba–Cu–O precursor powder to yield overall Y:Ba:Cu stoichiometry that forms Y211+Y123 upon peritectic melt (e.g., Y2O3 + BaCuO2 + CuO blended to reproduce Ba2Cu3Ox melt). Add 1 wt % CeO2. Ball mill under identical conditions to Step3. Dry, granulate with 2 wt % PVA, and sieve. Verify flowability and particle-size distribution (laser diffraction) aiming for D50 ≈ 10–30 μm agglomerates.
Step5: Fabricate CPP buffer pellets for seed protection. Press small CPP buffer pellets (6 mm diameter, thickness 1–3 mm per design) from the CPP batch with 1 wt % CeO2. These serve as a sacrificial/compatible cap under the SmBCO seed to mitigate seed corrosion by Ba–Cu–O liquid.
Step6: Press green bodies. Uniaxially press pellets: (i) CPP-only pellets for group A; (ii) MPP-only pellets for group B; and (iii) separate CPP and MPP sub-pellets for group C with planned heights to realize target layer ratios. Use 200–300 MPa. Optionally CIP at 150–200 MPa to improve green uniformity. Target green total height that yields 9–10 mm post-processed thickness (account for 30–35 % shrinkage in MPP and ~30 % in C-MPP).
Step7: Prepare Yb2O3 substrate layer. Make a Yb2O3 slurry (Yb2O3 + ethanol + small PVA). Coat MgO or dense Al2O3 plates with a ~50–200 μm Yb2O3 layer by doctor blade or dip-coating. Dry and pre-fire at 900 °C for 1 h in air to adhere the layer. Alternatively, use a thin Yb2O3 disk as a substrate.
Step8: Assemble layered C-MPP stacks. Place MPP pellet on the Yb2O3-coated substrate; place the CPP pellet concentrically on top. Lightly press to ensure contact. Place the CPP buffer pellet centered on the top surface. Place the SmBCO seed crystal on the buffer pellet with the a–b plane parallel to the pellet surface and known in-plane orientation. For controls, place seed directly on CPP (group A) or MPP (group B), and also run a subset with buffer pellet to decouple seed effects.
Step9: Furnace loading and thermal uniformity checks. Arrange all sample groups on the same alumina setter in a single-zone or multi-zone box or tube furnace with tight thermal uniformity (±2 °C over the sample area). Use sacrificial guard rings (dense YSZ/alumina) around the batch to reduce edge cooling. Place two thermocouples at representative positions near samples for in-situ temperature verification.
Step10: Top-seeded melt-growth (TSMG) thermal cycle. In air (pO2 ≈ 0.21 bar): ramp 60–100 °C/h to 500 °C (binder burnout hold 2 h), then 200 °C/h to 1035–1045 °C (above peritectic of Y123), hold 0.5–1 h to fully form Ba–Cu–O liquid. Cool at 1.0 °C/h to 1005–1015 °C to initiate and control growth from the seed. Continue slow cool across the growth window to ~980–990 °C at 0.3–0.5 °C/h. Then cool to 900 °C at 60 °C/h and furnace-cool to room temperature. Keep the door closed to avoid drafts and thermal gradients. Record the thermal profile for all runs.
Step11: De-mount and inspect as-grown bulks. Visually inspect top surfaces for facet lines and parasitic grains. Record growth facet lines count and symmetry. Photograph each sample with scale rulers. Document any bulging or warping.
Step12: Oxygenation anneal to form superconducting orthorhombic Y123. Place bulks in flowing oxygen (≥ 99.99 %) at 450 °C for 220 h (baseline), ramp at 60 °C/h, cool at 30 °C/h. For parameter sweep, also anneal subsets for 150 h and 300 h to assess δ sensitivity. Avoid rapid cooling across 350–200 °C to minimize oxygenation cracking.
Step13: Dimensional metrology and shrinkage. Measure diameter and thickness at four azimuths using a micrometer before and after processing. Compute radial and axial shrinkage. Record flatness/planarity (feeler gauge on a granite plate).
Step14: Phase and texture characterization. Perform powder XRD (θ–2θ) on polished surfaces to confirm Y123/Y211 phases and CeO2 residuals. Check orthorhombicity via (013)/(103) splitting. Perform rocking-curve (ω-scan) and pole figure or EBSD on top surfaces and a–c cross-sections to assess a–b plane alignment; target FWHM ≤ 8–10° for single-domain bulks seeded by SmBCO.
Step15: Microstructure and porosity quantification. Prepare a–c cross-sections by resin impregnation, grinding, and polishing to 0.05 μm. Optical microscopy with stitched images across diameter. Use ImageJ to threshold pores and quantify area porosity (≥ 5 fields across center and periphery). SEM-BSE for Y211 distribution; EDS maps for Y, Ba, Cu, Ce. For selected samples, TEM on FIB lamellae to quantify Y211 nanoparticle sizes (target 20–260 nm) and interparticle spacing.
Step16: Density and open porosity. Use Archimedes in ethanol or water with vacuum impregnation to estimate bulk density and open porosity. Compare to theoretical density of Y123/Y211 mixture to estimate total porosity.
Step17: Crack detection and internal defect mapping. Conduct ultrasonic C-scan at 5–15 MHz to detect internal macro-cracks and delaminations. For representative samples, perform micro-CT (voxel 5–10 μm) to map voids/cracks. Record any cracks ≥ 0.2 mm width or ≥ 0.6 mm length; target zero such macro-cracks in C-MPP.
Step18: Electrical superconducting properties. Measure Tc by AC susceptibility (χ′, χ″) and four-probe resistivity on small bars cut from non-critical regions (avoid seed cap). Target Tc onset ≥ 90 K, ΔTc ≤ 1 K. Optionally, compute self-field Jc at 77 K from magnetization (Bean model) on small pieces to compare pinning trends among groups.
Step19: Levitation force and relaxation testing at 77 K. Use a standardized Halbach NdFeB guideway with peak field ~0.67 T at 5 mm gap. Mount each bulk with its a–b plane parallel to the guideway surface. Perform zero-field-cooled (ZFC) approach: cool the bulk in LN2 away from the guideway, then approach to 1–10 mm gaps to record force–distance curves; perform full approach–retract loops (3 cycles) to assess hysteresis. Record maximum levitation force at a standardized gap sequence. Measure magnetic relaxation: hold at fixed gap (e.g., 5 mm) for 180 s and log force decay; compute R = (F0 − F180s)/F0 × 100 %. Repeat for field-cooled (FC) protocol for comparison.
Step20: Trapped field and flux distribution. After FC at a set gap, lift the magnet/guideway and map surface trapped field using a 2D Hall sensor array at 0.5–1.0 mm above the top surface. Alternatively, use magneto-optical imaging to visualize flux penetration and identify weak-link regions.
Step21: Mechanical integrity and performance under cryogenic load. Perform Vickers microhardness (500–1000 g load) on polished cross-sections (matrix vs. Y211-rich zones). Conduct room-temperature and 77 K three-point bending on bars cut from rims to assess strength; record fracture origin and correlate with pore/crack population. Conduct cyclic levitation loading: 10,000 approach–retract cycles at 77 K at a fixed minimum gap to simulate service loads; monitor force degradation every 500 cycles.
Step22: Finite-element electromagnetic modeling for force normalization. Build 3D H-formulation models in COMSOL Multiphysics using measured sample dimensions and a homogenized critical-state law (E–J power law with n from magnetization relaxation). Simulate the Halbach field profile and bulk response to generate normalization curves for thickness (9–10 mm) and a–b area (441–676 mm²). Validate simulations against measured force loops for a subset of samples; then use the model to normalize all forces to a common reference geometry to compute Fv = Fnorm/V.
Step23: Data analysis and statistics. For each group and parameter set, compute mean ± SD for porosity, crack metrics, Tc, Fv, and R. Use ANOVA with post-hoc tests to compare C-MPP vs CPP and MPP. Correlate Y211 nanoparticle size/number density with Fv and R using regression. Quantify texture (EBSD FWHM) correlation with levitation performance. Establish process–structure–property maps to identify optimal layer ratio and CeO2 content.
Step24: Optimization loop. Based on Step23, refine C-MPP: adjust layer ratio to maximize Fv while keeping porosity ≤ 18 % and zero macro-cracks; tune CeO2 to minimize Y211 coarsening without inhibiting growth; adjust oxygenation time if ΔTc > 1 K. Re-run TSMG for the refined recipe with n ≥ 6 to confirm reproducibility.
Step25: Seed and interface robustness tests. Compare samples with and without CPP buffer pellet under the seed to quantify seed survival, parasitic grain incidence, and reproducibility. Examine the seed after growth for signs of corrosion. If corrosion observed, increase buffer thickness or reduce maximum T by 5–10 °C and lengthen dwell slightly to maintain full melt.
Step26: Substrate layer efficacy. Compare Yb2O3-coated vs uncoated substrates within the same run to assess stray grain suppression. Inspect bottom surfaces for unwanted nucleation. If stray grains persist, increase Yb2O3 layer thickness to ~200–300 μm or add a thin MgO foil barrier under Yb2O3.
Step27: Process control and QA. Calibrate furnace thermocouples before each run (melting-point standards). Log temperature, atmosphere, and power vs time. Maintain identical thermal histories by co-processing all groups in the same run when comparing. Record green density and mass for each pellet to track variability.
Step28: Safety and handling. Handle Ba–Cu–O melts and hot substrates with appropriate PPE. Ensure LN2 testing area has oxygen depletion monitoring. Dispose of Ce-containing waste per regulations. Avoid seed contamination by handling with clean tweezers and Al2O3 pads.
Step29: Documentation and acceptance criteria. A C-MPP batch is accepted if: (i) single-domain with four facet lines and no parasitic grains; (ii) porosity ≤ 18 % on a–c sections; (iii) no macro-cracks ≥ 0.6 mm length; (iv) Tc ≥ 90 K and ΔTc ≤ 1 K; (v) normalized Fv ≥ 1.27e−2 N mm−3 and relaxation R ≤ 13 % at 77 K; (vi) less than 5 % force degradation after 10,000 levitation cycles at 77 K.
Step30: Scale-up and batch uniformity. Using the optimized C-MPP recipe, produce a batch of ≥ 12 bulks in a single run to assess uniformity. Apply Steps13–23 to all bulks. If coefficient of variation for Fv exceeds 5–7 %, investigate green density variations, thermal gradients, or powder agglomeration and iterate mixing/pressing parameters.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – Precursor powder synthesis  
- Starting oxides: Y₂O₃, BaCO₃, CuO.  
- Three stoichiometric mixtures prepared:  
  – Y123 (YBa₂Cu₃O₇−δ)  
  – Y211 (Y₂BaCuO₅)  
  – Y023 (Ba₂Cu₃Oₓ)  
- Each mixture calcined twice (40 h per calcination) at 930 °C (Y123), 950 °C (Y211) and 880 °C (Y023).

Step 2 – Precursor powder blending  
- CPP: 35 mol % Y211 + balance Y123 + 1 wt % CeO₂.  
- MPP: 72.34 mol % Y₂O₃ (Y200) + Y023 + 1 wt % CeO₂.  
- Blending performed by ball-milling; no further milling parameters given.

Step 3 – Green-body preparation  
- 40 g powder pressed into 30 mm × 30 mm square pellets (thickness not specified).  
- C-MPP pellet: 20 g CPP powder placed above 20 g MPP powder in the same die and co-pressed.  
- Identical uniaxial pressing conditions used for all pellets (pressure value not specified).

Step 4 – Seed/buffer/substrate assembly (same for all pellets)  
- Top surface: one polished SmBCO single-crystal seed (a–b plane down).  
- Buffer mini-pellet (6 mm Ø × 2 mm thick, made from CPP) inserted between seed and main pellet.  
- Bottom layer: substrate of Y123 + Yb₂O₃ powders (functions as extra liquid source and nucleation barrier).  
- Entire assembly placed in furnace as illustrated in Fig. 1.

Step 5 – Top-seeded melt-growth (TSMG) heat treatment (all samples processed together)  
- Ramp to T_max = 1050 °C in 12 h; dwell 1.5 h.  
- Cool to T_s = 1010 °C at 80 °C h⁻¹ to initiate epitaxial growth.  
- Undercooling: 120 h linear cool to T_e = 970 °C.  
- Furnace cool to room temperature.  
- Seed, buffer and substrate mechanically removed afterwards.

Step 6 – Oxygenation  
- Samples annealed at 450 °C in flowing O₂ for 220 h.

Step 7 – Dimensional inspection and cutting  
- Samples measured (callipers) to obtain a–b plane area and c-axis thickness (Table 2).  
- Each bulk cut along the c-axis through the centre with a precision diamond wire saw.  
- Cut surface ground and polished with a precision diamond surface grinder/polisher.

Step 8 – Optical microstructure characterisation  
- Polished a–c cross-sections imaged with an optical microscope.  
- Three to four local regions (positions 1–3/4) selected for porosity quantification.  
- ImageJ software used to count pores (n) and measure average pore diameter (D).  
- Porosity calculated as (n × D)/S, where S is the inspected area (~2.71 mm²).

Step 9 – Levitation-force measurement  
- Instrument: custom-built SCML-05 platform (Fig. 3).  
- Magnet: second track of a Halbach NdFeB guideway; surface field 0.67 T at working height (WH) 5 mm.  
- Temperature: 77 K by continuous liquid-nitrogen cooling.  
- Two magnetisation modes:  
  – Zero-field cooling (ZFC): sample cooled at 60 mm above track, then lowered to 5 mm.  
  – Field cooling (FC): sample cooled at 30 mm above track, then lowered to 5 mm.  
- Procedure (identical for ZFC and FC):  
  1. Cool to 77 K at fixed height (ZFCH or FCH).  
  2. Lower to WH = 5 mm and immediately retract at 1 mm s⁻¹ to record force loop.  
  3. Lower again at 1 mm s⁻¹, hold 3 min to record force-relaxation curve.  
- Force data sampled continuously; maximum force (F_max) and minimum force after 3 min (F_min) extracted.  
- Relaxation rate R = (F_max – F_min)/F_max.

Step 10 – Finite-element (FE) normalisation of levitation force  
- COMSOL Multiphysics used with H-formulation.  
- PMG field first calculated analytically and imported (Fig. 12a).  
- 3-D bulk model created (Fig. 12b); J_c set to 1.1 × 10⁴ A cm⁻² (Bean model).  
- Parametric sweep: thickness h = 2–20 mm (step 0.1 mm between 9–10 mm) with fixed 26 mm × 26 mm a–b plane; then area S varied 441–676 mm² with h = 9.5 mm.  
- Linear regression performed on F_max and F_min vs. h (9–10 mm) and vs. S (441–676 mm²); slopes and R² recorded (Figs. 13–14).  
- Experimental forces normalised to a “standard” bulk of h = 9.5 mm and S = 550 mm² using the combined thickness-and-area coefficient k_v (Table 5).  
- Engineering densities calculated:  
  – Force-area density F_s = F_min/S  
  – Force-volume density F_v = F_min/V (Table 6).

[Experimental Design Details]
- All growth runs performed simultaneously in one furnace to ensure identical thermal history; a second C-MPP sample (CM3) processed in a different furnace for reproducibility check.  
- Temperature uniformity inside the furnace verified by multipoint thermocouples (details not given).  
- No porosity measurement uncertainty or image-analysis threshold specified.  
- Error bars or statistical spread of force values not provided.  
- Sample identification: CPP, MPP, CM1, CM2, CM3 (CM = C-MPP).

Experiment: Step1: Define objectives and sample matrix
- Objective: Fabricate monolithic, single-grain, (103)-textured hollow cylinders of YBa2Cu3O7−x with 20 wt% Y-site substitution by a ternary Nd/Sm/Gd mixture and 0.5 wt% WO3 nanoparticles, plus excess Ba processing, to maximize high-field Jc and magnetic shielding at 77 K.
- Sample matrix:
  a) Target composition: (Y0.8Nd0.0667Sm0.0667Gd0.0667)Ba2Cu3O7−x with 0.5 wt% WO3 (relative to final 123 mass), ~35–40 vol% (Y/RE)-211 precipitates.
  b) Controls: (i) Pure Y-123 with identical processing (no RE substitution, no WO3), (ii) Y0.8( Nd0.0667Sm0.0667Gd0.0667)-123 without WO3, (iii) Y-123 + 0.5 wt% WO3 (no RE substitution).
  c) Parametric sub-set: RE-substitution at 10% and 30% and WO3 at 0.2 wt% and 1.0 wt% to map Fp scaling and Bp shift.

Step2: Materials and equipment
- Powders: Y2O3, Nd2O3, Sm2O3, Gd2O3 (≥99.9%), BaCO3 (≥99.9%), CuO (≥99.9%), nano-WO3 (2–6 nm primary size, high purity), optional Ba(NO3)2 for solution processing of BaCuO2.
- Additives: Ammonium polyacrylate dispersant (e.g., Darvan C-N), polyacrylamide monomer (AM) and N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide (MBAM) crosslinker, ammonium persulfate (APS) initiator, TEMED accelerator, NH4OH for pH control, ethanol or isopropanol for wet milling.
- Molds and tooling: Rapid-prototyped (3D printed) molds for hollow cylinders (e.g., OD ≈ 20–40 mm, ID ≈ 10–30 mm, height ≈ 10–40 mm; adapt to furnace and VSM limits), alumina setters, MgO/alumina support plates.
- Seeds and deposition: NdBCO thin-film seeds with (103) orientation on MgO or SrTiO3 substrates (procured or deposited by PLD), or polished bulk NdBCO seed plates if thin films are not available.
- Furnaces: Box furnaces with programmable ramps up to 1100 °C (air), oxygen anneal furnace (≤ 600 °C), vacuum oven for drying.
- Characterization: XRD with Rietveld refinement and texture capability (pole figures), FE-SEM with EDS, FIB-TEM (optional), microhardness, Archimedes density setup, AC susceptibility (10–10 kHz), VSM up to ±9 T (10–77 K), Hall sensor and solenoid setup for magnetic shielding tests.

Step3: Synthesize (Y,NSG)-211 precursor powders by solid-state reaction
- Target stoichiometry: (Y0.8Nd0.0667Sm0.0667Gd0.0667)2BaCuO5 (solid solution 211 to supply mixed RE for substitution).
- Weigh and mix oxides: Y2O3, Nd2O3, Sm2O3, Gd2O3, BaCO3, and CuO to the (RE)2BaCuO5 ratio. Include slight CuO excess (~1–2 mol%) to compensate volatilization during calcination.
- Wet-mill in ethanol with zirconia media for 12–24 h, dry at 80 °C, sieve (≤ 250 μm).
- Calcine in air: 900–950 °C for 12 h, cool, re-mill and re-calcine (second 12 h cycle) to ensure phase purity. Confirm 211 formation by XRD (no significant 123 or BaCuO2 residuals). Aim for d50 ≈ 0.5–1.5 μm after final milling.

Step4: Prepare Ba–Cu oxide melt source with +2 wt% Ba excess
- Target melt composition: Ba–Cu oxide rich in BaCuO2 to favor infiltration; a common choice is Ba3Cu5Oy (3BaCuO2 + 2CuO).
- Synthesize BaCuO2: Mix stoichiometric BaCO3 and CuO, calcine at 900–950 °C in air (two cycles), then blend with additional CuO to achieve Ba3Cu5Oy. Add +2 wt% Ba (as BaCO3 or BaCuO2) relative to Ba content to generate Ba-rich melt for suppressing RE/Ba solid solutions and porosity.
- Press melt-source pellets (e.g., 10–20 mm diameter × 3–5 mm thick), prefire at 800–850 °C to strengthen, store in desiccator.

Step5: Prepare WO3 nanoparticle dispersion
- Disperse nano-WO3 (2–6 nm) in deionized water with ~1–2 wt% (relative to WO3) ammonium polyacrylate under ultrasonication for 30–60 min. Adjust pH to ~9–10 with NH4OH to maximize electrostatic stabilization.
- Verify dispersion quality via dynamic light scattering or sedimentation test; re-sonicate if necessary. Prepare concentrate at known solids content for accurate dosing.

Step6: Formulate sol-casting slurry for gelcasting
- Solids: (Y,NSG)-211 powder targeting 35–40 vol% after densification; design slurry solids loading at 50–60 vol% to ensure low shrinkage and high green density. Keep particle size unimodal to control packing.
- Add WO3 dispersion to reach 0.5 wt% WO3 relative to expected final 123 matrix mass (account for conversion of 211 to 123; as a practical approach, set WO3 at 0.5 wt% of total ceramic solids for consistency across samples).
- Add dispersant (0.5–1.0 wt% relative to powder), adjust pH to ~9–10. Ball mill (ZrO2 media) for 4–8 h to homogenize; avoid overheating.
- Polymer system: Add AM (e.g., 15–20 wt% of solvent for targeted green strength) and MBAM (1–3 mol% of AM). Degas under mild vacuum.
- Initiate polymerization by adding APS (1–2 wt% of AM) and TEMED (few drops per 100 mL) immediately before casting. Maintain temperature ~20–25 °C for controlled gel time (5–15 min).

Step7: Rapid-prototyped gelcasting of hollow cylinders
- Use 3D printed, nonreactive molds (e.g., resin with release coating) designed for the target dimensions and including a split feature for demolding.
- Cast slurry to fill annular space; gently vibrate to remove bubbles. Cover to minimize evaporation.
- Gel at room temperature, then demold after gelation completes (≤ 1 h). Cure overnight at 25 °C.

Step8: Drying and binder burnout of green bodies
- Drying: 25 °C, 40–60% RH for 24–48 h; then 60 °C for 12 h. Support parts to minimize warping.
- Binder burnout in air: heat at 0.5–1.0 °C/min to 250 °C (2 h), then to 450 °C (2 h) and to 600 °C (2 h). Cool to room temperature. Monitor for cracking; adjust ramp if needed.

Step9: Preform presintering to establish robust, porous skeleton
- Heat in air at 880–920 °C for 2–4 h to lightly sinter the 211 network while preserving open porosity (target ~25–35% open porosity for effective infiltration). Determine porosity via Archimedes (water or ethanol immersion).

Step10: Seed preparation and verification
- NdBCO thin-film seeds: Obtain (103)-oriented NdBCO films on MgO or SrTiO3 plates (e.g., 5–10 mm squares). Verify orientation by XRD (θ–2θ and pole figures).
- If thin films are unavailable, use polished bulk NdBCO seed plates with appropriate orientation; ensure seed peritectic temperature exceeds processing temperature.
- Clean seed surfaces (ethanol), mountable on top and bottom faces of the preform.

Step11: Infiltration growth assembly
- Stack: Place Ba–Cu melt-source pellets in intimate contact with the top and bottom faces of the preform; place NdBCO seed on the outer surfaces of the melt-source pellets or interpose a thin (e.g., ~100 μm) porous alumina felt to promote wetting while maintaining seed protection. Alternatively, place seeds directly on the preform faces with a thin Ba–Cu layer beneath; ensure good thermal contact and alignment.
- Fixture: Place assembly on MgO or alumina setter; ensure vertical alignment to encourage symmetric infiltration. Use a light alumina weight (≤ 50 g) to maintain contact without crushing.

Step12: Infiltration growth thermal profile (air)
- Ramp: 3–5 °C/min to 700 °C (1 h), then 3 °C/min to 980 °C (1 h), then 1–2 °C/min to T_max near but below seed peritectic (typ. 1020–1040 °C depending on seed stability; confirm seed limit beforehand). Hold 1–2 h to fully melt Ba–Cu source and initiate infiltration.
- Infiltration/growth: Maintain T_max to allow full wetting and infiltration through the wall thickness (4–12 h depending on geometry and porosity). Then slow-cool at 0.2–0.5 °C/h through the 123 growth window (~1020→980 °C) to promote single-grain growth seeded from both ends with (103) texture. After passing ~980 °C, cool at 1–3 °C/min to 500 °C, then furnace-cool to room temperature.
- Notes:
  a) Use air atmosphere to suppress RE/Ba solid solution and excessive Ba loss; the +2 wt% Ba excess in melt compensates Ba consumption and reduces spherical porosity.
  b) If melt bleed-out occurs, add an alumina ring around the sample to contain flux.
  c) If seed dissolution is observed, reduce T_max by 5–10 °C or increase cooling rate slightly.

Step13: Oxygenation anneal
- Load parts in flowing oxygen (0.5–1 L/min), ramp at 1 °C/min to 450 °C, hold for 100–150 h to fully oxygenate (optimize for target Tc), then cool at 1 °C/min to room temperature in oxygen. For thick walls (>5 mm), extend hold to ensure uniform oxygen diffusion.

Step14: Machining and specimen preparation
- Lightly lap outer/inner surfaces to remove reaction layers and release seed residues without altering texture. Avoid water coolant if possible; use minimal lubricant and dry after.
- Prepare small bar specimens (e.g., 2×2×5 mm) cut from the cylinder wall for VSM tests with defined orientation relative to the (103) texture. Preserve one cylinder per composition for shielding tests.

Step15: Phase and texture characterization
- XRD (powder mode on crushed fragments): Rietveld refinement of lattice parameters a, b, c; quantify phase fractions (123, 211, BaWO4/WO3, Ba–Cu oxides). Confirm lattice parameters close to standard Y-123 and note any shifts due to RE substitution.
- Texture: XRD pole figures for (103) and (00l) reflections on the cylinder wall; compute Lotgering factor or orientation distribution; rocking-curve FWHM for (103) peak.
- Density: Archimedes to quantify residual porosity.

Step16: Microstructure and chemistry
- SEM (secondary and backscattered): assess 211 dispersions (0–2 μm), interface density, pores. Quantify 211 volume fraction and size distribution by image analysis (>500 particles per sample).
- EDS mapping/point analysis: map Y, Nd, Sm, Gd distribution across matrix and 211; map W to identify WO3/BaWO4 nanoprecipitates. Check for RE/Ba solid solution indicators.
- TEM/STEM (select samples): verify stacking faults, 123/211 interfaces, nanoprecipitate size (2–10 nm), and possible BaWO4 formation; correlate to pinning center types.
- Fractography (if cracking observed): identify failure modes.

Step17: Superconducting transition and connectivity
- AC susceptibility: measure χ′ and χ″ vs T (10–110 K, small AC field, e.g., 0.1–1 mT) on bars and small ring sections. Extract Tc(onset) and ΔTc; target sharp ΔTc (≤ 1.5–2 K).
- Four-probe resistivity (optional) on polished bars to confirm Tc and normal-state behavior.

Step18: Magnetization and critical current density measurements
- VSM: Measure M(H) hysteresis loops from −9 to +9 T at 10, 20, 40, 60, and 77 K on bars cut along defined orientations to minimize demagnetizing uncertainty. For ring segments, use appropriate sample holders and record geometry precisely.
- Data reduction: Compute Jc from ΔM using the extended Bean model appropriate for the specimen geometry (rectangular prism or ring section), including demagnetization corrections. Report Jc(B,T).
- Pinning force: Fp = μ0 Jc B. Determine Fp,max and Bp at each temperature; perform normalized Fp scaling f(b) analysis with b = B/Birr to extract p, q exponents and dominant pinning types (e.g., δκ, δl).
- Compare target vs controls to isolate contributions from RE substitution, WO3 nanoparticles, and texture.

Step19: Magnetic shielding test at 77 K
- Setup: Wind a small solenoid (e.g., length ≥ sample height, uniform field zone) on nonmagnetic former. Calibrate field with a Hall probe at room temperature and at 77 K without sample.
- Mount the oxygenated cylinder coaxially around the solenoid; place a calibrated cryogenic Hall probe at the geometric center inside the hollow. Immerse in liquid nitrogen.
- Procedure: Ramp DC current to generate external fields up to several tens of gauss (and higher if needed). Record internal field vs applied field to quantify shielding factor. Identify onset of flux penetration and maximum shielded field. Repeat for controls.
- Trapped-field (optional): Field-cool under a known field, switch off current, and measure trapped field distribution on inner and outer surfaces.

Step20: Acceptance criteria and iteration
- Structural: Single-phase 123 matrix with (103) texture; 211 uniformly distributed (average 0.5–2 μm); minimal secondary porosity; evidence of nanoscale W-containing precipitates.
- Superconducting: Tc ≈ 90–93 K with ΔTc ≤ 2 K; high intergranular connectivity.
- Magnetic: At 77 K, Jc(0 T) ≥ 4 kA cm−2; at high field, Jc at 8–9 T within target range; Fp,max at 77 K near several ×10 N cm−3 with Bp ≈ 7–8 T; presence of secondary low-field Fp peak attributable to nano-inclusions.
- Shielding: Demonstrable attenuation ≥ tens of gauss at 77 K for the target geometry.
- If criteria are not met, iterate on: WO3 dispersion quality (re-sonicate, alter dispersant), Ba excess (+1–3 wt%), porosity of preform (adjust presinter), T_max and cooling rate (refine to maintain seed, reduce microcracks), solids loading and gelcasting parameters to minimize shrinkage and cracks.

Step21: Control experiments and attribution
- Compare target to controls to deconvolve effects:
  a) Texture-only improvement (seeded IG on undoped Y-123).
  b) Compositional disorder (20% RE substitution without WO3).
  c) Interface/point pinning (WO3 only).
- Use Fp scaling and microstructural statistics to connect pinning features (stacking faults, 211 interfaces, W-precipitates) to observed Fp(b) characteristics.

Step22: Documentation and safety
- Record all batch compositions, milling times, pH, zeta potential (if measured), gelation times, furnace logs, and oxygenation durations.
- Safety: Handle nano-WO3 in fume hood with appropriate PPE; manage Ba–Cu melts at high temperature with shields; avoid inhalation of fine oxides; dispose of waste per regulations.

Step23: Timeline and resources
- Powder synthesis and QC: 2–3 weeks.
- Slurry optimization and gelcasting: 1–2 weeks.
- Burnout and presintering: 1 week.
- Infiltration growth (per batch): 3–5 days including cooldown.
- Oxygenation: 1 week.
- Characterization and magnetics: 2–3 weeks.
- Shielding tests and analysis: 1–2 weeks.
- Total per iteration: ~8–10 weeks.

Step24: Risk mitigation and troubleshooting
- Seed degradation: Verify seed stability; lower T_max or reduce hold time; use protective buffer layer; increase slow-cooling precision.
- Nonuniform infiltration: Increase open porosity (reduce presinter temp/time), improve contact with melt-source pellets, add capillary wicks.
- Poor WO3 dispersion: Increase dispersant, adjust pH, employ prolonged ultrasonication, consider surface-functionalized WO3.
- Excess Ba secondary phases: Tune Ba excess to 1–2 wt% range; adjust air flow to control volatilization; clean reaction layer post-growth.
- Cracking/porosity: Optimize gelcasting solids loading, burnout ramps, and cooling rates; consider partial isostatic pressing of green bodies if dimensional constraints allow (without sealing pores).

Step25: Reporting
- Provide full microstructure–property correlations, including texture metrics, 211 fraction/size, W-precipitate size, Jc(B,T), Fp scaling parameters, and shielding performance versus geometry, with clear attribution to the five tuning strategies (composition, interface, texture, stress via Ba excess, grain boundary removal via IG).

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – Precursor powders (all by solid-state reaction)  
- Y-123, Y-211, (Nd0.33Sm0.33Gd0.33)2BaCuO5 (NSG-211) and Yb-rich liquid-phase powder (Yb2O3:CuO:BaCuO2 = 1:6:10) prepared from commercial oxides/carbonates (>99 %).  
- 2 wt % excess Ba added to all batches to suppress RE/Ba solid-solution formation during air processing.  
- WO3 nanoparticles (2–6 nm) synthesised separately; 0.5 wt % added to the final powder mix.

Step 2 – Sol-casting of powder mix  
- 80 wt % Y-211 + 20 wt % NSG-211 + 0.5 wt % WO3 dispersed in an aqueous premix containing methacrylamide (monomer), MBAM (cross-linker) and Darvan 821-A (dispersant) to give 37 vol % solid loading.  
- Slurry ball-milled 8 h; TEMED catalyst and APS initiator added, remixed 10 min.

Step 3 – Net-shape forming (RPGC)  
- CAD model of the hollow-cylinder negative drawn (SolidWorks) and printed (Creality CR-5 h Pro, ABS filament, 0.4 mm wall, wax-coated).  
- Slurry cast into the ABS mould, gelled, cured 5 h at 60 °C.  
- Mould dissolved in acetone; green body dried 5 days at 50 °C, 90 % RH.  
- Organic binders burnt out at 800 °C for 24 h in air.

Step 4 – Pre-sinter & infiltration setup  
- Green preform pre-sintered 950 °C / 4 h.  
- Liquid-phase pellets (32 mm Ø × 30 mm) uniaxially pressed and stacked above, below and inside the bore of the preform; whole assembly placed on a Y2O3 base.  
- Infiltration carried out at 1060 °C for 1.5 h in air, furnace cooled. Excess liquid removed after cooling.

Step 5 – Seeded single-grain growth  
- Buffer pellets (75 wt % Y-123 + 25 wt % Y-211, pre-annealed 900 °C) capped with NdBCO thin-film seeds positioned on both ends of the infiltrated cylinder.  
- Heat treatment (air): ramp to 1050 °C in 1 h → rapid cool to 1012 °C → slow cool 0.2 °C h⁻¹ to 980 °C → furnace cool to RT.  
- Buffer pellets removed; cylinder surface lightly polished.  
- Oxygenation: 450 °C / 7 days in flowing O2.

Step 6 – Structural & microstructural characterisation  
- XRD (Cu Kα) on top surface and on ground powder; Rietveld refinement to obtain lattice parameters.  
- Optical and FESEM on polished sections (final polish 0.5 µm diamond); Image-J used to quantify RE-211 area fraction and size distribution.  
- EDAX area scan to confirm RE (Nd, Sm, Gd) incorporation.

Step 7 – Superconducting property measurements  
- AC-susceptibility (real part) versus T to obtain Tc and transition width ΔTc.  
- Magnetic shielding test at 77 K: homemade copper solenoid (ID 7.5 cm, length 16 cm) producing up to 41 G dc; axial field monitored with and without the cylinder.  
- M–H hysteresis loops (1.8 × 2.4 × 5.4 mm³ bar cut from top slice) recorded in a commercial magnetometer at 10, 20, 30, 50, 77 K up to 9 T.  
- Jc(B) extracted from loop width via extended Bean model:  
  Jc = 20 ΔM / [a (1 – a/3b)] with a < b the sample cross-section dimensions.  
- Flux-pinning force density Fp = Jc·B plotted versus B; normalized curves f(h) = Fp/Fp,max versus h = B/Bp constructed and compared with theoretical δκ, point- and surface-pinning functions to identify the dominant mechanism.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Final target composition: YBa2Cu3O7−x matrix containing ~20 wt % (Nd,Sm,Gd)BCO and 0.5 wt % WO3 nanoparticles.  
- Cylinder dimensions after growth: 45 mm long hollow geometry (exact outer/inner diameters not specified in the paper).  
- Infiltration temperature/time: 1060 °C / 1.5 h (air); growth cooling rate 0.2 °C h⁻¹ between 1012 °C and 980 °C.  
- Oxygenation: 450 °C for 7 days (O2 atmosphere).  
- RE-211 particle size after processing: majority 0–2 µm; area fraction ~37 %.  
- Tc onset ≈ 93 K; ΔTc (10 %–90 %) ≈ 1.5 K.  
- Jc(77 K, 0 T) ≈ 4.4 kA cm⁻²; Jc(77 K, 8.5 T) ≈ 0.4 kA cm⁻².

Alternatively use Ag metal powder of comparable size if Ag2O is unavailable, acknowledging minor differences in oxygen release during melting. Step6: Weigh powders for each composition. Mix a small batch (e.g., 60 wt% Gd211, 30 wt% Gd123, 10 wt% Ag2O with the same BaCeO3 level as the main pellet), press a 3–5 mm diameter, 1–2 mm thick buffer. Dissolve small chips in suitable acids and analyze by ICP-OES for Ce content to quantify total incorporation vs nominal addition. Use PPE during powder handling; manage Ag2O to avoid photodecomposition; vent oxygen anneals properly; handle Ce salts and nitrates with care, avoiding inhalation and skin contact. [Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Precursor preparation  
- Mix 70 wt % GdBa₂Cu₃O₇ (Gd123) and 30 wt % Gd₂BaCuO₅ (Gd211) powders.  
- Add 10 wt % Ag₂O powder.  
- Add nanosize BaCeO₃ powder (synthesised by a sol-gel method) at six levels: 0.189, 0.378, 0.567, 0.945, 1.890, 2.836 wt % (equivalent to 0.1–1.5 wt % CeO₂).  
- Homogenise the powder mixture and uniaxially press into 20 g cylindrical pellets (diameter 20 mm).

Step 2: Single-grain growth by TSMG  
- Place a commercial NdBCO thin-film seed (on MgO substrate) on top of each pellet.  
- Heat to 1060 °C, hold 1 h.  
- Cool to 1020 °C at 100 °C h⁻¹.  
- Grow single grain by slow cooling from 1020 °C to 975 °C at 0.4 °C h⁻¹.  
- Furnace-cool to room temperature.  
- Anneal grown pellets (Ø ≈ 17.5 mm) in flowing O₂ at 400 °C for 10 days to obtain orthorhombic Gd123.

Step 3: Structural characterisation  
- X-ray diffraction (Rigaku Ultima IV, Cu Kα, spinning mode) on polished top (a/b) surfaces to verify single-grain nature and identify phases.  
- Cut samples along the a/c-plane, polish, and examine by optical polarisation microscopy (Nikon UDMLV 100 D-U) and SEM (TESCAN Mira 3LM) with EDS.  
- Use image processing on SEM/optical images to quantify Gd211 particle size (d₂₁₁), volume fraction (V₂₁₁), Ag particles and porosity.

Step 4: Trapped-field measurement at 77 K  
- Magnetise each bulk in a 1.4 T field using a Weiss electromagnet (field-cooling): ramp current to 14 A at ≈14 A min⁻¹, cool to 77 K, hold 3 min, ramp down at same rate.  
- Scan the seeded surface with a Hall probe (step 0.3 mm, probe-to-sample distance ≈130 µm) to obtain 3D trapped-field profiles.

Step 5: Preparation of small test specimens  
- From the c-growth sector cut 1.5 × 1.5 × 0.5 mm³ pieces at three standardised locations: A (2 mm below seed), B (middle), C (end) (positions defined in Fig. 1).

Step 6: Magnetisation measurements  
- Zero-field-cooling (ZFC) magnetisation vs temperature in 1 mT field parallel to c-axis (Vibrating Sample Magnetometer, Cryogenic Limited).  
- Determine Tc as the 50 % point of the magnetic transition curve; transition width ΔTc = Tc(90 %) – Tc(10 %).  
- Measure M–B hysteresis loops at 77 K on the same pieces; calculate Jc using the extended Bean model.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Sample series: Gd01, Gd02, Gd03, Gd05, Gd10, Gd15 (numbers indicate nominal CeO₂ equivalent wt %).  
- All heating/cooling steps performed in a furnace (atmosphere not specified beyond O₂ anneal).  
- No information given on heating/cooling atmosphere before oxygen anneal.  
- No details on sol-gel parameters for BaCeO₃ synthesis except reference [10].  
- No specification of loop field range or sweep rate for VSM M–B measurements.

Experiment: Step1: Define targets and acceptance criteria: (a) Js ≥ 1 MA cm−2 at 77 K, 3 T and retention well above 0.3 MA cm−2 up to 8 T; (b) Js > 15 MA cm−2 at 3 K, self-field; (c) lift factor at 4.2 K ≥ 20 relative to 77 K self-field; (d) relaxation rate Q ≤ 0.06 for T ≤ 50 K and μ0H ≤ 8 T; (e) c-axis texture with rocking-curve FWHM ≤ 1.5°; (f) continuous BaZrO3 (BZO) columns aligned with the c-axis, 5–9 nm diameter, areal density ≈ 1.1×10^11 cm−2, no agglomerates or secondary phases.

Step2: Select and prepare templates: (a) Mechanism study on single-crystal SrTiO3(001) or LaAlO3(001) substrates for baseline microstructure; (b) Application-relevant coated conductor on Hastelloy with IBAD-MgO templates and standard buffer architecture (e.g., Y2O3/YSZ/CeO2/LaMnO3) with in-plane misorientation Δφ ≤ 3°. Clean substrates by solvent rinse (acetone/isopropanol), UV-ozone 20 min, and pre-anneal in O2 at 750–800 °C for 30 min to desorb contaminants.

Step3: MOCVD precursor selection and delivery setup: Use metal–organic chelates with compatible vapor pressures: Y(thd)3, Gd(thd)3, Ba(thd)2, Cu(thd)2 for REBCO; Zr(thd)4 for BZO. Use heated bubblers with N2 carrier; set bubbler temperatures to achieve stable partial pressures (typical ranges: Y/Gd 170–200 °C, Ba 170–190 °C, Cu 150–170 °C, Zr 150–180 °C). Calibrate individual precursor mass delivery via in situ quartz crystal microbalance on witness substrates and ex situ XRF/ICP-MS on test films.

Step4: Gas and pressure conditions: Use high-purity O2 as oxidant with N2 carrier. Total chamber pressure 5–15 Torr; O2 partial pressure 0.3–1.0 Torr. Maintain gas flow uniformity with showerhead distribution; employ substrate rotation (≥300 rpm) for thickness and composition uniformity.

Step5: Compositional feed ratios: Target RE:Ba:Cu = 1:(2+ΔBa):(3) with ΔBa matched to added Zr for 10 mol% BZO relative to REBCO formula units. For each REBCO unit, add 0.10 Ba and 0.10 Zr to form BaZrO3; keep Y:Gd = 0.5:0.5. Verify that added Ba does not perturb REBCO stoichiometry by compensating Ba feed accordingly.

Step6: Substrate temperature and growth rate window: Set substrate temperature 770–795 °C (optimize within ±5 °C) to promote c-axis epitaxy of REBCO and self-assembly of vertical BZO nanocolumns. Target growth rate 0.6–1.0 µm h−1 to achieve 1.5 µm thickness in 90–150 min. Avoid rates >1.2 µm h−1 which can broaden column diameters and induce misalignment.

Step7: Nucleation and steady-state growth: Initiate with a 20–50 nm REBCO seed layer without Zr to establish texture, then ramp Zr and extra Ba flows over 1–2 min to full 10 mol% BZO for the remaining thickness. Maintain steady precursor flows thereafter to keep column continuity. Monitor substrate temperature drift within ±2 °C.

Step8: Stress and interface tuning during growth: Keep thickness to 1.5 µm; avoid sudden temperature or pressure changes. Use LaMnO3 cap buffer on IBAD tapes to reduce lattice mismatch and residual stress. If wafer curvature indicates >300 MPa residual tensile stress, reduce Zr flux by 10–15% and/or lower growth rate by 10% to mitigate cracking while preserving column continuity.

Step9: Post-deposition oxygenation: Cool to 500–520 °C in 1 atm O2, hold 60–120 min to fully oxygenate REBCO (δ ≲ 0.1), then slow-cool to room temperature at 5–10 °C min−1. For tapes, perform ex situ oxygenation in flowing O2 at 450–500 °C for 2 h if in situ oxygenation is limited.

Step10: Thickness and surface inspection: Measure thickness by cross-section SEM and stylus profilometry; target 1.5 ± 0.1 µm. Use AFM to assess surface roughness (RMS < 10 nm over 5×5 µm2) and check for hillocks or agglomerates; flag any surface particulates >50 nm for process adjustment.

Step11: Phase and texture verification by XRD: θ–2θ scan to confirm c-axis oriented REBCO (00l) and BZO reflections without secondary phases (e.g., BaCuO2). Rocking curve ω-scan of REBCO(005) with FWHM ≤ 1.5°; φ-scan of REBCO(103) to confirm in-plane alignment; reciprocal-space maps around REBCO(103)/(109) and BZO peaks to assess strain state and coherency.

Step12: Microstructure by STEM: Prepare cross-sectional and plan-view lamellae by FIB with low-kV polish (≤2 kV) to minimize damage. Acquire HAADF-STEM to visualize BZO columns; perform EDS/EELS mapping to confirm Zr confinement in columns and coherent interfaces with REBCO. Quantify column diameter distribution (target 5–9 nm), inter-column spacing, and continuity along the c-axis across the 1.5 µm thickness.

Step13: Column density quantification: From plan-view HAADF images (≥1 µm2 fields), count columns to compute areal density; target (1.1 ± 0.2)×10^11 cm−2. Ensure uniformity by sampling at multiple positions along tape length or across wafer.

Step14: Residual strain assessment: Use nano-beam diffraction or 4D-STEM strain mapping across columns and matrix to quantify local strain; complement with XRD RSM-derived in-plane and out-of-plane lattice parameters. Use micro-Raman (Ag modes) to assess tensile/compressive stress and oxygen order; correlate with crack-free morphology.

Step15: Magnetization measurements (VSM-PPMS): Cut specimens to well-defined rectangles (a ≤ b, typical a=1–2 mm, b=2–4 mm) with thickness measured accurately. Measure M(H) loops at T = 3, 20, 30, 40, 50, 65, 77, 85 K for μ0H = 0–9 T; use sweep rates 50, 100, 200 Oe s−1 for dynamic relaxation. Calculate sheet current density Js from Bean critical-state model for rectangular prisms: Js = 20ΔM/[a(1 − a/3b)] (in A cm−1), then Jc = Js/thickness.

Step16: Dynamic relaxation analysis: Compute Q = d ln Js / d ln(dB/dt) from loops at multiple sweep rates. Additionally, perform time-dependent relaxation at fixed H and T (measure M(t) over 10^2–10^4 s) to extract S = −d ln M / d ln t. Derive effective barrier U* = T/Q and its J dependence to estimate glassy exponent µ via collective creep models. Confirm Q ≤ 0.06 for T ≤ 50 K and μ0H ≤ 8 T if achieved.

Step17: Angular dependence of pinning: Measure Jc(θ) at T = 20, 50, 77 K for μ0H = 1, 3, 5, 8 T with θ spanning −90° to +90° relative to c-axis. Expect a pronounced peak at θ = 0° indicating c-axis correlated pinning by BZO columns; quantify peak height, width (FWHM), and anisotropy ratio γJc. Compare with ab-plane peak near ±90°.

Step18: Transport Jc and n-value: Pattern 10–50 µm wide bridges by photolithography and Ar ion milling; deposit Au contacts. Measure E–J at 77 K and 65 K in μ0H = 0–5 T, angles θ = 0°, ±30°, ±90°. Use 1 µV cm−1 criterion to extract Jc and power-law exponent n from E = Ec(J/Jc)^n. Compare transport Jc to magnetization-derived Jc to verify scaling and connectivity.

Step19: Pinning mechanism discrimination (GIS and scaling): (a) Use Griessen temperature scaling to fit reduced Jc(t) = Jc(T)/Jc(0) at fixed fields to δl- and δTc-type expressions; determine fractional contributions as a function of field by fitting as a weighted sum. (b) Construct normalized pinning force curves Fp/Fp,max vs reduced field h = H/Hirr(T) and fit to Dew-Hughes forms to identify dominant p and q exponents. (c) Analyze how the dominant mechanism shifts from δTc at low field to δl at higher field, correlating with columnar BZO density.

Step20: Vortex phase diagram construction: Determine irreversibility field Hirr(T) from closure of M(H) hysteresis or from transport onset of dissipation at 1 µV cm−1. Map elastic creep regime boundaries by contours of constant Q (e.g., Q = 0.06) and by changes in the glassy exponent µ. Delineate elastic vortex-glass region expansion relative to a control film without BZO.

Step21: Process–structure–property feedback: Correlate column diameter and density with Jc(θ), Fp(h) peak position, Q(T,H), and U*(J). Identify optimal parameter windows where columns remain continuous, coherent, and 5–9 nm in diameter with minimal residual strain.

Step22: Targeted δTc-pinning enhancement without compromising columns: Implement controlled nanoscale composition/strain fluctuations by (a) slight RE site modulation (e.g., adjust Y:Gd to 0.55:0.45 or 0.45:0.55 in small increments) to create Tc inhomogeneity; (b) fine-tune post-oxygenation plateau (e.g., 480–520 °C, 30–120 min) to modulate oxygen ordering; (c) introduce low-level RE/Ba off-stoichiometry gradients via small ramp in RE flux (≤3%) during growth. After each perturbation, re-run Steps 11–20 to quantify changes in δTc vs δl contributions.

Step23: Parameter sweep (design of experiments): Prepare a matrix varying (a) BZO content: 5, 10, 15 mol%; (b) substrate temperature: 770, 780, 790, 800 °C; (c) growth rate: 0.6, 0.8, 1.0 µm h−1; (d) thickness: 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 µm; (e) oxygenation schedule as in Step22. Use identical templates to isolate effects. For each film, execute Steps 10–20. Identify trade-offs between column alignment, strain, and Jc retention at 77 K, 3–8 T.

Step24: Grain boundary control on tapes: Produce films on IBAD templates with Δφ ≈ 2–3° and, for comparison, Δφ ≥ 5°. Map transport Ic along 10–30 cm lengths by non-contact Hall-probe scanning and four-probe segments. Examine grain boundary weak-link behavior via MO imaging; correlate Δφ with Jc and n-values to ensure grain boundary tuning maintains uniform current flow and symmetric M(H) loops without second peaks.

Step25: Reliability and thermal cycling: Subject selected optimized films/tapes to 50 thermal cycles between 300 K and 77 K; re-measure XRD rocking curves, AFM, and Jc(77 K, 3 T) to assess stability of columns and strain. Perform repeated M(H) loops to verify persistent low Q and absence of degradation.

Step26: Scale-up demonstration: Deposit 1.5 µm, 10 mol% BZO REBCO on 30–100 cm IBAD tapes under optimized conditions. Map Ic uniformity (≥95% within ±10% variation) and Jc(θ) at 77 K, 3 T across the length. Verify microstructure at head/mid/tail positions by cross-sectional STEM to confirm column continuity and density uniformity.

Step27: Data reduction and reporting: Compile microstructure metrics (diameter, density, continuity), texture (ω, φ), strain, magnetization/transport Jc vs T, H, θ, relaxation metrics (Q, S, U*), GIS/deconvolution of δl and δTc contributions, and vortex phase diagrams. Compare against Step1 targets; iterate process parameters if criteria are not met. Finalize a reproducible recipe and control charts for MOCVD growth delivering the required hybrid pinning landscape for fusion/MRI magnet applications.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Film growth  
- 10 % BaZrO₃-doped (Y₀.₅Gd₀.₅)Ba₂Cu₃O₇₋δ film grown by metal–organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD).  
- Final superconducting layer thickness ≈ 1.5 µm (value given in paper).

Step 2: Micro-structural verification  
- Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) in plan-view and cross-section to confirm:  
  – columnar defects continuous along the c-axis, diameter 5–9 nm, average in-plane spacing ≈ 29.5 nm, areal density n ≈ 1.1 × 10¹¹ cm⁻².  
  – no large agglomerates (images shown in Fig. 1).

Step 3: Basic superconducting characterisation  
- Zero-field-cooled (ZFC) and field-cooled (FC) dc magnetic susceptibility versus temperature (M-T) recorded in PPMS-DynaCool-9 with VSM option.  
- Applied field 10 Oe perpendicular to film plane; temperature error < 0.01 K; measurement window 3–85 K.  
- Onset Tc = 89.1 K (transition width not quantified).

Step 4: Magnetic-hysteresis-loop (MHL) acquisition  
- MHLs recorded at selected temperatures (3–85 K) with external field H ‖ c-axis, swept between −8 T and +8 T.  
- Two sweep rates used: 50 Oe s⁻¹ and 200 Oe s⁻¹ (sufficient to resolve rate-dependent magnetisation according to authors).  
- Bean model applied to convert loop width ΔM to transient current density Js:  
  Js = 20 ΔM / [V·a(1 − a/3b)] with a < b the in-plane sample dimensions and V the volume.

Step 5: Dynamical magnetisation-relaxation measurement  
- At each (T, H) point the field sweep is paused and magnetisation M(t) recorded while the field is held constant.  
- Dynamical relaxation rate extracted as  
  Q = d ln(ΔM) / d ln(dB/dt) = d ln Js / d ln(dB/dt).  
- Field range: 0–8 T; temperature range: 3–85 K.  
- From Q(T) the ratio T/Q is formed; linear extrapolation of T/Q → 0 K gives characteristic pinning energy Uc(0,B)/kB ≈ 145 K for all studied fields.

Step 6: Construction of vortex phase diagram  
- Irreversibility field Hirr defined by criterion Jc = 100 A cm⁻².

- Normalised pinning energy function g(t, Be) calculated within the Griessen-Ioan-Schnack (GIS) framework.

- No details given on sample patterning, photolithography, or substrate removal.

- Fix FeCl₃ concentration at 200 g/L (best from Step 2).

- Fix FeCl₃ at 200 g/L and temperature at 0 °C.  
- Etch separate samples for 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 min; terminate by immediate dilution/rinse.
