Experiment: Step1: Define objectives and metrics: quantify how 4 wt % BaZrO3 (BZO) nanorod artificial pinning centres (APCs) in 200 nm epitaxial YBa2Cu3O6+x (YBCO) thin films on SrTiO3 (STO) (100) impact vortex pinning (Jc(B,θ), B*), transport n-value, and quench behavior (minimum quench energy MQE and normal-zone propagation velocity NZPV) versus an APC-free reference across 20–70 K, 0–8 T, and field angles, using microbridges that eliminate extrinsic grain boundary effects.

Step2: Materials and equipment: 10 mm × 10 mm × 0.5 mm STO (100) substrates; PLD system with KrF excimer laser (248 nm) and multi-target carousel; dense ceramic PLD targets: YBCO and YBCO+4 wt % BZO composite; standard chemicals for substrate cleaning (acetone, IPA), photoresists (e.g., S1813) and developer (MF-319), 10 wt % H3PO4 for wet etch; metallization (Ti/Au or Cr/Au) for contacts and on-chip heater; SQUID-VSM; XRD (θ–2θ, ω-rocking, φ-scan); AFM; Cs-corrected STEM (HAADF, EDS/EELS) at 200 kV; PPMS with 9 T (or 8 T minimum), variable temperature (20–300 K), sample rotator; NI PXIe-1073 (or equivalent) DAQ with ≥100 kS/s per channel; low-noise current sources/voltage sources; cryo-compatible wiring; magnet probe with multiple contacts; safety gear for laser, cryogens, acids.

Step3: PLD target preparation and verification: procure or fabricate a YBCO target and a composite YBCO+4 wt % BZO target (BZO uniformly dispersed); verify target density and composition by XRD and ICP-OES (for target bulk); polish target faces to uniform finish; pre-ablate to remove surface contamination.

Step4: Substrate preparation: solvent clean STO substrates (acetone, IPA), rinse DI water, blow dry; UV-ozone or oxygen plasma clean (5–10 min) to promote wetting; mount on heater block with backside silver paste or clamps to ensure thermal contact and planarity; preload in PLD chamber; outgas at ~700–750°C in 1×10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ Torr for 30 min.

Step5: PLD growth parameter calibration on test wafers (no BZO) to achieve epitaxial c-axis YBCO at 200 nm: substrate temperature 760–800°C, oxygen partial pressure 150–300 mTorr, KrF laser fluence 1.5–2.0 J cm⁻², rep rate 5–7 Hz, target–substrate distance 50–55 mm; determine growth rate (nm/pulse) by XRR on calibration films; select pulse count for 200 ± 10 nm thickness; implement in-situ RHEED if available to monitor layer-by-layer growth quality; verify Tc and c-axis texture on test.

Step6: Grow APC-free YBCO films: deposit 200 nm YBCO on STO using calibrated parameters; after deposition, ramp oxygen pressure to 300–500 Torr while cooling to 500°C, hold 30–60 min in 1 atm O2 to oxygenate (adjust to target doping level yielding Tc ≈ 88–92 K); cool to room temperature in O2; prepare at least n=3 wafers for statistics.

Step7: Grow 4 wt % BZO-doped YBCO films: use the YBCO+4 wt % BZO composite target under identical conditions to Step6 to maintain comparability; keep growth rate modest to encourage vertical alignment of BZO nanorods; same post-growth oxygenation protocol; prepare at least n=3 wafers.

Step8: Thickness and basic electrical screening: measure thickness by XRR or stylus profilometry on a masked step; pattern simple four-probe bars on as-grown films (temporary shadow mask) to measure R(T) 300–10 K; verify metallic normal-state behavior, sharp superconducting transition, and similar Tc between APC-free and BZO-doped within ±1 K; reject outliers.

Step9: Structural and texture characterization: perform XRD θ–2θ to confirm c-axis orientation and check secondary phases; measure (00l) rocking curve FWHM and in-plane φ-scans of (103)/(113) to assess epitaxy and mosaic spread; compare c-axis lattice parameter (oxygen content proxy); AFM scan 5×5 µm² for surface roughness and particulates; target RMS < 5 nm.

Step10: Nanostructure confirmation by STEM: prepare cross-sectional TEM lamellae by FIB with low-kV final polish; acquire HAADF-STEM images along [010]/[100] to visualize c-axis-aligned BZO nanorods; measure nanorod diameter and spacing statistics over multiple regions; perform EDS/EELS to confirm Zr- and Ba-rich nanorods and coherent interface with YBCO; confirm absence of unwanted secondary phases.

Step11: Microbridge patterning to eliminate extrinsic grain boundaries: spin-coat positive resist (e.g., S1813 at 4000 rpm, 45 s), soft bake (100°C, 60 s); expose maskless (DMD or laser writer) with microbridge design: width 50 µm, length 1.5–2.0 mm, with two voltage taps separated by 1.00 ± 0.02 mm centered on the bridge; develop in MF-319 (60–90 s); wet-etch exposed YBCO in 10 wt % H3PO4 at room temperature (calibrate etch rate ~10–30 nm/min; etch until 10–20% over-etch to ensure full clearance); rinse DI, dry; strip resist; inspect by optical microscopy and profilometry; repeat on all wafers to pattern ≥3 bridges per wafer.

Step12: Contact and on-chip heater metallization: define contact pads and heater by lithography; deposit Ti/Au (10/150 nm) or Cr/Au (5/150 nm) by e-beam evaporation or sputtering; pattern heater as a meander (~220 Ω at room temperature) located adjacent (within 50–100 µm) and thermally coupled to the microbridge but electrically isolated (on STO); lift-off; wire-bond or silver-paint leads to current/voltage pads and heater pads; measure contact resistance (<10 mΩ desired) and heater resistance vs T (20–300 K) to calibrate.

Step13: Sample mounting and wiring for PPMS: mount chip on sapphire or oxygen-free copper stage using thin GE varnish or Apiezon N for good thermal contact; use phosphor-bronze or Cu leads with appropriate thermal anchoring; route four-probe lines for transport and two lines for heater; verify electrical isolation and continuity; install on PPMS puck with rotation capability if available; ensure thermometer proximity for accurate local temperature.

Step14: Magnetization-based Jc by SQUID-VSM: measure M(H) loops at 10 K for both film sets with field perpendicular to film plane; use Bean or thin-film models to extract Jc(10 K, B) from ΔM, using film dimensions and thickness; compare with transport Jc; this provides cross-validation and field-sweep data without patterning artifacts.

Step15: Transport Jc(B,θ,T) measurements: in PPMS, at selected temperatures (e.g., 10, 20, 40, 60, 70 K), measure I–V on microbridges under fields 0–8 T; define Jc using E-field criterion 1 µV cm⁻¹; extract n-value from E ∝ (I/Ic)^n fit above Ic; perform angle-dependent measurements at θ = 0° (B ∥ c), 45°, and 90° (B ∥ ab) to quantify correlated pinning; compute Jc by dividing Ic by cross-section (width × thickness); record data for ≥3 bridges per wafer.

Step16: Accommodation field B* extraction: for each T and θ, fit Jc(B) to two regimes (low-field plateau/weak decay and high-field power law Jc ∝ B^−α); compute d[log Jc]/d[log B] and determine B* as the field where slope crosses a threshold (e.g., −0.2); report B*(T,θ) and compare APC-free vs BZO-doped; assess flattening of Jc(B) in doped films.

Step17: Flux dynamics characterization: measure resistivity ρ(T,B) just below Tc to assess TAFF regime; extract activation energy U0 from Arrhenius fits of E–J or ρ(T,B) where applicable; correlate U0 changes with BZO.

Step18: Quench experiment setup and calibration: integrate heater drive (constant-voltage or constant-current pulses) from a low-noise source; set DAQ to record heater current and voltage, bridge current and voltage at ≥100 kS/s; choose default pulse duration 0.7 s and also vary 0.1–1.0 s for sensitivity analysis; calibrate heater power P(t)=I_h(t)²R_h(t) or V_h(t)²/R_h(t) using the measured temperature-dependent heater resistance; establish baseline thermal time constant by applying sub-threshold pulses and monitoring temperature rise via resistance thermometer or using the bridge resistance in the normal state.

Step19: MQE measurement protocol: at each setpoint (T = 20, 40, 60, 70 K; B = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 T; θ = 0° and 90°), bias the microbridge at a fixed transport current fraction (e.g., 0.6, 0.8, 0.9 Ic at that T,B,θ); apply a single heater pulse of duration 0.7 s and adjustable amplitude; record whether a self-sustaining normal zone forms (post-pulse voltage remains above threshold) or the bridge recovers; bracket and converge on the minimum pulse energy that triggers a quench by stepping pulse amplitude using a binary search; compute MQE = ∫ P(t) dt over the pulse (or E ≈ I_h² R_h t for constant parameters); repeat three times for each condition to estimate uncertainty; compare MQE between APC-free and BZO-doped.

Step20: NZPV measurement protocol: with the bridge biased near 0.8–0.95 Ic at target T,B,θ, trigger a quench with a heater pulse slightly above MQE; capture time-resolved voltages from two taps separated by 1.00 mm; define onset when each tap crosses a 10 mV threshold; compute time delay Δt and NZPV = 1.00 mm / Δt; verify linearity by adding a third tap if available; repeat across T=20–70 K and B=0–8 T for θ=0°, 90°; examine current dependence of NZPV.

Step21: Stabilizer variation (optional): repeat MQE/NZPV on a subset of bridges after depositing an additional metal overlayer (e.g., 200–300 nm Au) spanning the bridge to emulate different stabilizer architectures; quantify how metal shunt impacts NZPV/MQE in APC-free vs BZO-doped, informing magnet protection trade-offs.

Step22: Angle-resolved quench behavior: at a fixed T (e.g., 60–70 K) and B (e.g., 4–8 T), rotate the sample to map NZPV and MQE versus angle (0°–90°) to link correlated pinning from BZO nanorods with quench observables; expect maxima/minima linked to pinning anisotropy.

Step23: Magneto-optical imaging (optional): use Faraday-active indicator film on top of the sample at 20–77 K to visualize flux penetration under ramped field and under heater pulses; correlate spatial flux patterns and avalanche propensity with microstructure; compare APC-free vs BZO-doped.

Step24: Data analysis and correlations: compile Jc(B,θ,T), n-values, B*, MQE, and NZPV with uncertainties; analyze correlations between increased B* and changes in MQE/NZPV; normalize MQE by Ic² and NZPV by thermal diffusivity proxies when comparing across samples; evaluate how reduced Jc,0 (if observed) and enhanced in-field Jc relate to quench metrics at high T/B.

Step25: Reproducibility and statistics: for each film type, aggregate results from ≥3 wafers and ≥3 bridges per wafer; use ANOVA or t-tests to assess significance of differences in B*, MQE, NZPV; report mean±std and confidence intervals.

Step26: Controls and systematic checks: verify oxygenation equivalence by Tc and c-axis parameter; check that contact resistance and heater geometry are consistent between samples; ensure identical mounting and thermal boundary conditions; verify that quench detection thresholds (10 mV) do not bias NZPV by repeating with 5 and 20 mV thresholds; perform zero-field quench tests to separate magnetic from purely thermal effects.

Step27: Uncertainty and error budget: include uncertainties from thickness (±5%), width (±2%), heater resistance calibration (±3–5%), temperature setpoint (±0.1 K), field (±0.5–1%), angle (±1–2°), voltage threshold timing jitter (≤10 µs), and DAQ sampling; propagate to Jc, B*, MQE, NZPV.

Step28: Safety and handling: follow laser safety (interlocks, eyewear); handle H3PO4 with PPE and proper waste disposal; observe cryogen and high-field safety; limit transport currents to avoid uncontrolled burn-out; implement interlocks to cut current on sustained normal voltage.

Step29: Timeline and milestones: Weeks 1–2: target verification, substrate preparation, PLD parameter calibration; Weeks 3–4: grow APC-free and BZO-doped films; Week 5: XRD/AFM; Week 6: STEM; Week 7: patterning and metallization; Weeks 8–9: SQUID-VSM and transport Jc(B,θ,T); Weeks 10–11: quench experiments (MQE/NZPV); Week 12: analysis and cross-correlation.

Step30: Deliverables: (i) microstructural confirmation of ~c-axis BZO nanorods in doped films; (ii) Jc(B,θ,T) and B* for APC-free vs BZO-doped; (iii) MQE and NZPV maps vs T, B, θ, current fraction; (iv) correlations linking enhanced correlated pinning to quench metrics; (v) guidelines for stabilizer and detection thresholds to balance stability and detectability in HTS magnet design.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Target preparation  
- Two ceramic targets prepared by solid-state reaction: undoped YBCO and YBCO + 4 wt % BZO.  

Step 2: Film growth  
- Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) on 10 mm × 10 mm SrTiO₃(100) substrates; film thickness ≈ 200 nm.  
- Exact PLD parameters are not listed; authors refer to earlier optimisation work.  

Step 3: Micro-bridge patterning (mask-less photolithography + wet etch)  
- Spin-coat Megaposit SPR 220-4.5 photoresist at 8000 rpm.  
- Expose pattern with Dilase 250 laser writer.  
- Develop in NaOH solution.  
- Etch unprotected YBCO in H₃PO₄ bath.  
- Strip resist in acetone.  
Final bridge: 50 µm wide, 2 mm long; contact pads for current and voltage as drawn in Fig. 1.  

Step 4: Resistor attachment for local heating  
- Glue a 220 Ω resistor (Loctite Stycast 2850FT) on the current pad ≈ 0.7 mm from the bridge; two Al wire-bonds connect it to the PPMS puck.  

Step 5: Electrical contacting  
- 33 µm Al wire-bonds (TPT HB05 bonder) link the sample to the PPMS puck: current leads at the two ends of the bridge, voltage taps in the middle.  

Step 6: Critical-current mapping  
- Measure I–V curves at every (T, B) point with PPMS AC transport option.  
- Define Ic with 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion (bridge length 2 mm → 20 µV threshold).  

Step 7: MQE / quench search  
- Cool to 70 K; set magnetic field.  
- Apply a fixed transport current (expressed as %Ic).  
- Inject 0.7 s heat pulses by stepping the resistor current in 1 mA increments until a quench is detected (voltage jump ≈ 100 × noise).  
- Record the smallest resistor current that triggers a quench; compute MQE ≈ I²Rt with R = 220 Ω and t = 0.7 s.  
- Repeat for other %Ic, then change T or B; always increase absolute current as little as possible to postpone burnout.  

Step 8: NZPV extraction  
- Use voltage traces from the two farthest channels (3 and 4, 1 mm apart).  
- Measure time delay for each signal to cross a 10 mV threshold.  
- NZPV = 1 mm / Δt.  

Step 9: Post-mortem structural check  
- Cs-corrected STEM (JEOL JEM-2200FS, 200 kV, HAADF) on BZO-doped piece to image nanorods (diameter ≈ 6 nm, spacing ≈ 20 nm).  

[Experimental Design Details]
- Temperature range: 20 K – 70 K (PPMS variable-temperature insert).  
- Magnetic field: 0 – 8 T applied perpendicular to film plane (PPMS superconducting magnet).  
- Transport current limit: 1 A (PPMS maximum), corresponding to ≈ 10 MA cm⁻².  
- Heat-pulse duration: fixed at 0.7 s (not varied).  
- Voltage recording: National Instruments PXIe-1073 digitiser, LabVIEW control; four channels sampled simultaneously.  
- Samples eventually failed by burnout: APC-free at 30 K, 8 T, 0.9 Ic; BZO-doped at 30 K, 8 T, 0.5 Ic.

Step17: Mechanical and thermal robustness tests. - Bending strain: measure Ic retention vs applied bending radius (R = 10–150 mm) at 77 K, self-field; aim for ≥95% Ic at design strain. - Thermal cycling: 20 cycles between room temperature and 77 K; measure Ic degradation. - Observe microcracks or delamination via SEM after tests. Step18: Diagnostics and feedback loop for common failure modes. - If BaCO3 detected (Raman, XRD), reduce pCO2 further, increase H2O during pyrolysis, or slightly increase crystallization dwell to promote reaction of residual BaCO3 to Ba–Cu oxides. - If Δϕ > 3° in early layers, reduce per-pass thickness to 0.25–0.30 µm for the first two passes, or increase crystallization temperature by 10–15 °C with shorter dwell. - If BHO agglomeration observed (TEM), decrease dwell time, lower crystallization temperature by 10 °C, and/or reduce BHO loading in initial passes; improve colloid dispersion (fresh sonication, ligand adjustment). - If Ic vs thickness sub-linear, check interlayer interfaces (TEM); add brief intermediate oxygenation (300–350 °C, 15–30 min) between passes to relieve stress and improve continuity. [Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – Substrate preparation  
- Start from commercial IBAD metal tapes (exact buffer stack not specified).  
- Deposit a 100–700 nm CeO₂ cap layer by RF magnetron sputtering to tailor surface texture.

Step 2 – Solution / dispersion preparation  
- Prepare FF-MOD coating solution: Gd, Ba, Cu precursors in fluorine-free solvents; total metal-ion concentration 0.6 mol L⁻¹.  
- Prepare separate BHO nanoparticle dispersion (particle size 1.6–2.2 nm by earlier DLS).  
- Mix the two to obtain precursor inks with 0–3.4 mol % BHO (most long-length work done at 2.7 mol %).

Step 3 – Coating & pyrolysis (repeated)  
- Slot-die coat the ink onto the CeO₂/IBAD tape.  
- Pyrolyse in 100 % O₂ from room temperature to 500 °C.  
- Repeat coating + pyrolysis 1–7 times until total REBCO thickness reaches 0.4–0.5 µm per cycle; final cumulative thickness 0.8–3.1 µm as required.

Step 4 – Crystallisation (reel-to-reel)  
- Heat pyrolysed film first at 700–840 °C in 100 ppm–100 % O₂ (1 atm total pressure) to decompose BaCO₃ and form polycrystalline GdBCO.  
- Cool to room temperature, then re-heat to 800–840 °C (same atmosphere) to obtain c-axis-oriented GdBCO with dispersed BHO.  
- The above two heating steps are collectively called “the crystallisation process” and are performed in a continuous reel-to-reel furnace.

Step 5 – Stabilisation / oxygenation  
- DC-sputter 100–700 nm Ag onto the superconducting film.  
- Oxygenate the tape at 200–500 °C in 100 % O₂.

Step 6 – Patterning for transport tests  
- Self-field Ic: chemically etch 1–2 mm-wide bridges.  
- In-field Ic (18 T): laser-pattern 80–85 µm-wide × 1 mm-long bridges.  
- Angular Ic (8 T): laser-pattern 0.5 mm-wide × 5 mm-long bridges.

Step 7 – Structural / microstructural characterisation  
- Measure in-plane texture (Δϕ) of CeO₂ and GdBCO by X-ray diffraction.  
- Observe surface morphology by SEM.  
- Acquire cross-sectional STEM images and map Hf by EDX to verify BHO dispersion (particles 2–10 nm after heat treatment).

Step 8 – Electrical measurements  
- Self-field Ic at 77 K: DC four-probe, 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion.  
- In-field Ic up to 18 T at 20 K and 77 K: DC four-probe at HFLSM, Tohoku Univ.  
- Angular Ic at 20 K, fields ≤ 8 T: automated rotator (SuperCurrent system, RRI, NZ), 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion.  
- Tc determination: four-probe R(T), define Tc as 90 % of normal-state resistance.  
- Long-length Ic uniformity: THEVA Tapestar mapping at 77.3 K under 80 mT (to avoid current limitation), 12 mm wide strip; values normalised to 4 mm width using a reference coupon measured by DC transport.

[Experimental Design Details]
- All process parameters (temperatures, O₂ partial pressure, number of coats, BHO content) are fixed for a given sample unless the text explicitly states otherwise.  
- Thickness control is achieved simply by counting coating–pyrolysis–crystallisation cycles; no in-situ thickness monitor is mentioned.  
- No details are given on heating/cooling rates, reel speed, or furnace residence time.  
- No information on precursor solvents, exact rare-earth salt types, or pH adjustment.  
- No post-annealing beyond the 200–500 °C oxygenation step is described.

pred_experiment: Experiment: Step1: Define objectives and hypotheses—test whether simultaneous incorporation of (i) self-assembled Ba2Y(Nb/Ta)O6 (BYNTO) nanocolumns and (ii) substrate-surface ZrO2 nanoislands (PAD-derived) that seed dense stacking faults/Y248 intergrowths synergistically enhances flux pinning in 250 nm epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7−x (YBCO) films on (001) SrTiO3 (STO), specifically raising Jc at 4.2–50 K for μ0H ≥ 9–18 T; verify that biaxial texture remains sharp (rocking-curve FWHM ≈0.15°) and that non-scaling of Fp(T,H) emerges from concurrent pinning channels. Step2: Materials and equipment—single-side-polished (001) STO substrates (10×10×0.5 mm); precursors for PAD ZrO2 (zirconyl nitrate or zirconium oxynitrate, polymer chelators like PEI/PAA, NH4OH, DI water); PLD system with KrF (248 nm) laser, substrate heater to 850–900 °C, oxygen delivery to 0.1–1.0 mbar; composite PLD target(s): YBCO with embedded Ba2YNbO6 and Ba2YTaO6 (total 5 at.% nominal; 2.5% each) or dual/segmented targets; AFM, XRD with high-resolution rocking-curve and φ-scan capability, XRR; FIB for TEM lamellae; Cs-corrected HAADF-STEM with EDX/EELS; cleanroom for lithography, ion milling; high-field magnet up to 18 T with 4.2 K cryostat; low-noise current source and nanovoltmeter; oxygen anneal furnace. Step3: Substrate preparation—ultrasonically clean STO in acetone and IPA (10 min each), rinse DI water, dry N2; UV-ozone (20 min) or oxygen plasma (2–5 min) to remove organics; optional high-temperature anneal to form TiO2-terminated terraces (e.g., 950 °C, flowing O2, 2 h), then cool to room temperature; store in clean desiccator. Step4: Synthesize PAD ZrO2 precursor—dissolve zirconyl nitrate in DI water (0.05–0.1 M Zr); add polymer chelator (e.g., PEI 0.1–0.2 wt% or PAA) to bind Zr; adjust pH to ~7–8 with NH4OH to stabilize; age 12–24 h; filter (0.2 μm); dilute to achieve sub-monolayer coverage upon coating; prepare a series of concentrations for coverage calibration. Step5: Deposit ZrO2 nanoislands on STO—spin coat at 2000–4000 rpm for 30–60 s under cleanroom conditions to target ~20% surface coverage and areal density ~375 μm−2; soft-bake 150 °C, 10 min; pyrolyze 350–400 °C in air (30–60 min) to remove organics; crystallize/induce dewetting into islands by annealing 750–800 °C in O2 (0.2–1 bar) for 30–60 min; cool at 5 °C/min to room temperature; tune spin speed and solution concentration to reach target island diameter (~45 nm) and height (~25 nm). Step6: Verify nanoisland template—AFM tapping mode over multiple 5×5 μm2 areas; extract height, diameter, areal density, and coverage statistics; adjust PAD parameters (solution concentration, spin speed, anneal) to converge on 20±3% coverage and 300–450 μm−2 density; optional XPS or GIXRD to confirm ZrO2 phase; retain several substrates with and without islands for controls. Step7: Fabricate composite PLD target—Option A: Mosaic composite—embed Ba2YNbO6 and Ba2YTaO6 ceramic chips into a stoichiometric YBCO target face to achieve 2.5 at.% each by area fraction and expected ablation yield; Option B: Co-sintered composite—mix YBCO powder with 5 at.% total BYNTO (2.5% each), press and sinter under controlled oxygen; polish target surface; validate target composition by EDX/ICP-OES; prepare pure YBCO target for controls; ensure density and mechanical integrity to avoid particulates. Step8: PLD growth conditions calibration—using a sacrificial STO, set substrate temperature Ts=840 °C (thermocouple-calibrated to surface), oxygen partial pressure pO2=200–300 mTorr; laser fluence 1.5–2.0 J/cm2, repetition rate 5–10 Hz; measure growth rate via in-situ RHEED oscillations (if available) or ex-situ thickness by XRR and AFM step edge after masking; adjust to 1.8 nm/s; confirm that pure YBCO grown under these conditions yields c-axis texture and Tc≈89–92 K after oxygenation. Step9: Deposit YBCO-BYNTO films—mount ZrO2-island-decorated STO on heater; degas at 500 °C, 10 min, 100 mTorr O2; ramp to 840 °C in 200–300 mTorr O2; optional 1–2 min pre-ablation of target to stabilize flux; deposit 250±10 nm YBCO-BYNTO at 1.8 nm/s; no intentional buffer layer so that initial interfacial reaction with ZrO2 can form a thin BaZrO3 interlayer from Ba in arriving flux; maintain plume-substrate distance and rotation for uniformity; after deposition, dwell 5 min at Ts in same pO2 to promote cation ordering; ramp down to 500 °C in 300 mTorr O2 at 10 °C/min. Step10: Post-deposition oxygenation—at 500 °C, increase pO2 to 1 bar O2, hold 30–60 min to oxygenate YBCO toward x≈0.05–0.1; cool to room temperature at 5 °C/min in O2; measure room-T resistivity to check for metallic behavior; store dry. Step11: Control films—prepare on the same day and under identical conditions: (i) YBCO-BYNTO on bare STO (no islands), (ii) pure YBCO on ZrO2-island STO (no BYNTO), (iii) pure YBCO on bare STO; aim for the same 250 nm thickness; these provide baseline and single-pinning-type references. Step12: Structural characterization (XRD)—θ–2θ scans to confirm c-axis oriented YBCO (00l) peaks and absence of secondary phases at detectable levels; rocking curves (ω) for YBCO (005) or (007) to quantify out-of-plane FWHM and check retention of ~0.15°; φ-scans of YBCO (103)/(113) and STO to confirm cube-on-cube epitaxy and in-plane alignment; reciprocal space maps around (103)/(109) to probe strain state and mosaicity; XRR to verify thickness. Step13: Surface morphology (AFM)—scan 2×2 and 5×5 μm2 after film growth to assess particulates and surface roughness (target RMS <3–5 nm); compare to pre-deposition island maps to confirm overgrowth; note any signatures of through-film columnar features. Step14: Cross-sectional TEM/STEM—prepare FIB lamellae both parallel and perpendicular to substrate steps; perform HAADF-STEM to image (i) c-axis aligned BYNTO nanocolumns (quantify diameter distribution 5–16 nm, spacing, meandering/tilt statistics), (ii) high-density stacking faults parallel to ab planes and Y248 intergrowths (count density per μm2 over multiple fields of view to target ~2×10^4 μm−2), (iii) interfacial BaZrO3 layer atop ZrO2 islands and misfit dislocations; use FFTs and geometric phase analysis to extract local strain; perform EDX/EELS maps for Ba, Y, Cu, O, Nb, Ta, Zr to assign phases (BYNTO columns enriched in Nb/Ta; interfacial Zr-rich regions with Ba indicative of BZO); check that nanocolumns are not nucleating preferentially at the interface (desired to avoid extra interfacial rods). Step15: Electrical patterning—photolithographically define 20–50 μm wide, 200–500 μm long bridges (multiple per sample across the wafer); deposit Au contact pads (e.g., 100 nm by sputtering) and lift-off; gently ion mill to isolate bridges if needed; attach 25 μm Au wires with silver epoxy; cure at 120 °C in O2; measure contact resistance (<1 Ω). Step16: Transport measurements—four-probe E–I curves at T=4.2, 20, 30, 40, 50, 65, 77 K in fields μ0H=0–18 T; define Jc at 1 μV/cm criterion; measure for H∥c, H∥ab, and full angular dependence (0–180°, 2–5° steps) at representative fields (5, 9, 12, 15, 18 T); use current ramp rates low enough to avoid heating (e.g., 50–200 A/s equivalent for microbridges), reverse sweep to check hysteresis; correct for sample dimensions (thickness from XRR/TEM) and subtract series voltage offsets. Step17: Pinning analysis—compute Fp=μ0 Jc H; plot normalized Fp(h) vs reduced field h at multiple T to test for absence of universal scaling; identify multiple pinning contributions by fitting with superposition models (e.g., core pinning by columns plus planar pinning by stacking faults); extract Hirr(T) from J–E criteria or from magnetization loops (optional VSM on unpatterned pieces) using standard Kramer extrapolation; quantify c-axis and ab-plane pinning peaks in angular Jc(θ) and their temperature/field evolution. Step18: Compare to controls—determine Jc enhancement factor at 4.2 K, 18 T relative to nanocolumn-only film; target ≈2.4×; compare Hirr at 20–50 K; verify that combined-pin film shows higher Jc above 9 T than either single-pin architecture; ensure texture (FWHM) is maintained at ≈0.15° in the combined film but may degrade if parameters drift—if so, re-optimize PLD conditions. Step19: Optimization matrix—systematically vary (a) BYNTO content (1–6 at.% total, keeping Nb:Ta=1:1) to tune column diameter/density and meandering; (b) growth rate (1.0–2.5 nm/s) and Ts (820–860 °C) to adjust column morphology; (c) ZrO2 island areal density (100–600 μm−2) and size (30–70 nm diameter) by PAD parameters; for each variant, repeat Steps12–17 to map Jc(μ0H,T,θ), Fp behavior, and microstructure; select optimum that maximizes Jc at 4.2–50 K and μ0H≥12 T while retaining FWHM ≤0.2°. Step20: Mechanism verification—correlate stacking fault/Y248 density from STEM with ab-plane Jc peak amplitude and low-T high-field Jc; correlate nanocolumn metrics with c-axis peak and intermediate-field performance; verify presence and continuity of thin BaZrO3 interlayer at ZrO2 island tops and associated misfit dislocations; use local strain mapping to link island-induced strain fields to fault nucleation; ensure Nb/Ta stays confined to columns (no extensive secondary phases). Step21: Reliability and statistics—fabricate ≥3 nominally identical samples for each condition; report means and standard deviations for Jc at key points (e.g., 4.2 K, 18 T; 20 K, 12 T; 77 K, 1–3 T); perform thermal cycling (300↔4.2 K, 10 cycles) and remeasure to check stability; assess aging over 30 days in dry air. Step22: Risk mitigation—if unintended BZO nanorods nucleate vertically at the interface (detrimental to design), lower pO2 during initial 5–10 nm growth (e.g., 150–200 mTorr) or reduce laser fluence to limit Ba surface mobility, then ramp to nominal pO2; if texture degrades (FWHM>0.2°), reduce island coverage or adjust Ts downward by 10–20 °C; if Tc is suppressed (oxygen deficiency), extend 500 °C O2 anneal or perform a two-step oxygenation (450 °C then 350 °C); minimize particulates by frequent target resurfacing and off-axis plume alignment tuning. Step23: Success criteria—(i) out-of-plane rocking curve FWHM ≈0.15°±0.03°, (ii) STEM-confirmed BYNTO nanocolumns (5–16 nm) plus dense ab-plane stacking faults/Y248 intergrowths (~2×10^4 μm−2), (iii) Jc(4.2 K, 18 T) ≥2.4× that of nanocolumn-only control, (iv) non-scaling Fp(h) across temperatures indicative of multiple pinning channels, (v) Hirr(T) >9 T for T<50 K with enhanced angular performance. Step24: Documentation—record all deposition parameters (Ts, pO2, fluence, rep-rate, target composition, growth rate), PAD recipe details (precursor concentrations, spin speeds, anneals), and all characterization raw data; maintain a sample log linking microstructure to transport metrics to guide scale-up and translation to coated conductors on technical substrates.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Substrate-decoration template preparation  
- Use polymer-assisted deposition (PAD, water-based metal-organic solution) to synthesise ZrO₂ nanoparticles  
- Deposit the solution onto (001) SrTiO₃ single-crystal substrates; anneal to obtain discrete ZrO₂ nano-islands  
- Store the decorated substrates for subsequent PLD growth  

Step 2: PLD target preparation  
- Fabricate a mixed ceramic ablation target containing YBCO plus 2.5 at % Ba₂YTaO₆ and 2.5 at % Ba₂YNbO₆ (total 5 at % BYNTO); detailed target manufacturing given in ref [38] of the paper  

Step 3: Film deposition  
- Mount either decorated (film A) or bare (film B) SrTiO₃ substrate on the PLD heater  
- Deposit YBCO-BYNTO layer by KrF excimer PLD: λ = 248 nm, 10 Hz, fluence ≈ 2 J cm⁻², substrate temperature 840 °C, growth rate ≈ 1.8 nm s⁻¹, final thickness ≈ 250 nm (measured 230 nm in micrographs)  
- Cool the sample; no post-annealing conditions are specified  

Step 4: Sample patterning for transport measurements  
- Cut 1 mm-long, 30–50 µm-wide bridges by standard photolithography and etching  

Step 5: Structural / morphological characterisation  
- AFM: image the decorated substrate before deposition to obtain nano-island diameter, height and density  
- X-ray diffraction: record ω-rocking curves of the (005) YBCO reflection with a 9 kW rotating-anode diffractometer in parallel-beam geometry  
- (S)TEM: prepare cross-sectional lamellae; acquire HAADF images and EDX maps to visualise nano-islands, nanocolumns, stacking faults, interface reactions  

Step 6: Electrical transport measurement  
- Load patterned bridges into a cryostat equipped with a superconducting magnet (maximum 18 T)  
- Apply magnetic field H || c-axis of YBCO (maximum Lorentz-force configuration)  
- Record current–voltage curves from 77 K down to 4.2 K in field steps; define Ic with 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion  
- Compute Jc = Ic / cross-section and Fp = Jc µ₀H  

Step 7: Data analysis  
- Build Jc(H) curves at fixed temperatures  
- Evaluate irreversibility field µ₀Hirr from Fp(µ₀Hirr) = Fp_max/100  
- Construct normalised pinning-force curves f_p(h) = Fp(H)/Fp_max versus reduced field h = H/H_max (or H/Hirr) to test temperature scaling  
- Compare film A vs film B to isolate the effect of ZrO₂ nano-islands  

[Experimental Design Details]
Materials  
- Substrates: (001) SrTiO₃ single crystals, used as-received or after PAD decoration  
- Precursor solution for PAD: water-based metal-organic Zr salt plus polymer (exact chemistry not repeated here)  
- PLD target: YBCO + 2.5 at % Ba₂YTaO₆ + 2.5 at % Ba₂YNbO₆, mixed ceramic  

Key process parameters explicitly stated  
- PAD annealing: not detailed in this paper (referred to earlier works)  
- PLD: KrF 248 nm, 10 Hz, fluence ≈ 2 J cm⁻², T_sub = 840 °C, growth rate ≈ 1.8 nm s⁻¹, thickness ≈ 250 nm  

Structural metrics reported  
- Nano-island mean diameter 25 ± 9 nm, mean height 4.3 ± 0.9 nm, density ≈ 375 µm⁻², surface coverage ≈ 20 % (AFM, before deposition)  
- After growth some islands appear larger (~45–50 nm dia., ~25 nm height) due to BYNTO overgrowth  
- Stacking-fault density ~ 2 × 10⁴ µm⁻² (TEM, film A)  
- FWHM of (005) YBCO rocking curve 0.15° (film A) vs 0.24° (film B)  

Transport metrics  
- T_c: 83.7 K (film A) vs 87.2 K (film B)  
- Jc(0, 77 K): 1.0 MA cm⁻² (film A) vs 2.1 MA cm⁻² (film B)  
- µ₀Hirr(77 K): 4.6 T (film A) vs 5.1 T (film B)  
- Jc and Fp measured in 0–18 T, 4.2–77 K; full data tables and figures provided

Experiment: Step1: Define specifications and acceptance criteria.
- Tape architecture: REBCO on IBAD-MgO/LaMnO3 (LMO) buffered Hastelloy C-276, 4–12 mm wide, 50–100 μm substrate thickness, with Ag cap for solderability.
- Superconductor layers: YBa2Cu3O7-δ (YBCO) and EuBa2Cu3O7-δ (EuBCO) on identical buffer stacks; EuBCO layer contains 3.5 mol% BaHfO3 (BHO) artificial pinning centers (APCs).
- In-plane texture target: Δφ (LMO 200 φ-scan) = 6–7°; out-of-plane rocking curve FWHM (REBCO 005) ≤ 2°.
- Layer thickness: REBCO 0.9–1.1 μm; Ag cap 1–2 μm.
- Solder interface: Sn63Pb37, 2–4 μm thickness; specific contact resistivity ρc ≤ 5 nΩ·cm² (goal ~2 nΩ·cm²).
- Electrical criterion: Ic defined at E = 1 μV/cm; n-value extracted from E = Ec(I/Ic)^n near Ec.
- Measurement condition: 65 K, 1.5 T; field angle θ swept from −40° to 220° (θ = 0° corresponds to B∥c, θ = 90° to B∥ab).
- Statistical rigor: ≥3 tapes per condition (YBCO, EuBCO+BHO, FFDS), ≥2 coupons per tape for transport, to assess reproducibility.
- Success metrics: Ic,FFDS(θ) ≈ Ic,YBCO(θ) + Ic,EuBCO+BHO(θ) within ±5%; reduction of angular anisotropy σ(Ic)/⟨Ic⟩ to ≤0.08 at 65 K, 1.5 T; minimum Ic improved by ≥30% over the higher of the two single-tape minima.

Step2: Prepare substrates and targets.
- Substrates: Procure IBAD-MgO/LMO buffered Hastelloy C-276 tapes with LMO cap layer compatible with REBCO epitaxy; verify delivered Δφ via XRD (LMO 200 φ-scan). Select coils with Δφ within 6–7°.
- PLD targets: Fabricate or procure dense ceramic targets for YBCO and EuBCO. For EuBCO+BHO, use a composite target with 3.5 mol% BaHfO3 or co-ablation (synchronized ablation of EuBCO and BHO targets) calibrated to 3.5 mol% in film.
- Characterize targets: Density >95% theoretical; phase purity by XRD; Hf-containing target surface conditioned by pre-ablation to steady-state plume.

Step3: Set up reel-to-reel PLD (R2R-PLD).
- Typical parameters (to be refined by short coupons): substrate (web) temperature 770–790 °C at growth surface (pyrometer-calibrated); oxygen partial pressure 200–300 mTorr; laser wavelength 248 nm (KrF) or 355 nm; fluence 1.5–2.0 J/cm²; repetition rate 5–10 Hz; target–substrate distance 5–6 cm; web speed tuned to yield ~1 μm thickness per pass.
- Install in-line optical monitoring (reflectivity) to track thickness and growth mode; maintain oxygen purity and flow stability; ensure uniform heating across tape width.

Step4: Deposit YBCO layer on IBAD-MgO/LMO.
- Run a process window study on 20–30 cm coupons to set web speed/laser rate for 0.95 ± 0.1 μm thickness with c-axis oriented growth and high in-plane texture transfer.
- Produce 10–20 m lengths under fixed conditions; segment 0.5–1 m spools for downstream processing.
- Post-deposition oxygenation: cool to 450–500 °C in 1 atm O2 (or 0.8–1 bar flowing O2), hold 30–60 min, then cool at 5–10 °C/min to room temperature to set δ close to 0 for maximal Tc.
- Deposit Ag cap: DC sputter or thermal evaporation 1–2 μm at ≤200 °C; surface roughness (Rq) ≤5 nm.

Step5: Deposit EuBCO+BHO layer on IBAD-MgO/LMO.
- Use similar thermal/oxygen conditions as YBCO, with potential minor adjustment in pO2 (e.g., 250–350 mTorr) to promote BHO nanorod formation.
- Maintain film thickness ~1.0 μm. Target the self-assembly of BHO nanorods aligned along c-axis; avoid excessive nanorod diameter (>8 nm) or splay that degrades ab-plane Jc.
- Post-oxygenation identical to YBCO; Ag cap deposition identical to Step4.

Step6: Microstructure and texture characterization.
- XRD texture: measure LMO (200) φ-scan for Δφ; REBCO (103) φ-scan and (005) rocking curve to ensure epitaxy (Δφ ≤ 7°, FWHM(005) ≤ 2°).
- θ–2θ scans: confirm c-axis orientation and absence of secondary phases beyond designed BHO.
- AFM on Ag-free witness samples (if available) or on Ag-etched windows to assess surface roughness (Rq ≤ 2–5 nm) for solder uniformity.
- Cross-sectional TEM/STEM on coupons (FIB-prepared) of EuBCO+BHO to quantify BHO nanorod density (~1–3×10¹¹ cm⁻²), diameter (3–6 nm), alignment (tilt distribution), and continuity; check for nanorod-induced defects at grain boundaries.
- Film thickness via profilometry or X-ray reflectivity.

Step7: Electrical characterization of single tapes (pre-lamination).
- Prepare 6–10 cm coupons with four-probe contacts (soldered or spot-welded to Ag cap) and voltage taps spaced 4–5 cm; measure at 65 K, 1.5 T in a rotatable probe.
- Angle calibration: define θ = 0° at B∥c by maximizing the c-axis correlated peak on EuBCO+BHO and minimizing on YBCO; verify B∥ab at θ = 90° from intrinsic peak.
- Sweep I at 0.1–1 A/s ramps while monitoring voltage; maintain temperature stability ±0.1 K; measure I–V curves at θ from −40° to 220° in 5–10° steps.
- Extract Ic(θ) at Ec = 1 μV/cm and n(θ). Record Joule heating onset and ensure no damage (repeatability of Ic within ±2% on re-measurement).
- Additionally measure 77 K self-field Ic for benchmarking and 4.2 K, 1–5 T on select coupons (optional for field scaling).

Step8: Surface preparation for solder lamination.
- Clean Ag surfaces: solvent rinse (IPA), low-power Ar plasma (≤30 W, 30–60 s) to remove organics/oxides; avoid REBCO exposure.
- Apply ultrathin Sn63Pb37 layer by:
  a) Solder foil of 2–4 μm (if available), or
  b) Electroplating 2–4 μm SnPb on one Ag surface (control composition), or
  c) Sputter Sn/Pb bilayers followed by reflow to form eutectic.
- Use mildly activated, no-clean flux compatible with Ag (minimal residues); test wetting on dummy Ag coupons.
- Verify solder thickness uniformity ±0.5 μm by cross-sectional microscopy on test laminates.

Step9: Reel-to-reel face-to-face double stacking (FFDS) lamination.
- Align YBCO tape and EuBCO+BHO tape with Ag sides facing each other (REBCO layers facing inwards through Ag).
- Lamination parameters: hot zone at 200 ± 5 °C; line pressure 0.2–0.5 MPa; dwell (thermal soak) 15–45 s depending on line speed to fully wet interfaces; inert N2 atmosphere (O2 < 1000 ppm) to limit Ag oxidation; maintain tension to prevent wrinkling.
- Control solder flow to avoid edge squeeze-out and shorts; edge-dam if necessary.
- Cool under pressure to prevent voids; clean external flux residues. Inspect with X-ray or ultrasonic C-scan for voids/delaminations; cross-section a few locations for bond line thickness.

Step10: Specific contact resistivity (ρc) and bond integrity measurement.
- Prepare 2–5 cm overlap coupons with four-terminal transverse measurement: inject current from top tape at one end to bottom tape at the other; measure V across the interface using separate voltage taps to avoid lead resistance.
- Apply transfer length method (TLM): fabricate multiple overlap lengths (e.g., 5, 10, 20 mm); plot R vs 1/A (A = overlap area) to extract ρc and verify linearity; target ρc ≤ 5 nΩ·cm².
- Map along tape length: perform TLM at ≥5 positions per meter on 3 m segments to assess uniformity; acceptance: ≤20% variation.
- Mechanical testing: lap shear and 90° peel on bonded coupons; acceptance: shear >10 MPa; peel >1 N/mm (adjust per tape thickness).

Step11: Electrical characterization of FFDS stacks.
- Configure leads: join the ends of both tapes electrically in parallel for total Ic tests; additionally, instrument separate voltage taps to each tape (installed before lamination and brought out at ends) to monitor individual voltages during current ramps.
- Measure at 65 K, 1.5 T with the same angular protocol as Step7. For each θ:
  a) Record global I–V of the stack; determine Ic,FFDS(θ) at 1 μV/cm.
  b) Record individual tape voltages to infer current sharing and identify the first-quenched tape.
  c) Confirm reversible behavior with two successive ramps (no degradation).
- Compute Ic summation: compare Ic,FFDS(θ) to Ic,YBCO(θ) + Ic,EuBCO+BHO(θ); acceptance: within ±5%. Compute σ(Ic)/⟨Ic⟩ across angles and compare to single tapes.

Step12: Equivalent-circuit/current-transfer modeling to extract interface resistance.
- Build a distributed transmission-line model: two superconducting branches (YBCO, EuBCO+BHO) with power-law E–J (Ec and n from Step7) coupled via a uniform contact resistivity ρc (per unit area) along the length; include metallic stabilizer resistances.
- Fit parameters: ρc and, if needed, an effective percolation-transition Rs(I) to capture the nonlinearity near Ic for each tape. Fit to the measured FFDS I–V curves and the spatial voltage distribution (if instrumented) across several angles and currents.
- Validate ρc: compare fitted ρc with TLM results from Step10; acceptance: agreement within a factor ≤2. Extract current transfer length (CTL) and ensure CTL << sample length (e.g., CTL < 1 cm) for efficient sharing.

Step13: Microstructural correlation with performance.
- Correlate BHO nanorod metrics (density, alignment) with c-axis Jc enhancement at θ ≈ 0° and with the angular width of the c-axis peak; ensure EuBCO+BHO complements YBCO’s ab-plane strength.
- Confirm that texture (Δφ) and grain boundary metrics remain within targets post-lamination (re-check XRD on delaminated witnesses or on exposed windows if possible).

Step14: Reliability testing of FFDS.
- Thermal cycling: 20–300 K for 10 cycles; repeat Ic,FFDS(θ) at 65 K, 1.5 T; acceptance: ≤5% change in Ic and ≤20% change in ρc.
- Bending strain: wind to radii 25 mm and 50 mm; measure Ic,FFDS(θ) post-bend; acceptance: ≤5% degradation at both radii.
- Lorentz-force endurance: hold at 65 K, 1.5 T, θ = 0°, 45°, 90° at 0.9 Ic for 30 min; monitor voltage stability and hot-spot formation; ensure no drift.

Step15: Optimization loop if targets are not met.
- If c-axis enhancement insufficient: adjust BHO content (2.5–5 mol%) or nanorod morphology via pO2, substrate temperature, or laser fluence; re-deposit EuBCO+BHO and re-test.
- If ab-plane Ic degrades: refine texture (reduce Δφ by adjusting IBAD-MgO process selection or LMO cap thickness/smoothness); adjust REBCO thickness to balance pinning and strain.
- If ρc too high or nonuniform: refine surface prep (longer plasma clean), flux chemistry, solder thickness control, lamination pressure/temperature; consider thin interlayers (e.g., Au flash on Ag) to improve wetting.
- Iterate Steps6–12 until performance targets are achieved.

Step16: Data analysis and reporting.
- Compile Ic(θ) and n(θ) for YBCO, EuBCO+BHO, and FFDS; calculate σ(Ic)/⟨Ic⟩ and minimum Ic improvements; plot Ic,FFDS(θ) versus the sum of singles.
- Document process parameters, microstructural images (TEM, XRD), ρc values (TLM and model), and reliability test outcomes.
- Provide a process window and guidelines for scaling to longer lengths (tens to hundreds of meters), including inline QC checkpoints (texture, thickness, solder bond inspection).

Step17: Safety and compliance.
- Laser safety for PLD: interlocks, eyewear, beam enclosures.
- High-temperature and oxygen handling: use compatible materials; monitor O2 levels.
- Lead-containing solder: fume extraction, gloves, waste disposal per institutional and regulatory guidelines; avoid lead exposure.
- Cryogen and magnet safety: training for 65 K operation (cryocooler or LN2 with heater), quench protocols, and rotator motion interlocks.

Step18: Optional extensions for magnet-relevant validation.
- Field scaling: repeat angular Ic at 4.2 K and 20–30 K up to 5–12 T, if available, to assess robustness across operating regimes.
- Long-length demonstration: laminate 10–20 m and perform moving-tap Ic mapping and periodic TLM to assess uniformity; target ≤10% variation in Ic and ρc along length.
- Coil segment test: wind a small racetrack or pancake with FFDS tape; measure turn-to-turn voltage and Ic anisotropy under field to emulate magnet conditions.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Fabricate two 4 mm-wide precursor tapes  
 – YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋δ (YBCO) CC without artificial pinning centres (APCs)  
 – EuBa₂Cu₃O₇₋δ (EuBCO) CC doped with 3.5 mol % BaHfO₃ (BHO) as APCs  

Step 2: Deposit superconducting layers by pulsed-laser deposition (PLD)  
 – Substrate stack: LaMnO₃ (LMO) / IBAD-MgO / Y₂O₃ / Al₂O₃ / Hastelloy C-276  
 – In-plane texture of LMO: Δφ ≈ 6–7° (FWHM from X-ray φ-scan of LMO 200 peak)  

Step 3: Produce ~10 m long tapes of each type; slit to 4 mm width  

Step 4: Assemble FFDS conductor by reel-to-reel soldering  
 – Stack YBCO and EuBCO-BHO tapes face-to-face (superconducting sides inward)  
 – Solder alloy: Sn₆₃Pb₃₇ (T_flow = 183 °C)  
 – Bath temperature: ≈ 200 °C → final solder thickness 2–4 µm  

Step 5: Cut 60 mm long samples from the ends of each single tape and from the FFDS conductor for electrical testing  

Step 6: Mount samples in a rotatable cryostat probe  
 – Attach voltage taps on the top (EuBCO-BHO) side with 10 mm separation  
 – Apply current through the same top surface (four-probe arrangement, Fig. 3)  

Step 7: Perform I–V measurements  
 – Magnetic field: 1.5 T, temperature: 65 K  
 – Field angle θ swept from −40° to 220° in the plane perpendicular to the tape width  
 – Record I–V curves at θ = 0° (B || c-axis), 45°, 90° (B || a-b plane) and intermediate angles  

Step 8: Analyse data  
 – Extract critical current Ic (1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion) at each angle  
 – Fit FFDS I–V curves with an equivalent-circuit model: two nonlinear superconducting resistances R_sc(YBCO), R_sc(EuBCO) connected through a constant joint resistance R_c (fitted value 2 nΩ)  
 – Compare experimental Ic(θ) with the arithmetic sum Ic,YBCO(θ) + Ic,EuBCO(θ)  
 – Quantify anisotropy by standard deviation of Ic(θ) normalized to average Ic  

[Experimental Design Details]
- Sample geometry: 4 mm wide, 60 mm gauge length  
- Solder joint resistivity: ≈ 50 nΩ cm² at 77 K (cited from authors’ earlier work); fitted R_c = 2 nΩ for present 65 K data  
- Field & temperature fixed at 1.5 T, 65 K; angle is the only variable during I–V acquisition  
- Voltage criterion for Ic: 1 µV cm⁻¹ (not explicitly stated in the paper but standard in the field and consistent with figure axis)

Experiment: Step1: Define sample matrix and controls:
- Prepare three buffer categories on MgO(100): (A) pure STO (100 and 150 nm), (B) STO+CeO2 nanocomposite (NC) with CeO2 volume fractions 5, 10, 15, 20% at two thicknesses (100 and 150 nm), and (C) no buffer (bare MgO) to serve as a baseline for interface effects.
- For each buffer condition, deposit YBCO (target thickness 300–360 nm) at four laser repetition rates: 10, 20, 50, and 100 Hz. Maintain all other YBCO growth parameters constant.
- Include two external controls: YBCO on single-crystal STO(100) and YBCO with 5 vol% BaHfO3 nanorods on STO(100) (same YBCO thickness and growth conditions), to benchmark against conventional artificial pinning strategies.

Step2: Substrate preparation (MgO(100) single crystals):
- Cut to 5 × 5 mm (or compatible with PPMS puck), solvent clean (acetone, isopropanol), UV-ozone 15 min, then mount on PLD heater.
- Pre-anneal in PLD chamber at 950 °C in 100 mTorr O2 for 30 min to smooth surface; cool to buffer deposition temperature. Verify surface by tapping-mode AFM on a witness substrate to ensure rms roughness ≤ 0.5 nm.

Step3: Buffer layer deposition by PLD:
- Pure STO buffer: 880 °C, 400 mTorr O2, KrF laser (248 nm), fluence 1.5–2.0 J/cm², repetition 10 Hz. Target-substrate distance 5 cm. Grow 100 or 150 nm. Optional in-situ RHEED (if available) to monitor layer-by-layer evolution.
- STO+CeO2 NC buffer: Co-deposit STO and CeO2 using two synchronized PLD guns (or alternate target switching at sub-monolayer periods ~1–3 s) to achieve vertical self-assembly. Maintain 880 °C and 400 mTorr O2, 10 Hz per target (effective combined flux adjusted for desired CeO2 vol%). Calibrate volume fraction by XRD peak intensities and cross-sectional STEM on first trial set; then lock flux ratios.
- After growth, cool to 600 °C at 10 °C/min in 400 mTorr O2, then to room temperature in 500 Torr O2 to stabilize buffer oxygen stoichiometry.

Step4: Buffer characterization and gatekeeping:
- XRD 2θ/ω scans to confirm perovskite phase, out-of-plane c-axis texture; φ-scans of STO {103} and CeO2 {220} to verify cube-on-cube epitaxy and Δφ < 3° for STO. Rocking curves (ω) to quantify mosaic spread (FWHM target ≤ 1°).
- Reciprocal space maps (RSM) around asymmetric reflections (e.g., STO 103, CeO2 331) to assess lattice parameters and strain state.
- AFM on buffer surfaces to ensure rms roughness ≤ 1 nm and absence of large particulates.
- Cross-sectional STEM-HAADF and EDX on one sample per NC condition to verify vertical CeO2 nanorods (tens of nm diameter, 10–20 nm spacing) confined within buffer and to observe misfit dislocation networks at MgO/NC and NC surface. Proceed to YBCO deposition only for buffer conditions meeting epitaxy and smoothness criteria.

Step5: YBCO deposition by PLD:
- Substrate temperature 805–815 °C (optimize within this window on first trial set for highest Tc without Ce interdiffusion), O2 pressure 200–300 mTorr, laser fluence 1.5–2.0 J/cm², target-substrate distance 5 cm.
- Laser repetition rate as variable: 10, 20, 50, 100 Hz; keep total thickness 300–360 nm by time control (calibrate deposition rate via X-ray reflectivity on calibration films).
- Apply a 5–10 min dwell after the first 10–20 nm to promote interface equilibration at low repetition rate (10–20 Hz) for the runs intended to maximize straight threading dislocations.
- After deposition, ramp down to 500–520 °C in 300 Torr O2 at 10 °C/min, hold 1 h in 1 atm O2 (or flowing O2 at ≥ 0.5 l/min) for oxygenation, then cool to room temperature at 5 °C/min. For high-frequency (100 Hz) samples, extend oxygenation hold to 2 h to compensate for any increased disorder.

Step6: Prevent and assess interdiffusion:
- Include a thin (5–10 nm) STO cap atop NC buffer before YBCO for a subset to act as a diffusion barrier; compare to uncapped NC buffers.
- Perform ToF-SIMS depth profiling and STEM-EELS line scans across the buffer/YBCO interface on representative samples to verify Ce remains below detection within YBCO. Reject any growth parameter set that shows detectable Ce in YBCO.

Step7: Structural characterization of YBCO films:
- XRD 2θ/ω to confirm c-axis oriented YBCO (00l peaks), extract c-axis lattice parameter; ω rocking curve of YBCO 005 (target FWHM ≤ 1°). φ-scans of YBCO {103} to confirm cube-on-cube texture and Δφ comparable to buffer.
- RSM around YBCO (103)/(109) to assess in-plane strain and potential lattice parameter shifts indicative of elastic strain transfer; perform sin²ψ scans to evaluate residual strain.
- AFM to assess surface morphology and step-flow features; record rms roughness.
- Plan-view TEM (FIB-prepared thin lamella) and/or weak-beam dark-field imaging to quantify threading dislocation density and types (use g·b analysis to identify c-axis [001] threading dislocations). Compute linear density (μm⁻¹) and spacing statistics across multiple fields of view.
- Cross-sectional STEM-HAADF to visualize dislocation trajectories from buffer into YBCO; quantify straightness via tortuosity (path length/film thickness) and angular deviation distribution for each laser frequency. Apply geometric phase analysis (GPA) to map nanoscale strain in YBCO above NC vs pure STO buffers.

Step8: Patterning for transport:
- Deposit Au (50–100 nm) contact pads by sputtering or e-beam evaporation through a shadow mask immediately after a gentle Ar-ion clean to ensure low contact resistance.
- Photolithography and Ar-ion milling to define 50–100 μm-wide, 0.5–1.0 mm-long four-probe microbridges aligned along a well-defined in-plane direction; leave multiple bridges per sample to assess uniformity.
- Wire bond using Al wires; verify contact resistance < 0.5 Ω per pad at room temperature.

Step9: Electrical measurements (PPMS/VSM):
- Measure resistivity vs temperature (ρ–T) from 300 K to 10 K at zero field to obtain Tc onset and Tc,0 (zero resistance). Target Tc ≥ 89 K; if below, adjust oxygenation protocol.
- Four-probe I–V at 77 K self-field to determine Jc with 1 μV/cm criterion; repeat at 65, 40, and 20 K.
- Field dependence: at 20, 40, 65, and 77 K, measure Jc(H) from 0 to 9 T for two principal orientations (B∥c and B∥ab). Compute flux-pinning force density Fp = μ0 H Jc(H).
- Angular dependence: at fixed fields (e.g., 3, 5, 7, 9 T) and temperatures (20, 40, 65 K), measure Jc(θ) with θ from −10° to 190° relative to c-axis in 2–5° steps. Extract c-axis correlated peak height and full width at half maximum (FWHM), and the ab-plane peak parameters.
- Determine irreversibility field Hirr(T) using a fixed electric field criterion (e.g., 1 μV/cm) from I–V curves for both orientations; construct Kramer plots to assess pinning regimes.
- Optional: VSM magnetization loops at 20–77 K up to 9 T to extract Jc via Bean model for cross-validation.

Step10: Data analysis and pinning model evaluation:
- Compare Fp,max and Jc(H) across buffer types and laser frequencies. Use Dew-Hughes scaling to plot reduced pinning force f(h) versus reduced field h = H/Hirr and identify dominant pinning types. Evaluate how straightness (tortuosity) and density of threading dislocations correlate with c-axis peak strength in Jc(θ).
- Apply anisotropic scaling (Blatter scaling) to collapse Jc(θ) where appropriate and quantify deviations due to correlated pinning. Extract anisotropy parameter γ from scaling and check consistency with known YBCO values.
- Quantify strain-pinning contribution by correlating GPA strain amplitudes with enhancements in Jc for B∥c and B∥ab. Assess whether increased misfit strain from NC buffers shifts Fp,max to higher reduced fields at low temperatures.

Step11: Optimization loop:
- Identify the CeO2 volume fraction and buffer thickness yielding the highest Fp at 20 K and ≥ 5 T while maintaining Tc ≥ 89 K and 77 K self-field Jc ≥ 2 MA/cm².
- Identify the YBCO laser repetition rate that maximizes c-axis correlated pinning (largest c-axis Jc peak, minimal tortuosity) without degrading texture or Tc; refine around 15–30 Hz if 20 Hz is optimal, and test intermediate rates (e.g., 15, 25, 30 Hz).
- If meandering dislocations are observed at high frequency, experiment with brief growth interruptions (pause 1–2 s every 50 pulses) to restore straightness while keeping an overall higher throughput; evaluate impact.

Step12: Texture and grain boundary control:
- Confirm that Δφ of YBCO remains ≤ Δφ of STO buffer across all conditions; if increased mosaic or sub-grain formation is seen at 100 Hz, reduce substrate temperature by ~10 °C or introduce intermittent pauses to recover in-plane alignment.
- Use rocking curve mapping across the wafer (grid of positions) to ensure uniform texture; correlate with local Jc values from multiple microbridges.

Step13: Reliability and uniformity assessment:
- For the top-performing condition(s), fabricate at least three independent samples to verify reproducibility. Map Jc across 5–9 microbridges per sample to assess within-sample variation (target coefficient of variation ≤ 10%).
- Perform thermal cycling (room temperature ↔ 20 K) for 10 cycles and re-measure Jc(H) at 20 and 40 K to evaluate stability. Store samples in dry nitrogen; repeat measurements after 4 weeks to test aging.

Step14: Comparative benchmarking:
- Compare optimized NC-buffered pure YBCO with pure STO-buffered YBCO and with YBCO+5% BaHfO3 on STO at 20–40 K and 3–9 T for both B∥c and B∥ab. Normalize Jc(H) by self-field Jc at each temperature to highlight high-field performance differences.

Step15: Documentation and safety:
- Maintain detailed run sheets for each deposition (substrate ID, temperature, O2 pressure, laser energy, frequency, pulses, thickness, oxygenation schedule).
- Ensure compliance with laser safety (class IV), high-temperature operation protocols, and oxygen handling for anneals. Verify cooling water flow and interlocks before PLD operation.

Step16: Contingencies and risk mitigation:
- If Ce diffusion into YBCO is detected, increase STO cap thickness to 10–15 nm or reduce buffer deposition temperature by 20–30 °C while preserving vertical nanorod formation (verify by STEM).
- If NC buffers induce surface roughness > 1.5 nm rms causing degraded texture, adjust CeO2 fraction downward or reduce total buffer thickness to 100 nm.
- If Tc drops below 89 K in any set, adjust oxygenation (increase O2 partial pressure and soak time) and consider lowering YBCO growth rate or temperature by ~10 °C to reduce point defect density.

Step17: Final selection and reporting:
- Select the buffer composition/thickness and YBCO laser frequency combination that delivers the highest Fp at 20 K and ≥ 5 T without sacrificing Tc and self-field Jc. Provide a comprehensive correlation between interfacial defect metrics (dislocation density, straightness, strain) and transport performance, supported by XRD, TEM, and PPMS datasets.

Experiment: Step1: Prepare buffered metal tapes. Obtain C276 alloy tapes with Al2O3/Y2O3/IBAD-MgO/LaMnO3/CeO2 buffer stack. Verify in-plane and out-of-plane texture uniformity across 10 mm width by XRD (CeO2 (002) and phi scans), and AFM roughness (<3 nm RMS). Use SEM cross-sections at left edge, center, right edge to confirm buffer thickness uniformity and absence of pre-existing defects. Record baseline Ni content at the CeO2/LMO interface by SEM-EDS line scans (control for later contamination checks).
Step2: Configure the reel-to-reel MPMT-PLD system. Install multi-plume sources for EuBCO and BaHfO3 (BHO). Calibrate laser fluence (e.g., 1.5–2.5 J/cm2) and spot size for each target to ensure stable ablation. Implement synchronized firing for co-deposition with adjustable pulse ratio (EuBCO:BHO) to set BHO volume fraction. Set initial oxygen partial pressure at 150–300 mTorr and a growth rate corresponding to ~1 μm EuBCO thickness per pass (adjust tape speed/laser repetition accordingly).
Step3: Add transverse temperature diagnostics. Install three two-color IR pyrometers (left edge, center, right edge) with emissivity calibration using embedded K-type micro-thermocouples spot-welded to a sacrificial metal tape with identical surface finish. Run calibration through the heater at deposition temperature (target 780–800 °C at the substrate surface) and correct for view factor and emissivity differences. Validate pyrometer readings against thermocouples up to deposition temperature.
Step4: Map the transverse temperature profile under deposition conditions. With vacuum and oxygen flow at setpoints, run the tape at the planned speed without laser firing. Record steady-state temperatures at left/center/right across several helical turns. Repeat with lasers firing onto a dummy target to account for radiative and gas heating. Quantify ΔTedge-center and identify edge hot spots associated with helical travel.
Step5: Implement heater zoning and edge thermal control. Retrofit the radiant heater with independently controlled edge zones or add auxiliary edge heaters/thermal shields to reduce radiative losses and balance convective loads. Iteratively tune zone setpoints to achieve ΔTedge-center ≤ ±5 °C at process conditions. Verify with pyrometry during a simulated deposition run.
Step6: Optimize gas flow uniformity. Using CFD-informed baffles or adjustable oxygen inlet nozzles, balance local oxygen flux across the 10 mm width. Measure spatial pO2 using a calibrated zirconia oxygen probe or by mapping plume scattering with a photodiode array. Target uniform pO2 within ±5% across width; avoid jetting that locally cools or heats edges.
Step7: Reduce mechanical stress and edge friction. Align guide rollers to minimize torsion; install low-friction ceramic-coated edge guides or non-contact gas-lubricated edge supports at turns; set tape tension to a stable value (e.g., 10–30 N range, adjust for tape width/thickness). Add a shield management protocol: rotate or replace deposition shields at set intervals to prevent residue build-up in inter-lane gaps. Confirm via thermal imaging that no localized frictional hot spots form at edges during a dry run.
Step8: Calibrate deposition uniformity and BHO fraction. Use a stationary coupon traverse at the tape plane to collect thickness and composition vs transverse position. Measure thickness by profilometry or X-ray reflectivity across width; measure BHO fraction by XRD (BHO reflections) and cross-sectional TEM area fraction at center and edges. Adjust laser pulse ratio and scanning to achieve 4–8 vol% BHO uniformly across width and thickness uniformity within ±5%.
Step9: Establish a baseline EuBCO+BHO deposition. Deposit EuBCO with 6 vol% BHO onto 2 m of buffered tape using the current settings (heater/oxygen/tension). Post-anneal inline in oxygen at 1 bar, 450–500 °C for 0.5–1 h (tune dwell to tape speed using a heated oxygenation zone). Cool in oxygen to avoid oxygen loss. This baseline will define initial transverse Jc variation and microstructure at edges.
Step10: Baseline transverse property mapping. Mechanically slit the 10 mm tape into 1–2 mm filaments across width (label left edge to right edge). Measure Ic at 77 K, self-field by four-probe transport with a 1 μV/cm criterion; compute Jc using the superconducting cross-sectional area and Je using total cross-section. Complement with vibrating-sample magnetometry on short segments to extract Jc via the Bean model. Plot Jc versus transverse position to quantify left/right edge deficits relative to center.
Step11: Baseline microstructure and composition mapping. Perform micro-XRD mapping with ~50 μm beam across width to collect EuBCO (005) intensity and rocking curves; generate a transverse map of (005) peak intensity and FWHM. Prepare SEM cross-sections at left edge, 2 mm from edge, center, mirror right-side positions. Use SEM-EDS to quantify Ba/Cu and Cu-rich precipitates at edges; map any Ni signal. Prepare FIB lamellae at edges to inspect (i) arched, non-c-axis grains, (ii) BHO nanocolumn alignment, (iii) buffer interfaces (CeO2/LMO) for signs of decomposition. Use STEM-EDS/EELS to detect any CeO2 or LMO decomposition or interdiffusion.
Step12: Composition tuning to suppress Cu segregation. Using the heater zoning and gas uniformity controls, run a designed set of experiments varying edge-zone setpoints (±10–30 °C from center), oxygen pressure (150–300 mTorr), and tape speed (e.g., 3, 5, 7 m/h) while holding plume parameters fixed. For each condition, deposit 0.5–1 m, oxygenate, and assess Ba/Cu vs width by SEM-EDS line scans and by ICP-OES on dissolved film strips (left, center, right). Select conditions that minimize Ba/Cu deviation and eliminate Cu-rich precipitates at edges in SEM.
Step13: Grain boundary tuning to eliminate arched grains. Reduce total thermal budget at edges by lowering edge-zone temperature setpoints until arched grain incidence is minimized without sacrificing c-axis texture at the center. If needed, increase pO2 within the PLD chamber (toward 250–300 mTorr) and increase target–substrate distance to reduce energetic re-sputtering that can cause surface roughening. Confirm by micro-XRD rocking curves (uniform FWHM across width) and TEM that arched grains are suppressed and low-angle grain boundaries dominate.
Step14: Interface tuning to prevent buffer decomposition. At each tuned thermal condition, prepare FIB cross-sections at edges to verify CeO2 and LMO integrity (no porosity, delamination, or composition change). If decomposition is observed, reduce peak edge temperature further, adjust laser fluence downward to reduce high-energy species, or increase pO2 to mitigate reduction. Verify that the CeO2 (002) and LMO reflections and interface planarity are preserved and that EuBCO nucleates epitaxially with flat interfaces across the width.
Step15: Texture tuning via helix management. Implement dual-pass multi-turn deposition with alternating helical angle (e.g., reverse wrap direction or invert the reel orientation between passes) so each physical edge alternately experiences the left/right edge environment to average any residual asymmetry. Compare micro-XRD (005) intensity maps and in-plane phi scans across width for single-pass vs dual-pass tapes; choose the configuration that yields the flattest transverse texture metrics.
Step16: Stress and contamination tuning. Systematically vary tape tension (e.g., 10, 20, 30 N) and guide configurations while monitoring edge temperatures with IR pyrometry and measuring Ni contamination by SEM-EDS at edges after deposition. Implement non-contact edge supports if frictional heating is detected. Accept only configurations with no detectable Ni at the EuBCO/LMO interface and no edge hot spots exceeding the growth temperature.
Step17: Plume distribution and rate balancing across width. Program laser beam scanning or employ beam-shaping optics to compensate for any edge under/over-deposition observed in Step8. Validate thickness and BHO fraction uniformity across width again. Ensure BHO nanocolumns remain well aligned along c-axis (via TEM) and that Tc remains acceptable (e.g., >88–90 K for EuBCO+BHO, measured by magnetization) to avoid over-doping.
Step18: DOE and multivariate optimization. Construct a fractional factorial or response surface design varying: edge zone temperature, center zone temperature, pO2, tape speed, helix alternation (on/off), tension, and BHO fraction (4, 6, 8 vol%). Responses: (i) transverse Jc uniformity (left/center/right), (ii) micro-XRD (005) intensity uniformity and rocking curve FWHM, (iii) arched grain area fraction at edges (TEM/SEM), (iv) Ba/Cu uniformity and Cu-precipitate count, (v) interface integrity score (no decomposition), (vi) Ni contamination (none). Use ANOVA to identify significant factors and their interactions. Select a parameter set that satisfies all constraints and maximizes Jc uniformity.
Step19: Confirm optimized process on mid-length tapes. Deposit three independent 10 m tapes under the optimized conditions. Oxygenate identically. Slit each tape into 1–2 mm filaments and map Ic at 77 K along the width at three positions along length (start, middle, end). Compute Je and transverse variation. Confirm left-edge Jc/center ≥ 0.95 and target ≤5% transverse variation.
Step20: Correlate microstructure with performance at the edges post-optimization. Repeat micro-XRD mapping, SEM-EDS, and FIB-TEM at edges and center to document: (i) absence of arched grains, (ii) preserved CeO2/LMO integrity, (iii) uniform BHO nanocolumn alignment, and (iv) uniform Ba/Cu without Cu-rich precipitates. Archive representative images and diffraction data.
Step21: Angular and field-dependent pinning verification. On optimized samples (left, center, right), measure Jc(B, θ) at 77 K and at lower temperatures (e.g., 65 K) up to available fields (e.g., 1–3 T in VSM or transport, if available). Confirm that c-axis correlated pinning from BHO nanocolumns is consistent across width and that no edge-specific anomalies exist.
Step22: Long-length production run. Produce ≥100 m of EuBCO+BHO tape with the optimized parameters, alternating helix as defined. Implement scheduled shield maintenance to prevent residue accumulation. Use inline pyrometry to continuously monitor left/center/right temperatures; log ΔTedge-center. Oxygenate inline as before.
Step23: Statistical quality mapping of the long-length run. Every 10 m, cut 10 cm segments; from each, slit across width into 1–2 mm filaments. Perform quick micro-XRD (005) intensity scans across width and four-probe Ic at 77 K self-field at least at left, center, right filaments. Compile transverse Jc variation statistics over length. Target Je ≥ 2.5×10^9 A/m^2 at 77 K self-field across width with ≤5% transverse variation.
Step24: Failure analysis loop if criteria are not met. If any segment shows >5% transverse variation, return to diagnostics: check pyrometry logs for ΔT excursions, inspect shields for residue build-up, examine guide wear, and perform SEM-EDS at the failing edge to identify Cu precipitation or buffer damage. Apply corrective actions (e.g., adjust edge zone setpoints, maintenance frequency, helix pattern) and re-run a shorter validation tape before resuming long-length production.
Step25: Documentation and handoff. Compile a process manual detailing: heater zone setpoints, pO2, tape speed, helix alternation protocol, tension and guide configuration, shield maintenance intervals, and oxygenation conditions. Include metrology SOPs for micro-XRD mapping, SEM-EDS, FIB-TEM, ICP-OES, and transverse Ic mapping. Define acceptance criteria: (i) ΔTedge-center ≤ ±5 °C during deposition, (ii) no detectable Ni at EuBCO/LMO interface, (iii) no arched grains at edges by SEM/TEM, (iv) uniform BHO nanocolumns, (v) Je ≥ 2.5×10^9 A/m^2 at 77 K self-field with ≤5% transverse variation across the 10 mm width.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Tape fabrication  
- A several-hundred-metre-long, 10 mm-wide EuBCO tape with the layer sequence C276/Al2O3/Y2O3/IBAD-MgO/LaMnO3/CeO2/EuBCO/Ag (total thickness 54 µm) was grown on a Hastelloy C276 substrate using an industrial reel-to-reel MPMT-PLD system (details of deposition temperature, laser energy, repetition rate, oxygen pressure, tape speed, etc. are not given).

Step 2: Mechanical slitting  
- Two short sections were cut from the long tape.  
- Scheme 1: slit into five 2 mm-wide filaments.  
- Scheme 2: slit into six filaments (1/2/2/2/2/1 mm).  
(Exact slitting tool or conditions are not specified.)

Step 3: Transport Jc measurement (four-probe)  
- Each filament was measured at 77 K in self-field.  
- Critical current Ic was defined with a 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion and extracted by power-law fitting.  
- Jc was calculated by dividing Ic by the filament cross-sectional area (thickness × width).

Step 4: Magnetic Jc measurement (Bean model)  
- For scheme-1 filaments, magnetic moment versus field (B || c-axis) was recorded at 77 K in a 9 T Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS).  
- Jc(μ₀H) was derived from the magnetic hysteresis loops using the Bean model.

Step 5: Chemical analysis  
- The silver cap layer was removed with an ammonia + hydrogen-peroxide solution.  
- Filaments from scheme 2 were dissolved and analysed with a Perkin-Elmer Avio™ 500 inductively-coupled-plasma optical-emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) to obtain Eu/Ba and Ba/Cu atomic ratios across the tape width.

Step 6: Surface morphology and local chemistry  
- A TESCAN RISE-MAGNA scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) was used to image the EuBCO surface and map elemental distributions.

Step 7: Crystallographic survey  
- Micro-area X-ray diffraction (micro-XRD) θ–2θ scans were performed with a Rigaku SmartLab system using a 50 µm-diameter Cu-Kα beam (λ = 1.54 Å).  
- Patterns were collected every 0.5 mm from the left edge to the centre (11 points total).  
- EuBCO (005) peak intensity was normalised to the CeO2 (002) peak to track relative crystallinity.

Step 8: Cross-sectional microstructure  
- A GAIA3 dual-beam focused-ion-beam (FIB) system prepared electron-transparent lamellae.  
- A Talos F200X transmission electron microscope (TEM) with EDS mapped phase distribution, grain orientation and elemental composition in arched/loose regions at the tape edge.

[Experimental Design Details]
- All electrical and magnetic measurements were carried out at 77 K; no other temperatures are reported.  
- Magnetic field orientation was fixed parallel to the crystallographic c-axis (B || c).  
- No information is given on sample mounting, contact geometry, voltage-tap separation, or loop sizes for magnetic measurements.  
- Slitting-induced cracks are acknowledged but not quantified; authors argue that the observed Jc trend cannot be explained by cracking alone.
