Experiment: Step1: Define composition sets and metrics.
- Choose five equiatomic multi-RE compositions on the RE site of REBa2Cu3O7−y (RE123): (Eu1/3Gd1/3Y1/3)BCO; (Eu1/4Gd1/4Y1/4Er1/4)BCO; (Eu1/5Gd1/5Y1/5Er1/5Yb1/5)BCO; (Nd1/4Eu1/4Gd1/4Y1/4)BCO; (La1/5Nd1/5Eu1/5Gd1/5Y1/5)BCO. Include single-RE references (YBCO, GdBCO, NdBCO) prepared identically for baseline comparison.
- Compute configurational entropy at the RE site, ΔSmix = −R Σi xi ln xi (equiatomic: 3-RE ≈ R ln3, 4-RE ≈ R ln4, 5-RE ≈ R ln5).
- Compute average RE3+ ionic radius r̄RE = Σi xi ri using Shannon RE3+ radii with a consistent coordination (recommend CN=8 for comparability). Record r̄RE target range (≈1.03–1.08 Å) and plan supplementary “decoupling” pairs:
  • Constant r̄RE, variable ΔSmix: adjust non-equiatomic fractions of (Nd, Yb, Eu, Gd, Y) to match r̄RE of the 4-RE Eu–Gd–Y–Er while using 3, 4, and 5 species (two compositions per ΔSmix level).
  • Constant ΔSmix (same number of species), variable r̄RE: 4-RE sets (Eu–Gd–Y–Er), (Nd–Gd–Y–Er), (Eu–Gd–Y–Yb).
- Establish sample IDs and batch plan: at least N=3 independent pellets per composition for statistics.

Step2: Prepare starting reagents and pre-treat oxides.
- Reagents: high-purity (≥99.9%) RE2O3 (RE = La, Nd, Eu, Gd, Y, Er, Yb), BaCO3, and CuO.
- Dry RE2O3 at 900 °C for 12 h in air to remove adsorbed water/CO2; cool in desiccator.
- Pre-sieve powders (200 mesh). Store and weigh in a dry box to minimize moisture uptake.

Step3: Stoichiometric weighing and mixing.
- Target nominal RE:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3; compute individual RE2O3 masses to realize designed RE molar fractions at the RE site.
- Wet-mix with isopropanol in a ZrO2 media planetary mill (ball:powder = 5:1) for 6 h at 300 rpm. Dry at 80 °C; sieve again.

Step4: First calcination to form RE123 precursor.
- Calcine mixed powders in flowing air: ramp 3 °C/min to 940 °C, dwell 12 h, furnace-cool. Break agglomerates; verify color and flowability.
- Intermediate XRD check (Cu Kα) to confirm major RE123 formation and absence of BaCO3. If BaCO3 persists, extend calcination to 16 h.

Step5: Second grind and calcine for phase homogenization.
- Regrind 30 min; second calcination at 940 °C for 12 h in air; slow cool to 600 °C at 2 °C/min, then to room temperature. Sieve powders.

Step6: Differential scanning calorimetry/thermogravimetry (DSC-TG) to determine peritectic temperature Tp for each composition.
- DSC-TG on ~30 mg powder in flowing air (or O2/air blend), Pt crucibles. Heat 25→1100 °C at 10 °C/min; record endothermic signature of peritectic decomposition (RE123 → RE211 + liquid).
- Define Tp as the onset of the peritectic endotherm; tabulate Tp for each composition. This enables tailored sintering at Tp + 5 °C.

Step7: Powder consolidation.
- Add 1–2 wt% PVA binder in ethanol; granulate; dry.
- Uniaxial press bars (e.g., 2×3×12 mm) and pellets (Ø10 mm×2 mm) at 250 MPa. Optionally cold isostatic press at 300 MPa. Binder burn-out: heat in air to 600 °C at 1 °C/min, dwell 2 h.

Step8: Peritectic-assisted densification (interface tuning).
- For each composition, sinter in air with the same thermal program relative to its Tp to generate a minute CuO-rich liquid:
  • Ramp 3 °C/min to Tp − 20 °C, dwell 1 h (stress relaxation).
  • Ramp 1 °C/min to Tp + 5 °C, dwell 10–15 min (brief wetting by liquid).
  • Cool at 2 °C/min to Tp − 10 °C, dwell 6 h (re-formation of 123, grain bonding).
  • Furnace-cool to 450 °C at 3 °C/min.
- Keep identical dwell times, heating/cooling rates, and atmosphere for all compositions to isolate compositional effects. Use type-S thermocouple near samples to avoid overshoot. Use dense alumina setters to minimize reaction with crucibles.

Step9: Oxygenation (400 °C, 48 h).
- Transfer to a tube furnace with flowing O2 (≥99.99%, 0.5–1 L/min). Heat to 400 °C at 1.5 °C/min, dwell 48 h, then slow cool at 0.5 °C/min to 200 °C and 1 °C/min to room temperature. Alternate protocol for confirmation: 450 °C 12 h + 350 °C 24 h. Quench a subset to capture oxygen content for iodometry.

Step10: Geometric metrology and density.
- Measure dimensions (±2 μm) and mass. Determine bulk density by Archimedes in ethanol; compute relative density using theoretical density for RE123 (~6.3 g/cm3; adjust per lattice parameters if needed). Target 84–92% relative density.

Step11: Phase analysis and lattice parameters (XRD-Rietveld).
- Powder XRD: 10–120° 2θ, step 0.02°, count ≥1 s/step, Cu Kα; collect for powders from crushed pellets.
- Rietveld refinement: refine cell parameters, scale, background, preferred orientation, microstrain; quantify secondary phases (RE211, BaCuO2). Confirm orthorhombic structure (a ≠ b; splitting of (020)/(200)).
- Plot a, b, c vs r̄RE; fit linear trends; extract orthorhombicity (b − a)/(b + a).

Step12: Composition verification and homogeneity (SEM-EDS; ICP).
- FE-SEM backscatter to visualize second phases; quantify grain size and aspect ratio (platelets).
- EDS area mapping (≥5 grains per sample) to confirm ~equi-atomic RE occupation and uniform RE distribution at micrometer scale.
- ICP-OES or ICP-MS on digested powders to verify bulk RE:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3 within ±1–2%. Compare La occupancy to assess possible Ba-site substitution (look for Ba deficiency coupled with La excess).

Step13: Oxygen stoichiometry and chain ordering.
- Iodometric titration on crushed, oxygenated pellets to determine average oxygen content 7 − y; target near fully oxygenated Ortho-I regime.
- Optional Raman spectroscopy (200–700 cm−1) to assess chain vibration modes indicative of Ortho-I ordering.

Step14: Nanoscale defect characterization (FIB, STEM/HRTEM, FFT).
- Prepare [001]-oriented lamellae by FIB lift-out with low-kV final polish to reduce damage.
- HRTEM at 200–300 kV; acquire images along [010]/[100] to resolve ab-plane stacking. Use FFT to index lattice and identify stacking faults (SFs); perform g·R analysis to highlight planar defects.
- STEM-HAADF with EDS/EELS line scans across faults to assess cation/oxygen perturbations.
- Quantify SF areal density (faults per μm), mean spacing, and length distribution over ≥20 fields and ≥5 grains per sample. Correlate SF metrics with ΔSmix and r̄RE.

Step15: Thermal stability cross-check (DSC on sintered pellets).
- Repeat DSC on small pieces to confirm Tp and evaluate any shift due to densification/oxygenation. Ensure processing did not introduce unwanted secondary phases.

Step16: Superconducting properties: magnetometry (PPMS/SQUID).
- Cut bar-shaped specimens with parallel faces; record dimensions for demagnetization correction.
- ZFC/FC magnetization M(T) from 120 K to 10 K at 1–10 mT to determine Tc onset and transition width; estimate superconducting volume fraction from low-field shielding at 10 K with demag correction.
- M–H loops at 4.2 K and 77 K up to ±7–9 T; sweep rates ~10–20 Oe/s. Calculate critical current density Jc using the extended Bean model for rectangular prisms: Jc = 20ΔM/[a(1 − a/3b)] (A/cm2) with a ≤ b; correct for demagnetization where needed.
- Compute normalized pinning force Fp = Jc μ0 H; construct Fp(h) vs reduced field h = H/Hirr and fit with Dew-Hughes scaling to infer dominant pinning type (planar vs point/volume). Extract Fp,max and its h position.

Step17: Transport critical current validation.
- Four-probe I–V at 4.2 K (liquid He) and 77 K (liquid N2) on bars; voltage criterion 1 μV/cm. Use silver paste contacts cured at 450 °C in O2. Compare transport Jc with magnetic Jc to assess connectivity and weak-link behavior.

Step18: Magneto-optical (MO) imaging of current flow.
- Use in-plane Bi-substituted iron garnet indicator film; image trapped flux at 77 K after field cooling and zero-field cooling. Analyze current streamlines to distinguish intergranular vs intragranular current limitation and to visualize flux penetration linked to microstructural features.

Step19: Decoupling analysis framework.
- Build a dataset per pellet: ΔSmix, r̄RE, density, grain size, orthorhombicity, oxygen content, SF density metrics, Tc, superconducting volume fraction, Jc(0 T, 4.2 K), Jc(5 T, 4.2 K), Jc(0 T, 77 K).
- Perform multivariate regression and partial correlation to quantify the independent contributions of ΔSmix, r̄RE, SF density, and density to Jc and Tc, controlling for microstructure. Use ANOVA across composition groups (La-free vs La-containing).

Step20: Control experiments to isolate mechanisms.
- Processing control: prepare a subset sintered at Tp − 10 °C (no liquid) with all else identical to test the role of liquid-phase wetting on density and intergrain Jc.
- Defect density control: vary the Tp + ΔT dwell time (0, 5, 15, 30 min) for the 4-RE Eu–Gd–Y–Er to examine SF density tuning and its effect on Jc.
- La effect control: compare La-containing 5-RE with La-free 5-RE at matched r̄RE; assess Tc suppression, transition width, and Jc.
- Oxygenation control: compare 400 °C/48 h with 450 °C/12 h + 350 °C/24 h to ensure full oxygenation without decomposition; verify lattice orthorhombicity.

Step21: Quality assurance and reproducibility.
- Replicate each composition in at least three independent batches; report mean ± standard deviation for key metrics.
- Calibrate furnaces with reference thermocouples; verify oxygen flow with a mass flow controller; periodically validate magnetometer calibration with a standard sample (e.g., Ni sphere).
- Document exact thermal profiles from embedded thermocouples near samples to ensure Tp + 5 °C accuracy within ±2 °C.

Step22: Safety and environmental controls.
- Handle RE and CuO powders in a fume hood; use P100 respirators and gloves. Dispose of waste according to local regulations.
- High-temperature oxygen processing: ensure oxygen-compatible tubing and purge protocols; avoid combustible materials; install flashback arrestors. Use eye/hand protection for liquid He/N2 operations.

Step23: Go/no-go and success criteria.
- Structural: single-phase orthorhombic RE123 with secondary phases <2 wt% by Rietveld; equiaxed platelet grains with similar size distributions across compositions.
- Superconductivity: Tc ≥ 90 K with narrow transition (ΔT ≤ 3 K) for La-free compositions; superconducting volume fraction ≥90% at 10 K (demag corrected).
- Performance: quantify and compare Jc across compositions; identify whether 4-RE Eu–Gd–Y–Er or other La-free medium-entropy mixes maximize Jc at 4.2 K and maintain Jc(5 T, 4.2 K) ≥ 10 kA/cm2. Correlate high Jc with increased SF density and high superconducting volume fraction.

Step24: Reporting and data integrity.
- Archive raw XRD, DSC/TG, SEM/TEM, magnetometry, transport, and MO data with metadata (sample ID, batch, geometry, processing profile).
- Provide plots of lattice parameters vs r̄RE (linear fits), Tc and superconducting volume vs ΔSmix and r̄RE, Jc vs field, Fp scaling, and Jc vs SF density. Include statistical analyses supporting conclusions about the relative roles of configurational entropy, ionic size, and composition-driven defect engineering.

Step25: Optional extensions toward applications.
- Machine larger rings or slabs from the best-performing composition; evaluate trapped field at 77 K and 4.2 K; assess mechanical robustness (Vickers hardness, fracture toughness).
- Evaluate AC loss (P–Q measurements) at 77 K for coil-relevant conditions to preliminarily assess suitability for magnet and flywheel applications.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Raw-material weighing  
- Commercial oxide/carbonate powders (La₂O₃, Nd₂O₃, Eu₂O₃, Gd₂O₃, Y₂O₃, Er₂O₃, Yb₂O₃, BaCO₃, CuO; all ≥99.9 % purity) were weighed to give the atomic ratio RE : Ba : Cu = 1 : 2 : 3 for each of the five target compositions (Table 1).  

Step 2: Powder calcination (twice)  
- The mixed powders were heated in flowing air (200 SCCM) at 600 °C h⁻¹ to 940 °C, held 10 h, cooled at 60 °C h⁻¹ to 400 °C, then furnace-cooled to room temperature.  
- Manual grinding in an agate mortar for 15 min was carried out between the two identical calcination runs.  

Step 3: Bulk-sample forming  
- Calcined powder was uniaxially pressed in a 10 mm-inner-diameter cylindrical steel die at ≈250 MPa to form green pellets.  

Step 4: Bulk sintering  
- Pellets were sintered in flowing air at T = Tₚ + 5 °C (Tₚ individually measured by DSC) to generate a small liquid-phase assist.  
- After sintering, an oxygen-annealing step was added: 400 °C for 48 h in air (furnace cooled).  

Step 5: Phase identification & lattice-parameter determination  
- Room-temperature X-ray diffraction (Bruker D8 Advance, Cu Kα 40 kV/40 mA, 3 ° min⁻¹, 0.02 ° step) on powder samples; Rietveld refinement provided lattice parameters.  

Step 6: Thermal stability (Tₚ) measurement  
- DSC/TG (NETZSCH STA 449F5) on powders from 40 °C to 1100 °C at 5 °C min⁻¹ in flowing gas (air); Tₚ taken as the second endothermic peak (T₂).  

Step 7: Density measurement  
- Bulk density obtained by the Archimedes method; relative densities reported as 84–92 %.  

Step 8: Microstructural & compositional analyses  
- FE-SEM (JEOL JSM-IT800) with EDS on polished surfaces (successively ground to 2000-grit SiC, polished with 0.5 µm diamond paste, ultrasonically cleaned in alcohol; water contact minimized; final etch 0.5 wt % HCl in ethanol 4–6 s).  
- TEM/EDS (FEI Talos F200X G2, 200 kV) on FIB-cut foils (Helios G4Ux; Pt protective layer, Ga-ion milling).  

Step 9: Superconducting property measurements  
- T꜀: DC magnetic moment vs temperature (M–T) recorded in a Quantum Design PPMS under zero-field-cooled (ZFC) and field-cooled (FC) protocols at 10 Oe.  
- J꜀: Magnetic hysteresis loops (M–H) at 4.2 K and 77 K on cuboid specimens (≈1.8 × 2.0 × 2.0 mm³); J꜀ extracted using the extended Bean critical-state model.  

[Experimental Design Details]
- Atmosphere: flowing air (200 SCCM) for all heat treatments unless otherwise stated; final oxygen anneal in static air.  
- Heating/cooling rates: 600 °C h⁻¹ up, 60 °C h⁻¹ down (powder calcination); 5 °C min⁻¹ for DSC/TG.  
- Sintering temperature: individually set at Tₚ + 5 °C for each composition (Tₚ from prior DSC run; values listed in Table 2).  
- Sample shapes: powders for XRD/DSC; 10 mm-diameter pellets for bulk property/microstructure studies; small cuboids cut from pellets for magnetic measurements.  
- Magnetic measurement fields: 10 Oe for T꜀; hysteresis loops taken up to 5 T (J꜀ field dependence).

Experiment: Step1: Define objectives and acceptance criteria.
- Objective: Maximize transport critical current density Jc at 20 K and 9 T with B parallel to c-axis in YBa2Cu3Oy films containing 3 vol.% BaHfO3 nanorods deposited on IBAD-MgO buffered metallic tapes.
- Target performance: Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) ≥ 0.4 MA cm^-2 on patterned microbridges using 1 μV cm^-1 electric field criterion.
- Strategy variables to optimize: Y stoichiometry (x in YxBa2Cu3Oy) and substrate temperature T_sub during PLD; hold BaHfO3 volume fraction at 3 vol.%.
- Constraints: Preserve strong biaxial texture (Δφ ≤ 5°, Δω ≤ 2°), maintain film integrity (no microcracks), and minimize grain boundary weak links.

Step2: Prepare BaHfO3 (BHO) powder for composite targets.
- Starting reagents: BaCO3 (99.99%), HfO2 (99.9%).
- Stoichiometric mixing for BaHfO3, ball mill in ethanol for 12 h with zirconia media, dry at 120 °C.
- Calcine in air at 1200–1250 °C for 12 h, cool, regrind, and re-calcine at 1250 °C for 12 h to complete perovskite formation.
- Verify phase by powder XRD (no residual BaCO3/HfO2 peaks), then sieve to <45 μm.

Step3: Synthesize YxBa2Cu3Oy powders for PLD targets.
- Starting reagents: Y2O3, BaCO3, CuO (≥99.9%).
- Prepare series of compositions for x = 1.00, 0.95, 0.92, 0.90, 0.88, 0.85.
- For each x, weigh stoichiometric Y2O3:BaCO3:CuO for YxBa2Cu3; wet-mix and ball mill in ethanol 12 h; dry at 120 °C.
- First calcine in air at 900 °C for 12 h; regrind; second calcine at 920 °C for 12 h; regrind; third calcine at 930–940 °C for 12 h in flowing oxygen to promote phase formation.
- Confirm phase by XRD (dominant YBCO peaks; minimal BaCuO2/CuO secondary phases).

Step4: Fabricate composite PLD targets with 3 vol.% BHO.
- For each Yx composition, blend pre-synthesized YxBa2Cu3Oy powder with 3 vol.% BaHfO3 powder thoroughly (ball mill in isopropanol 6 h, low media-to-powder ratio to avoid particle size segregation), dry.
- Press 1-inch or 2-inch diameter pellets at ≥150 MPa; cold isostatic press if available at 300 MPa.
- Sinter in flowing O2 at 930–940 °C for 24 h; slow cool (1–2 °C/min) to 450 °C in O2, hold 12 h to oxygenate; cool to room temperature.
- Lap/polish target faces to flatness; pre-ablate in PLD chamber to remove surface contamination.
- Characterize targets: density ≥ 90–95% theoretical; XRD confirms YBCO matrix with BHO secondary phase; measure electrical resistance (qualitatively low) to ensure robust laser coupling.

Step5: Prepare IBAD-MgO buffered metallic tapes.
- Use Hastelloy-based substrates with standard buffer stack (example: Y2O3/YSZ/IBAD-MgO/homoepitaxial MgO/CeO2 cap), with room-temperature texture targets: Δφ(IBAD-MgO) ≤ 5°, Δω ≤ 2°.
- Cut 10×10 mm or 5×20 mm coupons; clean in acetone and isopropanol; dry with N2.
- Optional: Gentle UV-ozone or low-power O2 plasma clean (≤5 min) to remove organics.
- Verify texture by XRD rocking curve (002) and phi scan; document Δφ and Δω for each coupon.

Step6: Set up PLD growth system and calibrations.
- Use KrF excimer laser (248 nm); calibrate fluence at target to 1.5–2.0 J cm^-2; repetition rate 5–10 Hz; spot size 2–4 mm^2; ensure uniform target rotation and rastering.
- Target–substrate distance: 45–55 mm; substrate rotation 5–20 rpm.
- Substrate heating: Radiant heater with optical pyrometer calibrated against thermocouple on a dummy coated substrate; correct emissivity for CeO2/MgO surface.
- Chamber background: Oxygen partial pressure 150–300 mTorr for growth; base pressure <1×10^-6 Torr before O2 backfill.
- Growth rate calibration: Deposit test film at nominal conditions, measure thickness by profilometry or X-ray reflectivity (XRR); establish nm/pulse and adjust pulse count to reach 0.7–1.0 μm thickness (target 0.8 μm for initial runs).
- Pre-ablation: With shutter closed, ablate target for 2–3 min at growth fluence and rep rate.

Step7: Define Bayesian optimization loop parameters and initial design.
- Decision variables: Y stoichiometry x ∈ [0.85, 1.00]; substrate temperature T_sub ∈ [820, 890] °C.
- Fixed parameters: 3 vol.% BHO; pO2 = 200 mTorr; laser fluence 1.8 J cm^-2; rep rate 7 Hz; target–substrate distance 50 mm; film thickness ≈0.8 μm; substrate rotation 10 rpm; in-situ oxygenation schedule as in Step9.
- Objective function: Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) measured on patterned microbridges.
- Surrogate model: Gaussian process with Matérn 5/2 kernel; input standardization; output log(Jc) to stabilize variance.
- Acquisition: Expected Improvement (EI) with exploration parameter ξ = 0.01–0.05.
- Initialization: Space-filling 6-point design (e.g., x,T_sub pairs: [1.00, 840], [0.95, 840], [0.90, 870], [0.88, 870], [1.00, 870], [0.90, 830] °C). Randomize run order to reduce drift.
- Stopping criteria: No EI-proposed improvement >5% after 5 consecutive iterations or total runs reach 18–24.

Step8: Deposit YBCO+BHO films for each planned run.
- Mount tape coupon with ceramic clips; introduce into chamber; pump to base pressure; backfill O2 to 200 mTorr.
- Ramp to target T_sub; dwell ≥10 min for thermal equilibration; verify steady pyrometer reading.
- With shutter closed, pre-ablate target; open shutter to deposit; use pulse count from Step6 for ~0.8 μm thickness.
- Monitor plume visually; adjust laser energy if plume dims; keep target and substrate rotation on.
- For compositions x ≠ 1.00, switch to the corresponding Yx+3 vol.% BHO composite target; maintain identical optics and distance.
- Maintain constant pO2 and laser parameters across all runs to isolate the effects of x and T_sub.

Step9: In-situ oxygenation and cooldown.
- After deposition, increase chamber O2 pressure to 500 mTorr and ramp down to 500 °C at 10 °C/min; hold at 500 °C for 30 min.
- Increase O2 to 1 Torr; ramp to 450 °C at 2–3 °C/min; hold 60 min to oxygenate; cool to room temperature at 2 °C/min in 1 Torr O2.
- Vent with dry O2 or N2; unload samples.

Step10: Measure film thickness, surface morphology, and texture.
- Thickness: Stylus profilometry across a masked step or XRR; target 0.8 ± 0.1 μm.
- AFM: 5×5 μm scans to assess surface roughness (RMS ≤ 5–10 nm).
- XRD: θ–2θ scans to confirm c-axis orientation (00l peaks); rocking curve (005) for Δω; phi-scan of (103) for Δφ; reciprocal space maps (RSM) around (103) to estimate in-plane strain.
- Record any secondary peaks indicative of BHO; document peak widths and positions.

Step11: Prepare TEM specimens and quantify BHO nanorods.
- Cross-section and plan-view lamellae by focused ion beam (FIB) with low-kV final polish (≤2 kV) to minimize damage.
- STEM imaging: HAADF and BF for rod contrast; measure rod diameter distribution (target 5–10 nm) and number density (rods per μm^2) from plan-view images; analyze ≥10 fields per sample for statistics.
- Determine nanorod alignment/tilt angle relative to c-axis from cross-sections; compile histograms of tilt angles.
- Record presence of stacking faults, porosity at grain boundaries, and any secondary phases.

Step12: Pattern microbridges and form contacts.
- Define microbridges by UV laser scribing or photolithography plus ion milling: width 50–100 μm, length between voltage taps 0.5–1.0 mm.
- Deposit Au contact pads (e.g., 100 nm by sputtering or evaporation); anneal at 200–250 °C in O2 for 15–30 min if needed for contact resistance reduction.
- Four-probe wiring with low-thermal EMF leads; verify contact resistance <0.1 Ω at 300 K.

Step13: Transport measurements in PPMS.
- Mount sample on rotator puck to control field angle; ensure thermal anchoring and minimal loop area in leads.
- Cool to 20 K in helium; apply magnetic field up to 9 T; align B//c and B//ab as required.
- I–V characterization: Sweep current until criterion E-field of 1 μV cm^-1 is reached; extract Jc = I_c/(w·t); correct for actual bridge width and thickness.
- Measure Jc(B) at 20 K for B = 0–9 T at B//c and B//ab; measure Jc(θ) at fixed 9 T over ±90° to capture angular pinning.
- Optional: Measure resistivity vs T (R–T) to determine Tc and assess oxygenation; measure B_irr by 1% resistive criterion vs field at 20 K.

Step14: Feed results into Bayesian optimization and iterate.
- For each run, input (x, T_sub) and objective value Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) into the GP model; include measurement uncertainty (e.g., 5–10%) as noise level.
- Compute EI; select next (x, T_sub) pair; prioritize exploration near promising regions and around T_sub ≈ 870 °C if suggested by model.
- Repeat Steps 8–13 for each new proposal until stopping criteria are met.

Step15: Microstructure–performance correlation and mechanism checks.
- Correlate Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) with nanorod number density, average diameter, and tilt angle from TEM; examine whether increased supersaturation (via lower x) correlates with finer, denser, slightly tilted rods.
- Assess grain boundary quality: TEM/SEM for porosity and second phases; quantify if lower x reduces boundary porosity.
- Strain/residual stress: Use XRD peak shifts and Williamson–Hall analysis to estimate microstrain; optionally use Raman spectroscopy to probe lattice strain; look for trends with x indicating stress compensation.
- Verify texture retention across x and T_sub (no degradation in Δφ, Δω) to ensure percolative current paths remain long.

Step16: Validate the best-performing recipe.
- Select the top 1–2 parameter sets from the BO loop; reproduce films on at least 3 independent tape coupons each.
- Repeat Steps 10–13; evaluate mean and standard deviation of Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c); acceptance if mean ≥0.4 MA cm^-2 with ≤10% relative standard deviation.
- Perform extended angular Jc(θ) mapping and extract anisotropy; confirm correlated c-axis pinning peak with slight broadening consistent with nanorod tilt.
- Determine B_irr at 20 K by resistive transition under field; compare to baseline x=1.0.

Step17: Engineering and robustness assessments.
- Thermal cycling: Cycle between 300 K and 20 K for 10 cycles; remeasure Jc at 20 K, 9 T (B//c) to assess retention.
- Bending/tensile test (if equipment available): Apply axial strain up to ±0.3%; measure Jc at 77 K self-field and at 20 K, 9 T to evaluate strain tolerance.
- Long-length feasibility check: Deposit a short reel-to-reel section (e.g., 10–50 cm) at the best recipe; perform non-contact Hall-probe scanning for Ic uniformity at 77 K; cut samples for PPMS tests as above.

Step18: Risk mitigation and contingency adjustments.
- If Jc falls below target while texture is good, adjust oxygenation schedule (e.g., extend 450 °C O2 hold to 90 min) and remeasure Tc and Jc.
- If nanorods are too coarse or sparse at intended x and T_sub, reduce T_sub by 10–20 °C or increase pO2 to 300 mTorr to raise supersaturation; alternatively, modestly increase laser rep rate to reduce adatom surface diffusion length.
- If nanorod over-tilt or meandering degrades B//c pinning, narrow T_sub window and reduce plume energy (slightly lower fluence) to stabilize vertical alignment.
- If grain boundary porosity is observed at lower x, increase substrate temperature dwell before deposition and/or implement a brief low-rate seed layer (~50 nm) to promote island coalescence before full-rate growth.

Step19: Documentation and data management.
- Record all PLD parameters, target batch IDs, substrate IDs, XRD metrics, TEM quantification, and transport data in a centralized database.
- Store raw and processed data from PPMS, XRD, TEM; maintain BO model state and history (hyperparameters, acquisition values) for reproducibility.

Step20: Final reporting and go/no-go decision.
- Summarize best recipe (x, T_sub, and fixed conditions), microstructural metrics (nanorod density, diameter, tilt), and transport performance with uncertainty.
- Confirm whether the acceptance criterion Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) ≥ 0.4 MA cm^-2 is met reproducibly without compromising texture or self-field Jc.
- If met, proceed to scale-up planning and integration into compact fusion magnet conductor test protocols; if not, revisit Step18 and iterate targeted refinements focusing on supersaturation and interface control.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Substrate preparation  
- Use IBAD-MgO templates (CeO2/LaMnO3/IBAD-MgO/Y2O3/Al2O3/Hastelloy C-276) with biaxially textured MgO.

Step 2: Target preparation  
- Prepare PLD targets with nominal Y compositions x = 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2 in YxBCO + 3 vol.% BHO.

Step 3: Film deposition  
- Deposit ~300 nm thick YBCO+BHO films by PLD using a KrF excimer laser (λ = 248 nm).  
- Fixed deposition parameters: oxygen pressure 400 mTorr, target–substrate distance 50 mm, laser repetition rate 10 Hz, laser fluence 2.0 J cm⁻².  
- Vary Ts in 10 °C steps from 820 °C to 900 °C.

Step 4: Iterative optimization loop (data-driven)  
- After each deposition batch, measure Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) on patterned micro-bridges.  
- Update a Gaussian-process-regression (GPR) model with the new Jc data; compute Expected-Improvement acquisition map using BOXVIA software.  
- Select next Ts–Y-ratio conditions either at the acquisition maximum, in unexplored regions, or at empirically promising points.  
- Repeat until the acquisition map shows no further high-value regions (22 explored conditions total).

Step 5: Sample patterning  
- Pattern films into 50–100 µm wide, 1 mm long bridges using a 355 nm UV laser marker.

Step 6: Electrical characterization  
- Perform standard DC four-probe I–V measurements in PPMS at 20 K (and additionally 77 K, 65 K) under magnetic fields up to 9 T.  
- Define critical current Ic with 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion; calculate Jc = Ic/bridge cross-section.

Step 7: Microstructural analysis (on selected samples)  
- Prepare cross-sectional and plan-view TEM specimens.  
- Acquire STEM images to measure BHO nanorod diameter, number density, and tilt distribution.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Objective variable: Jc at 20 K, 9 T, B//c (A cm⁻²).  
- Input variables for GPR: normalized Y ratio and Ts.  
- Kernel: rational quadratic, k(xi,xj)= (1+d²/2αl)^-α; α and l fitted during regression.  
- Acquisition function: Expected Improvement (EI).  
- Optimization terminated when suggested points overlapped already-tested conditions and no high-uncertainty regions remained.  
- Optimum identified at Y = 0.9, Ts = 870 °C.

Step2: Prepare materials and equipment: KrF excimer laser (~248 nm), four PLD systems (two static R&D, two reel-to-reel), oxygen supply with mass flow control, in-situ plume imaging (ICCD or high-speed camera), optical pyrometer (two-color preferred), thermocouples for calibration, energy meter for laser fluence, XRD (θ–2θ, ω-rocking, φ-scans), AFM, SEM/TEM, PPMS or equivalent for Tc and magnetotransport up to 9 T, four-probe measurement setup with cryostat and rotator to set B||c, photolithography or laser scribing for bridges, oxygen annealing furnace. Step3: Substrate selection and preparation—IBAD templates: select IBAD-MgO/CeO2 on Hastelloy or Ni-W tapes with in-plane Δϕ ≤ 2.0° (measured by supplier or verified by φ-scan); prefer CeO2-terminated templates; inspect surface by AFM (RMS roughness ≤ 2 nm over 5×5 µm^2). Clean in acetone/isopropanol, dry N2; avoid wet chemistries that attack buffer layers. Step4: Substrate selection and preparation—SrTiO3: choose single-crystal (001) STO; perform chemical TiO2 termination (e.g., buffered HF etch) followed by anneal in flowing O2 at 950–1000 °C for 1–2 h to form atomically flat terraces; AFM verify step-terrace morphology; solvent clean before loading. Step5: YBCO target preparation: use stoichiometric YBa2Cu3O7-δ ceramic targets (density > 90% theoretical); pre-ablate the target (5–10k pulses at growth fluence in O2) to reach steady-state stoichiometry; inspect target surface; maintain target rotation and rastering during deposition. Step6: PLD system calibration per chamber: measure target–substrate distance, laser spot size, and set laser fluence to 1.5–2.0 J cm^-2 (measured at target); set repetition rate 5–10 Hz; calibrate Tsub readings using (i) contact thermocouple on a dummy substrate, (ii) two-color pyrometer focused on substrate, and (iii) post-deposition phase/texture response on STO across a Tsub sweep; record chamber metadata (heater type, thermocouple placement, base pressure, plume–substrate geometry). Step7: Oxygen partial pressure and gas flow standardization: fix pO2 during growth to 200 mTorr (±10 mTorr) and total flow (e.g., 50–100 sccm) across all chambers to isolate Tsub effects; verify chamber stabilization time and repeatability. Step8: Define experimental design (DoE) for initial Tsub exploration: per chamber and substrate type, choose 6–8 Tsub set points spanning each system’s safe window (e.g., IBAD: 830–870 °C; STO: 780–880 °C) informed by calibration; include replicate runs at two Tsub values to assess process variability; keep all other variables constant (pO2, laser fluence, repetition rate, target–substrate distance, thickness). Step9: Deposition protocol—general: load substrate; evacuate to base pressure (<1×10^-6 Torr), introduce O2 to 200 mTorr; heat substrate to set Tsub; dwell 10–15 min for thermal equilibrium; confirm Tsub with pyrometer; start deposition with target rotation; deposit to thickness 200–250 nm (calibrate pulses-to-thickness via TEM or profilometry on pilot runs; typical growth rate 0.01–0.02 nm/pulse); monitor plume shape/color via in-situ imaging for qualitative consistency; after growth, hold at growth pO2 for 3–5 min. Step10: Oxygenation strategy A (during cooling): ramp O2 to 500 Torr at end of growth; cool at 5 °C min^-1 to 450 °C, dwell 30 min, then cool to room temperature at 5 °C min^-1. Step11: Oxygenation strategy B (post-anneal): after growth and cool-down in 200 mTorr O2, transfer to furnace; anneal in flowing O2 at 400 °C for 60–90 min; cool at 2–5 °C min^-1 to room temperature; compare Strategy A vs B on matched samples to determine which yields higher Tc and Jc while preserving microstructure. Step12: Stress control: for IBAD tapes, limit cooldown rates to ≤5 °C min^-1 between 500–200 °C; ensure buffer stack compatibility; inspect for cracks by optical microscopy; measure residual stress by XRD sin^2ψ or wafer curvature (for STO) on a subset; adjust cooldown if cracking observed. Step13: Structural characterization: perform XRD θ–2θ to confirm c-axis orientation; measure ω-rocking curve FWHM (target ≤0.5–0.8° on STO, ≤1–2° on IBAD) and φ-scan Δϕ (verify transfer of IBAD texture into YBCO; target Δϕ close to substrate); for selected samples, perform cross-sectional TEM to assess interface quality and threading dislocation density; AFM surface roughness (target RMS ≤ 5 nm). Step14: Patterning for transport: define bridges (e.g., 0.2–0.5 mm width, 2–5 mm length) by photolithography and wet etch or laser scribing; deposit Au pads (50–100 nm) for low-resistance contacts; bond wires with indium or ultrasonic wedge bonding. Step15: Electrical measurement—Tc: measure resistive Tc in PPMS (0 T) with 1 mA bias; define Tc onset and zero; aim for Tc ≥ 90 K; if Tc < 88 K, adjust oxygenation protocol. Step16: Electrical measurement—Jc(B,T): four-probe measurements at 77 K and 65 K with B||c; apply voltage criterion 1 µV cm^-1; measure Jc at B = 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1, 2, 3 T (extend to 9 T for model validation subset); record E–J curves to confirm power-law behavior; note flux-flow onset; ensure self-field measurement free of heating (pulsed current if necessary). Step17: Length-uniformity assessment for reel-to-reel samples: for long tapes, cut 10–30 cm segments every 1–2 m for transport tests; complement with non-destructive scanning Hall-probe or magneto-optical imaging to map Ic uniformity; correlate Ic variations with Δϕ and surface defects. Step18: Metadata and data curation: for each sample log chamber ID, substrate type, Δϕ, buffer termination (CeO2 vs STO), Tsub readings (thermocouple and pyrometer), pO2, fluence, repetition rate, thickness, plume imaging descriptors, oxygenation method, structural metrics (ω, Δϕ, roughness), and electrical results (Tc, Jc(B,T)); store in a unified database. Step19: Baseline modeling—single-chamber GPR: build a Gaussian Process Regression for each chamber predicting log10(Jc_77K,0T) as a function of Tsub, substrate type, Δϕ, thickness (held fixed), oxygenation method, and plume-imaging features; use ARD RBF kernel for continuous features and Hamming/one-hot kernel for categorical features; 5-fold cross-validation to assess RMSE and uncertainty calibration. Step20: Transfer learning setup (multi-task GP): implement a linear model of coregionalization where each chamber is a task; learn a per-chamber affine mapping Tsub* = a_ch Tsub + b_ch into a shared latent temperature coordinate; initialize a_ch,b_ch from pyrometer vs controller calibration; jointly fit across all chambers using shared kernel hyperparameters for Tsub*; include categorical variables (chamber design, substrate type) to capture non-numerical factors. Step21: Anchor experiments for Tsub scale alignment: for each chamber, deposit at three “anchor” Tsub values spanning the window on both STO and IBAD; use resulting Jc_77K,0T and structural metrics to refine a_ch,b_ch; iterate until latent Tsub* distributions overlap across chambers within ±10 °C equivalent. Step22: Active learning for Tsub optimization: using the multi-task GP, compute Expected Improvement (EI) on Jc_77K,0T over the latent Tsub*; select 2–3 new Tsub setpoints per chamber that maximize EI while maintaining safe Tsub limits (avoid buffer degradation on IBAD); run, measure, and update the model; repeat 2–3 cycles until Jc target is achieved or EI plateaus. Step23: Physics-aided modeling (PAM) for Jc(B): transform field data to y = 1/Jc^3; for each sample or grouped by substrate/pinning class, fit y(B) = y0 + c B^α over 0.05–3 T at 65 K (reference dataset); validate linearizability and goodness-of-fit (R^2 ≥ 0.81 in Jc-space back-transform); use the fitted parameters with the Jc_77K,0T baseline and measured temperature scaling (from a subset) to predict Jc(B) at 77 K up to 3 T; quantify prediction intervals by propagating GPR and fit uncertainties. Step24: Incorporate microstructural priors: include Δϕ and ω as features influencing the PAM exponent α or select separate PAM fits for (i) STO nearly single-crystal, (ii) IBAD with Δϕ ≤ 2°, and (iii) IBAD with Δϕ > 2°; use TEM/dislocation density (if available) as an optional covariate to classify pinning regime. Step25: Grain-boundary and interface tuning loop: prioritize IBAD substrates with Δϕ ≤ 2°; for these, run high Tsub (target ≥ 860 °C if buffer stack integrity is maintained) to minimize weak-link behavior; verify crossover field (self-field to vortex-dominated) < 0.05 T by low-field Jc(B) at 77 K; ensure CeO2-terminated templates or atomically flat STO are used; if interfacial disorder or secondary phases are detected by TEM/XRD, reduce Tsub by 10–20 °C or adjust dwell before growth. Step26: Oxygen stoichiometry tuning: for top-performing Tsub windows, perform a small matrix varying oxygenation method (Strategy A vs B) and duration to maximize Tc and Jc; maintain identical cation growth parameters; choose the method that yields Tc ≥ 90 K and improved Jc without increasing roughness or inducing cracks. Step27: Stress management validation: for optimized runs, measure residual stress and inspect for microcracks; if tensile stress is significant on IBAD tapes, reduce cooldown rate or slightly reduce Tsub (5–10 °C) while checking that Jc remains within 95% of peak; avoid exceeding 250 nm if cracking appears; confirm mechanical integrity via bend tests on short tape sections. Step28: Scale-up to reel-to-reel: apply the learned Tsub* mapping and optimal setpoint to production PLD; run a short coil (e.g., 10–50 m) with identical pO2/fluence; sample every meter for Jc_77K,0T and Δϕ; use non-destructive scanning to fill gaps; feed results back into the multi-task GP to refine the chamber offset parameters. Step29: Validation of predictive performance: with PAM predictions trained on reference field data, predict Jc(B) at 65 K and 77 K up to 3 T for new samples; compare to measured values and compute R^2 and calibration of prediction intervals; accept the model if median R^2 ≥ 0.81 and 90% of measurements fall within 95% prediction intervals. Step30: Process transfer demonstration: use the integrated GPR-TL-PAM to select Tsub in a different chamber for a target Jc_77K,0T ≥ 3 MA cm^-2 and specified Jc(65 K, 3 T); run 3–5 validation samples; if ≥80% meet targets within predicted uncertainty, proceed to larger production run. Step31: Contingency measures: if Ni diffusion or buffer degradation is detected (secondary phases at interface, increased roughness), lower Tsub by 10–20 °C, increase CeO2 buffer thickness, or reduce dwell time at high T; if Jc self-field is high but drops rapidly at low fields, further reduce Δϕ or increase Tsub within safe limits; if Tc is suboptimal, adjust oxygenation time/temperature; if chamber-to-chamber variance remains high, increase the number of anchor points and incorporate plume-imaging features more explicitly in the GP. Step32: Safety and quality assurance: enforce laser and high-temperature safety protocols; verify oxygen handling and purge procedures; implement run sheets and checklists for each deposition; use control samples (reference STO and IBAD runs) every 10 samples to monitor drift; maintain traceability from substrate lot to final measurements. Step33: Documentation and dissemination: compile process windows (Tsub*, pO2), microstructural metrics, and model parameters for each chamber; provide standard operating procedures for production lines; archive data and models to enable rapid re-initialization when hardware maintenance occurs. Step34: Exit criteria: declare success when (i) ≥3 MA cm^-2 at 77 K, self-field is met on both STO and IBAD (Δϕ ≤ 2°) for ≥80% of optimized runs, (ii) PAM R^2 ≥ 0.81 for Jc(B) up to 3 T at 65 K, and (iii) transfer from R&D to production meets targets with ≤2 validation iterations.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Sample Preparation – YBCO films were deposited using pulsed laser deposition (PLD) with a KrF laser (wavelength 246 nm) under varying substrate temperatures (Tsub) and fixed oxygen pressure, laser frequency, and thickness within each series.

Step 2: Substrate and Chamber Variation – Five sample series were prepared using different PLD chambers (reel-to-reel or R&D type) and substrate types (IBAD A, IBAD B, or single-crystal SrTiO₃), with Tsub measured either by radiation thermometer (RT) or thermocouple (TC).

Step 3: Post-Annealing – All films were post-annealed: series 1–3 and 5 at 400 °C with oxygen gas flow; series 4 during cooling with oxygen introduction.

Step 4: Structural Characterization – Δϕ (full width at half maximum of YBCO(103) or (102) ϕ-scan in X-ray diffraction) was measured to assess in-plane texture; values are listed in Table 1.

Step 5: Electrical Transport Measurement – Four-probe method using Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) to obtain:
- Resistivity-temperature curves for critical temperature (Tc)
- Current-voltage curves for Jc at 65 K and 77 K, 0–9 T (B//c)

Step 6: Database Construction – Measured Jc, Tc, Tsub, Δϕ, thickness, and deposition conditions compiled into a database (Supplementary Tables S1–S2).

Step 7: GPR-TL-PAM Modeling – GPR models trained on source domain (series 1) and transferred to target domains (series 2–5) using location-scale (LS) shift coefficients; PAM functions (1/Jc³, 1/Jc², log Jc, linear Jc) tested to extend Jc predictions across magnetic fields.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Deposition method: PLD with KrF laser (246 nm)
- Oxygen pressure: 200 or 400 mTorr (fixed within each series)
- Laser frequency: 10 or 100 Hz (fixed within each series)
- Film thickness: 200–250 nm (measured or estimated, fixed within each series)
- Tsub ranges: 700–940 °C (varied within each series)
- Tsub measurement: RT (series 1, 2) or TC (series 3, 4, 5); authors note measured Tsub is not necessarily the true temperature and is treated relatively
- Post-anneal: 400 °C with O₂ flow (series 1–3, 5) or O₂ during cooling (series 4)
- Magnetic field orientation: B//c-axis for all Jc–B measurements
- Reference fields for TL: 0 T (77 K), 0.3 T (65 K), 1 T (65 K)

Experiment: Step1: Define sample matrix and study design:
- Prepare a EuBa2Cu3Oy (EuBCO) thin-film series on industrial IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes with coherent BaHfO3 (BHO) inclusions at nominal volume fractions: 0, 1.9, 2.8, and 4.8 vol% BHO. Keep total thickness constant at 400 ± 30 nm across all samples to avoid thickness-dependent Jc variations.
- For reliable microstructural and magnetization analysis free of metallic substrate background, co-deposit identical “witness” films on single-crystal substrates (e.g., (001) LaAlO3 and/or SrTiO3) under identical conditions for each BHO fraction.

Step2: Fabricate PLD targets enabling precise BHO volume fraction:
- Base target: EuBCO ceramic made from Eu2O3, BaCO3, and CuO powders (≥99.99% purity). Ball mill, calcine at 900–930 °C in flowing O2 with intermediate grindings to ensure phase formation; press and sinter at 950–980 °C in O2 to densify.
- BHO addition: Use BaHfO3 nanopowder (20–50 nm primary particle size). Mechanically blend with EuBCO powder to the desired volumetric fraction (convert to weight fraction using densities ρEuBCO ≈ 6.3 g cm−3, ρBHO ≈ 7.7 g cm−3). Press composite targets and sinter at 900–950 °C in O2 to avoid BaHfO3 decomposition. Prepare distinct targets for 1.9, 2.8, and 4.8 vol% BHO.
- Alternative for fine-tuning: Use a segmented composite target (EuBCO and BHO sectors) or dual-target sequential firing to adjust the effective BHO fraction; calibrate via film composition (Step13).

Step3: Prepare IBAD-tape substrates and witness substrates:
- IBAD tapes: Use Hastelloy with standard buffer stack (e.g., amorphous oxide barrier/Y2O3 or Gd2Zr2O7 seed/CeO2/LaMnO3/IBAD-MgO/CeO2 cap). Cut 4 × 4 mm and 10 × 3 mm pieces. Clean with acetone/isopropanol and mild O2 plasma (≤10 W, 1–2 min).
- Single-crystal witnesses: Clean LaAlO3/SrTiO3 substrates (solvent rinse, UV-ozone 10–15 min).

Step4: Calibrate substrate temperature and oxygen partial pressure:
- Use a two-color pyrometer directed at the film surface to calibrate the heater readback to the actual surface temperature. Establish that the setpoint corresponds to a surface temperature in the 760–820 °C range during growth (typical for REBCO PLD).
- Verify oxygen partial pressure gauge accuracy (capacitance manometer). Prepare for growth at 150–300 mTorr O2.

Step5: PLD system setup and plume calibration:
- Laser: KrF excimer (248 nm). Fluence 1.2–1.8 J cm−2 at target, 5–10 Hz repetition rate. Target–substrate distance 45–55 mm; raster the laser to minimize target grooves.
- Pre-ablate targets for 3–5 minutes at growth conditions to reach steady-state plume chemistry.
- Determine deposition rate using a predeposited step edge and stylus profilometry or X-ray reflectivity on a test film; target growth rate ~0.5–1.0 nm s−1.

Step6: Grow EuBCO films (undoped and BHO-doped) on IBAD tapes:
- For undoped EuBCO: Substrate surface temperature set to the calibrated value corresponding to ~780–800 °C; oxygen pressure 200–300 mTorr. Grow to 400 nm. Maintain cube-on-cube epitaxy (c-axis normal to plane).
- For BHO-doped EuBCO: Reduce growth temperature by ~20–40 °C relative to undoped to promote coherent BHO self-assembly and nanorod formation while preserving epitaxy; oxygen pressure same as above. Use respective BHO targets for 1.9, 2.8, 4.8 vol%.
- Growth interruptions: None for baseline; maintain steady plume to favor vertical nanorod alignment. Document heater readback (users’ 1055 °C with BHO vs 1150 °C without) alongside calibrated surface temperatures for traceability.

Step7: Grow identical witness films on single crystals:
- For each BHO fraction, deposit a 200–300 nm film on LaAlO3/SrTiO3 at the same calibrated conditions to facilitate XRD, TEM, and magnetometry without metallic substrate background.

Step8: In-situ cooldown and oxygenation anneal:
- After growth, raise O2 pressure to 300–700 Torr and cool to 500–550 °C at 10–15 °C min−1; hold 0.5–1 h.
- Ex-situ oxygenation: Anneal in flowing O2 at 250–350 °C for 2–6 h to target near-optimal hole doping p ≈ 0.15. Use identical anneal for all samples.

Step9: Verify thickness, Tc, and doping:
- Thickness by stylus profilometry across a masked step or XRR on witnesses; target 400 ± 30 nm on tapes; note any variation for Bean-model geometry corrections.
- Resistivity ρ(T) on witnesses (four-probe), Tc onset and zero-resistance; aim Tc ≈ 90 K. Optionally measure room-temperature thermopower S(290 K) to estimate hole concentration; adjust oxygenation if needed.

Step10: Phase and texture analysis by XRD:
- θ–2θ scan to confirm c-axis oriented EuBCO and absence of secondary phases beyond Eu2O3 (if present in undoped) and BHO. Monitor EuBCO c-axis lattice parameter as a proxy for oxygen content.
- Rocking curves (ω) on EuBCO (005) for out-of-plane texture; φ-scans on (103) for in-plane texture. Confirm FWHM consistent with sharp biaxial texture inherited from IBAD-MgO.
- Scan for BHO (hkl) reflections; their presence and broadening provide qualitative inclusion information.

Step11: Surface morphology by AFM/SEM:
- AFM over 2 × 2 μm to assess surface roughness (RMS ≤ 5 nm typical). SEM plan-view for grain size statistics via image segmentation; compare undoped vs BHO-doped for grain growth trends.

Step12: TEM sample preparation:
- Cross-sections: Focused ion beam (FIB) lift-outs from tapes and witnesses; finish with low-kV milling (2–5 kV) to minimize damage. Prepare lamella along and across tape rolling direction.
- Plan-view: For witnesses, ion-mill from the substrate side or use wedge polishing to electron transparency for grain and dislocation network visualization.

Step13: STEM-HAADF/EDS/EELS microstructure quantification:
- Map BHO inclusions: measure diameter, length, areal density, spacing, and splay angle distribution. For 1.9 vol% expect ~4–5 nm nanoparticles; for ≥2.8 vol% expect nanorods aligned near c-axis with possible splay increasing at 4.8 vol%.
- Quantify Eu2O3 precipitates (~20 nm) in undoped films (number density, size distribution).
- Identify and count c-axis threading dislocations and grain boundary dislocation arrays; weak-beam dark-field imaging for dislocation density.
- Twin boundary density and spacing via plan-view imaging (g = 110 conditions).
- Strain mapping around BHO using geometric phase analysis; correlate local strain with inclusion diameter and spacing.
- Determine actual BHO vol% from 3D number density and dimensions; refine target fraction if needed.

Step14: Texture propagation and interface analysis:
- High-resolution TEM at EuBCO/BHO interfaces to confirm coherency and cube-on-cube epitaxy.
- Evaluate interfaces across buffer stack (CeO2/LMO/MgO) to ensure no reaction layers or dewetting; correlate with Jc performance.

Step15: Prepare specimens for magnetic measurements and background subtraction:
- Cut 2–4 mm squares from each tape sample; record precise dimensions (a × b × t, with t = film thickness).
- Prepare identical-sized bare buffered tape pieces (without EuBCO) for background magnetization measurement; measure and subtract to remove Hastelloy/buffer contributions.
- Mount samples using low-background quartz sample holders and GE varnish; align for H∥c (field perpendicular to film plane) and H∥ab (in-plane).

Step16: Magnetization loops (M–H) for Jc extraction:
- Instrument: Quantum Design MPMS3 SQUID (1.8–400 K, up to ±7 T) or higher-field VSM if available for >7 T.
- Temperatures: 1.8, 5, 20, 30, 60, and 77 K.
- Fields: 0 to ±7 T for both H∥c and H∥ab. Sweep rates ~10–50 Oe s−1 to minimize heating and eddy-current effects.
- Protocol: Zero-field cool to target T; acquire full M–H loop. Repeat for both orientations. Acquire corresponding loops of the bare buffered substrate and subtract.

Step17: Calculate Jc from magnetization (Bean critical-state):
- Use rectangular-slab Bean model corrected for sample dimensions: Jc = 20ΔM/[a(1 − a/3b)] for a ≤ b (cgs units), convert to SI; or thin-film perpendicular-field model for H∥c with thickness correction. Use the film’s volume (film area × thickness) for ΔM normalization.
- For H∥ab, correct for demagnetization and geometry; cross-check with witness films on single crystals for consistency.
- Compare Jc from magnetization with optional four-probe transport Jc on lithographically patterned microbridges (50–100 μm wide, 1 μV cm−1 criterion) on witness films to calibrate the Bean model conversion.

Step18: Determine strong-pinning exponents and scaling:
- Fit Jc(B) at fixed T to a power law Jc ∝ B^−α in the field range where single-vortex strong pinning is expected. Compare α across BHO contents; expect α to decrease with BHO addition, indicating stronger pinning.
- Analyze H∥c and H∥ab anisotropy; extract Jc anisotropy γJ = Jc(H∥ab)/Jc(H∥c). Assess the c-axis nanorod contribution.

Step19: Magnetic relaxation for vortex creep S and glassy μ:
- At each T (20, 30, 40, 60 K) and B (0.5, 1, 2, 3 T; H∥c and H∥ab), perform 1-hour magnetic relaxation.
- Protocol: Field-cool to target T at measurement field; stabilize for 300 s; start recording M(t) from t0 ≈ 10 s to 3600 s. Alternatively, set field to slightly above target, ramp down to target, then log M(t).
- Compute normalized creep rate S = d ln M / d ln t from the slope of ln M vs ln t. Repeat 2–3 times for reproducibility.
- Apply the collective-creep interpolation formula to M(t) data to extract μ and U0: incorporate U(J) = U0[(Jc/J)^μ − 1] and use Maley analysis to construct U vs J; determine μ. Compare μ trends across BHO fractions and orientations.

Step20: Angle-resolved Jc(θ) and S(θ):
- Use a sample rotator (if available) to sweep θ from H∥c (0°) to H∥ab (90°) at fixed B and T (e.g., 1 T at 30 and 60 K). Step size 5° near c-axis to resolve nanorod peaks.
- Extract Jc(θ) and S(θ) to identify correlated pinning peaks and any enhanced creep near H∥c indicating double-kink excitations along nanorods, especially at 4.8 vol% BHO.

Step21: Grain boundary and dislocation contributions:
- Correlate plan-view TEM-dislocation density and grain size with Jc(θ) background and S for undoped vs doped films. Assess whether reduced grain boundary density with BHO coincides with changes in low-field Jc and creep.

Step22: Strain-pinning analysis:
- From GPA strain maps, estimate strain amplitude around BHO and compute an effective additional pinning energy contribution. Correlate strain field metrics with U0 and Jc enhancements at low and intermediate fields.

Step23: Build structure–property relationships:
- Plot Jc(B,T,θ), α, S(T,B,θ), μ, and U0 versus BHO vol%. Identify the optimum regime (expected near 2.8 vol% BHO) balancing high Jc and low S. Note the increase in S at 4.8 vol% particularly for H∥c consistent with double-kink motion along splayed nanorods.

Step24: Robustness and reproducibility checks:
- Prepare at least three replicates per BHO fraction on tapes and witnesses. Report mean and standard deviation for key metrics (Jc at 5 T and 1 T; S at 30 K, 1 T).
- Thermal cycling: 10 cycles between 300 K and 20 K in O2; re-measure Jc and S at 60 K, 1 T to confirm stability.
- Length uniformity on tapes: measure Jc via magnetic or transport methods at multiple positions along 5–10 cm to assess process uniformity; if transport is unavailable, use scanning Hall probe to map local Jc surrogates.

Step25: Address potential pitfalls and process refinement:
- If substrate magnetic background subtraction introduces uncertainty, prioritize witness-film magnetometry and use transport Jc on tapes for absolute benchmarks.
- If BHO nanorods show excessive splay at 4.8 vol% (large angular spread), reduce growth temperature slightly and/or growth rate to encourage vertical alignment, or reduce BHO fraction increments (e.g., 3.2–3.5 vol%) to probe the threshold for splay-induced creep penalty.
- If Eu2O3 precipitates coarsen with certain anneals, adjust oxygenation ramp rates and dwell times to limit secondary phase growth while achieving optimal p.

Step26: Reporting and application mapping:
- Summarize the optimized composition (targeting ~2.8 vol% BHO) that maximizes in-field Jc while minimizing creep in 20–77 K. Provide Jc(5 T, 1.8 K) and Jc(1 T, 60 K), S(30 K, 1 T) for each fraction and orientations.
- Translate results to application scenarios (high-field magnets, fault-current limiters) by estimating engineering current density Je using realistic fill factors and accounting for tape geometry.

Step27: Data management and sharing:
- Archive all raw and processed data (PLD parameters, XRD, TEM/STEM datasets, M–H loops, M(t), analysis scripts). Record exact calibrated substrate temperatures beyond heater readbacks for reproducibility.

Step28: Safety and handling:
- Follow laser safety protocols for PLD; handle Hf-containing powders in a fume hood with appropriate PPE; use cryogen safety procedures for MPMS3 operation.

Step29: Timeline and resources:
- Weeks 1–2: Target fabrication and calibration.
- Weeks 3–5: Film growth on tapes and witnesses (all BHO fractions).
- Weeks 6–8: Oxygenation and basic XRD/AFM characterization.
- Weeks 9–12: TEM/STEM/EDS/EELS; concurrent magnetization and relaxation measurements.
- Weeks 13–14: Data analysis and correlation; process iteration if needed.

Step30: Success criteria:
- Achieve c-axis oriented EuBCO with coherent BHO inclusions whose morphology transitions from nanoparticles (1.9 vol%) to nanorods (≥2.8 vol%) with controlled splay.
- Demonstrate Jc enhancement versus undoped in fields up to at least 5–7 T and temperatures up to 60–77 K, with minimal increase of S at the optimized BHO fraction and a measurable creep penalty only at the highest BHO content.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Film growth  
- EuBCO layers (550–600 nm) deposited by PLD on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes.  
  – BHO-doped films: 1055 °C growth, 250 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.  
  – Undoped EuBCO: 1150 °C growth, 350 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.  
- (Y,Gd)BCO reference films grown by MOD on similar buffered tapes; BHO introduced via Hf-naphthenate precursor; 300 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.

Step 2: Microstructural characterisation  
- Cross-sectional TEM/HAADF and plan-view SEM/TEM to measure inclusion diameter (≈4.5 ± 1 nm in EuBCO; 12–14 nm in (Y,Gd)BCO), morphology (nanoparticles → nanorods with increasing BHO), separation d, grain size, twin-boundary spacing, dislocation density.  
- EDS mapping to confirm chemical identity of precipitates.

Step 3: Magnetisation measurements  
- All films cut into rectangular pieces (lateral size 3–4.5 mm) and mounted on Delrin disks.  
- Quantum Design MPMS3 SQUID magnetometer with field H ‖ c-axis.  
  – Tc determination: zero-field-cooled moment m(T) in 0.2–0.4 mT, sweep rate 0.5–4 K min⁻¹.  
  – Jc(B,T): hysteresis loops m(H) at fixed T (1.8, 20, 40, 60 K); Bean model for rectangular plates Jc = 20Δm /[w²lδ(1−w/3l)]; VSM mode used to reduce creep contribution.  
  – Magnetic relaxation (creep): after establishing critical state (ΔH = 2 T > 4H*), record m(t) every 4–10 s for 1 h at fixed (H₁,T₁); extract creep rate S = −d ln m / d ln t from linear fit to ln m vs ln t.

Step 4: Data analysis  
- Fit log Jc vs log B in the strong-pinning region to obtain exponent α.  
- Fit relaxation curves M(t) to interpolation formula M(t)=M₀[1+(μk_BT/U₀)ln(t/t₀)]^(−1/μ) with t₀ = 10⁻⁶ s to extract μ and U₀; construct μ(T,B) contour maps.  
- Compare experimental μ with theoretical values for single-vortex (1/7), small-bundle (3/2), large-bundle (7/9), half-loop (1), variable-range hopping (1/3) regimes.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Sample set: five EuBCO films (0, 1.9, 2.8, 3.8, 4.8 vol % BHO) and two (Y,Gd)BCO films (0 and 8.9 vol % BHO).  
- Film thickness: 550–600 nm (measured, Supplementary Table 1).  
- Applied magnetic field range: 0–9 T perpendicular to film plane.  
- Temperature range: 1.8–60 K for Jc(B); 1.8–60 K for creep.  
- Self-field regime identified via μ₀H_sf = μ₀γJ_sfδ/π with γ = 5.  
- Oxygen content y deduced from empirical relation 0.21y = 1.283+p (carrier concentration p from Hall data).  
- Doping consistency maintained within each growth method; absolute doping differs between PLD and MOD groups.

Step9: Microstructure and domain identification by (S)TEM: (a) Cross-sectional lamella prep by FIB with low-kV (2–5 kV) final polish; (b) HR-TEM and STEM-HAADF imaging to locate embedded cubic-phase domains and assess size (2–20 nm), density, and coherence with matrix; (c) SAED/NBD to determine orientation relationship between cubic domains and orthorhombic YBCO; (d) STEM-EDS maps (Y, Ba, Cu, O) to confirm Cu enrichment within domains and lack of Ba/Y segregation; (e) EELS (optional) for oxygen/valence mapping to distinguish non-superconducting inclusions; (f) Ensure no high-angle grain boundaries across film thickness. Step14: Magnetization and Birr (VSM): (a) Measure M–H loops at 77 K and 80 K up to 7–9 T for unpatterned films on substrates; (b) Extract Jc via thin-film Bean model (using sample dimensions and thickness); (c) Determine irreversibility line Birr(T) by vanishing ΔM or Kramer extrapolation; (d) Cross-check Birr via resistive criteria in PPMS (e.g., 10% of normal-state resistivity). Step15: Correlate microstructure with pinning: (a) Quantify cubic-domain size/density from TEM; (b) Correlate with Jc(B) scaling and angular behavior; (c) Assess whether domains introduce isotropic pinning (reduced anisotropy ratio Jc(θ = 0°)/Jc(θ = 90°)); (d) Identify optimal growth window that maximizes domain coherence and density while preserving smooth surfaces. Step16: Parameter optimization loop: (a) If Jc at 80 K and 1–2 T is below targets, increase domain density via slight increase in Cu content (e.g., use a composite ablation sequence: alternate pulses from 1:2:3 target and CuO target in 10:1 to 5:1 ratios to fine-tune effective Cu flux); (b) If granular particles appear, reduce laser fluence and increase oxygen pressure to suppress splashing; (c) If Tc is depressed, increase post-anneal oxygenation or lower growth temperature slightly to limit Cu substitutional disorder on Ba sites; (d) Iterate until meeting acceptance criteria. Step17: Acceptance criteria and benchmarks: (a) Structural: c-axis only XRD with ω-FWHM ≤ 0.3°, φ-scan four-fold symmetry, Δc ≤ 0.001 nm on LSAT; (b) Morphology: AFM RMS ≤ 1 nm, no SEM-visible particulates; (c) Superconducting: Tc,zero ≥ 89 K; Jc(80 K, 0 T) ≥ 3 MA cm−2; Jc(80 K, 1–1.5 T) showing ≥1.5× improvement over stoichiometric control; Birr(80 K) increased by ~20% over control; (d) Reproducibility across ≥3 samples. Step18: Strain/stress and thickness study: (a) Compare 20, 40, 80 nm on LSAT/STO/LAO; (b) Use RSM to verify relaxation above critical thickness; (c) Check uniform distribution of cubic domains across thickness by through-thickness STEM; (d) Identify substrate that optimizes both epitaxy and domain formation (expectation: LSAT best interface/texture). Step19: Device-level demonstration (microwave relevance): (a) On LSAT, pattern coplanar waveguide or microstrip resonators (line widths 2–10 μm) using standard photolithography; (b) Measure S-parameters and Q-factor at 77 K (e.g., 5–10 GHz) in a cryogenic probe station; (c) Compare to stoichiometric YBCO devices for Q and power handling; (d) Inspect edges and surfaces post-pattern to ensure smoothness and no redeposition. Step20: Documentation and QA: (a) Maintain a growth log including target age, laser energy, spot size, pulse count, substrate lot, and thermometry calibration; (b) Archive raw data (XRD, TEM, AFM, PPMS, VSM) and analysis scripts; (c) Perform uncertainty analysis on Jc extraction (geometry, thickness, voltage criterion) and RBS stoichiometry; (d) Prepare a process of record for the optimal parameter set enabling reproducible Cu-YBCO films meeting the performance targets. Step21: Safety and handling: (a) Follow laser safety protocols (class IV, interlocks, eyewear); (b) Handle high-pressure O2 with appropriate regulators and purge procedures; (c) HF etching (for STO) in certified wet hood with PPE and calcium gluconate gel on hand; (d) Dispose of Cu-containing waste per institutional guidelines. Step22: Contingencies and troubleshooting: (a) If XRD shows secondary bulk phases (e.g., BaCuO2) at high volume fraction, lower substrate temperature and/or oxygen partial pressure during growth to suppress macroscopic phase separation, then compensate oxygenation post-growth; (b) If c-axis texture degrades on LAO due to twinning, focus device fabrication on LSAT; (c) If domain size exceeds ~20–30 nm (reducing pinning efficacy), decrease Cu flux (switch from 1:2:4 to combined 1:2:3 with brief CuO pulses) and/or increase growth rate to limit coarsening; (d) If Jc anisotropy remains large, refine domain orientation by adjusting growth temperature or using vicinal substrates to promote coherent alignment; (e) If surface roughness >1 nm, reduce fluence, increase target–substrate distance, and employ off-axis PLD geometry. Step23: Final comparative analysis: (a) Compile structure–property maps across substrates and parameters; (b) Quantify gains in Jc and Birr relative to control YBCO; (c) Identify the processing window that yields uniform epitaxial cubic domains, high Jc/Birr at 77–80 K, and device-compatible smooth surfaces; (d) Prepare samples for external validation (e.g., independent TEM and transport) to confirm reproducibility.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Target synthesis  
- A ceramic PLD target with nominal cation ratio Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:4 was prepared by a conventional solid-state reaction (details of powder calcination/sintering not given).

Step 2: Substrate selection and cleaning  
- Three single-crystal substrates were chosen: SrTiO₃ (STO), LaAlO₃ (LAO), and [LaAlO₃]₀.₃[Sr₂TaAlO₆]₀.₇ (LSAT).  
- Surface preparation procedure not specified in the paper.

Step 3: Pulsed-laser deposition of Cu-rich YBCO films  
- A 248 nm KrF excimer laser PLD system was used.  
- Laser power density: 1 J cm⁻²; target–substrate distance: 5.5 cm.  
- Two growth temperatures were explored: 780 °C and 750 °C.  
- Oxygen partial pressure during ablation: 100 mTorr.  
- Typical film thickness investigated: 40 nm (strain study) and 120 nm (microscopy study).  
- Deposition rate: ≈1.6 nm min⁻¹ (not explicitly stated whether this value applies to both temperatures).  
- After deposition the chamber was filled with 700 Torr O₂; samples were cooled at 5 °C min⁻¹ with an intermediate 1 h anneal at 400 °C.

Step 4: Reference sample growth  
- A stoichiometric YBCO target (Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3) was used to deposit a reference film on LSAT under identical PLD parameters (780 °C, 100 mTorr O₂, etc.).

Step 5: Structural characterisation  
- X-ray diffraction (Bruker D8 Explorer) θ–2θ scans and φ-scans on (106)/(016) reflections to verify c-axis orientation and epitaxy.  
- Cross-sectional high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (Thermo Fisher Talos F200XG2) with fast-Fourier-transform analysis to image embedded cubic domains; energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy inside TEM to obtain local Y:Ba:Cu ratios.  
- Surface morphology and compositional surface spots checked by scanning electron microscopy (NOVA NANO SEM 450) coupled with EDS.

Step 6: Electrical transport measurements  
- Temperature-dependent resistivity R(T) recorded for 40 nm films; experimental details (current, contact geometry, criterion) not specified.

Step 7: Magnetisation measurements and J_C extraction  
- Quantum Design PPMS equipped with a vibrating-sample magnetometer (VSM) module.  
- Sample size for magnetic measurements: 5 mm × 2.5 mm.  
- Zero-field-cooled M(T) taken under 20 mT out-of-plane field.  
- M–H hysteresis loops recorded at several temperatures.  
- Critical current density calculated with the extended Bean model for a rectangular plate:  
  J_C = 20 ΔM / [w (1 – w/3l)] where l = 5 mm, w = 2.5 mm, ΔM is the magnetisation width.  
- Irreversibility field B_irr determined by linear extrapolation of Kramer plot J_C^½ B^¼ versus B at each temperature (data below 35 K excluded because of large uncertainty).

Step 8: Data analysis  
- Power-law fits of B_irr(T) ∝ (1 – T/T_C)^n and J_C(T) ∝ (1 – T/T_C)^s performed to compare Cu-YBCO and reference YBCO.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Cu-excess level: 33 % (Cu/Y = 4 vs 3).  
- Substrate choice for J_C/B_irr comparison: LSAT (microwave-device oriented).  
- Thickness for electrical/magnetic comparisons: 40 nm.  
- Thickness for TEM inspection: 120 nm.  
- All comparative superconducting property data shown in the paper refer to films grown at 780 °C; 750 °C data are only used to illustrate temperature sensitivity.
